Teaser: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Appearing today: James Catchpole…
Description: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Appearing today: James Catchpole.

Title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
Teaser: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Appearing today: Bashabi Fraser…
Description: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Appearing today: Bashabi Fraser.

Title: Alayo Akinkugbe & Zarina Muhammad: Rewriting Art History
Teaser: Can we trust art history as it’s conventionally told? And who writes its story from now?…
Description: Can we trust art history as it’s conventionally told? And who writes its story from now? With her ‘A Black History of Art’ Instagram, A Shared Gaze podcast, and book, Reframing Blackness, Alayo Akinkugbe chats about rewriting art history from an often-omitted Black perspective. And Zarina Muhammad from The White Pube unpacks her book Poor Artists (co-authored with Gabrielle de la Puente) and its wild ride through the contemporary art world via imaginative storytelling and anonymised interviews with big-name artists. Hear both of them in conversation today with Tomiwa Folorunso.

Title: Kerri Andrews & Roger Clough: Walking for Life
Teaser: Writers Roger Clough and Kerri Andrews are both walkers and both at a crossroad. Clough's Oldenland interrogates how we learn to be old, while Andrews' Pathfinding brings mothers in the outdoors to the fore…
Description: Who do you picture when you imagine hikers? Perhaps not those nearing the final chapters of life, or those in the maelstrom of motherhood. Yet writers Roger Clough and Kerri Andrews are both walkers and both at a crossroad. Clough's Oldenland interrogates how we learn to be old, while Andrews' Pathfinding brings mothers in the outdoors to the fore. A fascinating discussion awaits: of how walking and writing can inform a way forward for life. Chaired by Jamie Jauncey.

Title: Jen Calleja & Annelise Finegan: Life in Translation
Teaser: Calling all language lovers and word nerds for this conversation on the art of translation and life as a literary translator…
Description: Calling all language lovers and word nerds for this conversation on the art of translation and life as a literary translator. International Booker nominated translators Jen Calleja (German-English) and Annelise Finegan (Chinese-English) will discuss the nuances of their craft, the realities of publishing, and individual works such as Finegan’s translation of Can Xue’s Love in the New Millennium and Calleja’s inventive new translation memoir Fair. Chaired by Camilla Grudova.

Title: First Person Singular: A Workshop with Xiaolu Guo
Teaser: Join writer Xiaolu Guo (Call Me Ishmaelle, My Battle of Hastings) in this workshop exploring how to work with first-person narrative to bring a distinctive voice onto the page…
Description: Join writer Xiaolu Guo (Call Me Ishmaelle, My Battle of Hastings) in this workshop exploring how to work with first-person narrative to bring a distinctive voice onto the page. Together you’ll explore different perspectives on how to construct fiction and non-fiction pieces through the first-person, and explore the borders between fact and fiction, history and everyday events. You’ll also dive into masterworks by Franz Kafka, Virginia Woolf, Annie Ernaux, asking: how can they inspire us?

Title: Children’s Perspective: A Workshop with Catherine Chidgey
Teaser: In this workshop, Catherine Chidgey will guide you through a series of exercises to help you to practise writing your own child narrators as three-dimensional figures who ring true without ever sounding twee…
Description: Many of Catherine Chidgey’s novels feature child narrators, from The Wish Child and Pet to The Book of Guilt (and, arguably, Tama Magpie in The Axeman’s Carnival). In this workshop, Chidgey will discuss how she created these characters and their voices, guiding you through a series of exercises to help you to practise writing your own child narrators as three-dimensional figures who ring true without ever sounding twee.

Title: Claire Mitchell and Zoe Venditozzi: Women, Not Witches
Teaser: Campaign group Witches of Scotland are on a mission to illuminate the unjust killings of nearly 4,000 Scottish women in the 1500s. They want an official pardon, an apology, and appropriate memorialisation of those who were killed…
Description: Campaign group Witches of Scotland are on a mission to illuminate the unjust killings of nearly 4,000 Scottish women in the 1500s. They want an official pardon, an apology, and appropriate memorialisation of those who were killed. Human rights lawyer Claire Mitchell and novelist Zoe Venditozzi are here to expose this dark side of Scottish history with their illuminating book, How to Kill A Witch: A Guide for the Patriarchy. Chaired by Leonie Bell.

Title: Helen Gordon and Kelly Weinersmith: Finding Home
Teaser: This captivating event juxtaposes the intimately human with the wonders of outer space…
Description: This captivating event juxtaposes the intimately human with the wonders of outer space. Zach and Kelly Weinersmith's A City on Mars investigates whether colonising new planets will create a nightmare, both for settlers and those left behind. While Helen Gordon's The Meteorites traces the stories of fallen space objects and the human lives they've touched. They join us to reflect on mankind's relationship with the universe and the precious fragility of life on Earth. Chaired by Dan Richards.

Title: Battle of the Blitzers with Alastair Chisholm
Teaser: Are you ready for a gamer battle like no other? Join bestselling author, Alastair Chisholm as he shares his newest sci-fi mystery, where everyone is desperate to have a Blitzer, the new fighting-game craze…
Description: Are you ready for a gamer battle like no other? Join bestselling author, Alastair Chisholm as he shares his newest sci-fi mystery, where everyone is desperate to have a Blitzer, the new fighting-game craze. But not everything as it seems, and the people behind the invention are hiding a deadly secret. Uncover the truth before it's too late in this interactive and mind-blowing event!

Title: Alistair Moffat: Scotland in a Lifetime
Teaser: Prolific social historian and Edinburgh favourite, Alistair Moffat returns to discuss To See Ourselves: A Personal History of Scotland Since 1950. Through this latest work, Moffat chronicles the radical changes seen in every aspect of Scottish life over…
Description: Prolific social historian and Edinburgh favourite, Alistair Moffat returns to discuss To See Ourselves: A Personal History of Scotland Since 1950. Through this latest work, Moffat chronicles the radical changes seen in every aspect of Scottish life over the last 75 years: from politics and society to the arts and environment. In this fascinating conversation, Moffat shares recollections of events and eyewitness accounts. Expect poignant reminiscence and insightful opinions.

Title: Reverend Richard Coles: Murder in the Parish
Teaser: Join us to find out what makes a former man of the cloth want to write about murder, and whether Canon Clement can solve this latest crime…
Description: Reverend Richard Coles has lived many lives: pop star, priest, public figure, and now bestselling author of the Canon Clement Mysteries. In A Death on Location, the arrival of a glamorous movie set causes a stir around town, not least when a murder takes place during filming. Join Coles to find out what makes a former man of the cloth want to write about murder, and whether Canon Clement can solve this latest crime. Chaired by Dan Richards.

Title: David Keenan: Adventures in the Underground
Teaser: Following the success of the Fringe Firstwinning show, This is Memorial Device, at our 2022 Book Festival, Gordon Burn Prize-winner David Keenan is back with new book, Volcanic Tongue…
Description: Following the success of the Fringe First-winning show, This is Memorial Device, at our 2022 Book Festival, Gordon Burn Prize-winner David Keenan is back with new book, Volcanic Tongue. As a musician and former member of Telstar Ponies, Keenan has always interwoven music through his books. This collection brings together his influential writing about revolutionary late 20th century music makers. Keenan joins us tonight for a spirited, sharp conversation about Volcanic Tongue and the music that influences him. Chaired by Wendy Erskine.

Title: Shani Akilah & Jeda Pearl: Celebrating Andrea Levy
Teaser: Join writers Shani Akilah and Jeda Pearl as they celebrate the enduring legacy of Andrea Levy…
Description: Join writers Shani Akilah and Jeda Pearl as they celebrate the enduring legacy of Andrea Levy. Through her powerful novels – most famously the multi-award-winning Small Island – Levy illuminated the experiences of the Windrush generation and explored themes of identity, belonging, and historical injustice. This event, held in partnership with the Andrea Levy Scholarship, honours Levy’s vital contribution to British literature and her continued influence and impact on a new generation of writers. Chaired by Lisa Williams .

Title: Mona Arshi, Rosa Beltrán & Sunny Singh: Giving Voice
Teaser: Join us today for a powerful conversation delving into three urgent and gripping new books: Mona Arshi's Mouth, Rosa Beltrán's Free Radicals, and Sunny Singh's Refuge: Stories of War (and Love)…
Description: Join us today for a powerful conversation delving into three urgent and gripping new books: Mona Arshi's Mouth, Rosa Beltrán's Free Radicals, and Sunny Singh's Refuge: Stories of War (and Love). In distinct ways, each of the authors turns a lens on often overlooked and marginalised women. With insights from Arshi, Beltrán and Singh, this event will explore the intersections of fiction, poetry, feminism, and survival.

Title: Singing and Stories with Mr Men and Little Miss
Teaser: Join storyteller George in a gentle Mr Men and Little Miss story journey. Perfect for young children, you’ll find lots of live music, nursery rhymes, sensory participation, action, and movement – and classic characters from the much-loved Mr Men and……
Description: Join storyteller George in a gentle Mr Men and Little Miss story journey. Perfect for young children, you’ll find lots of live music, nursery rhymes, sensory participation, action, and movement – and classic characters from the much-loved Mr Men and Little Miss universe. Get ready to dance, play, and join in with the fun.

Title: Anshel Pfeffer: Behind the Curtain of Israeli Politics
Teaser: As Israel correspondent for the Economist and formerly of Ha’aretz, few writers are better placed than Pfeffer to offer a critical understanding of the political psyche of Israel and the on-the-ground situation for Israelis and Palestinians at this…
Description: Anshel Pfeffer has covered Israeli politics for more than two decades, including producing the rigorously reported biography Bibi: The Turbulent Life and Times of Benjamin Netanyahu. As Israel correspondent for the Economist and formerly of Ha’aretz, few writers are better placed than Pfeffer to offer a critical understanding of the political psyche of Israel and the on-the-ground situation for Israelis and Palestinians at this calamitous moment. Hear him in conversation with Guardian and BBC journalist Jonathan Freedland.

Title: Lindsey Hilsum: Poetry as an Act of Witness
Teaser: Lindsey Hilsum has been a war correspondent for four decades. She’s been a poetry lover for even longer…
Description: Lindsey Hilsum has been a war correspondent for four decades. She’s been a poetry lover for even longer. While in Ukraine, she began tweeting a poem a day, a practice which led to her compiling a collection of beloved poems alongside memories of her own work. In this moving event, Hilsum talks with us about I Brought the War with Me and why we turn to poetry in dark times. Chaired by Festival director Jenny Niven.

Title: Lucy Inglis: Where We Began
Teaser: Whatever our journey since, we were all born into this world. But have we ever considered the ancient nature of birth, and how it connects us? In Born: A History of Childbirth, cultural historian Lucy Inglis charts the battle for control over…
Description: Whatever our journey since, we were all born into this world. But have we ever considered the ancient nature of birth, and how it connects us? In Born: A History of Childbirth, cultural historian Lucy Inglis charts the battle for control over reproduction, birth, and women's bodies, exploring the myriad experiences of birth across time. Expect a fascinating discussion, chaired by Devi Sridhar, on the medical, scientific, political, and social changes that have influenced childbirth - and will impact all those who come next.

Title: Changing Worlds with Robert Macfarlane and Emily Sutton
Teaser: Take a lyrical journey through ever-changing landscape and discover The World to Come with nature writer Robert Macfarlane and acclaimed illustrator, Emily Sutton…
Description: Take a lyrical journey through ever-changing landscape and discover The World to Come with nature writer Robert Macfarlane and acclaimed illustrator, Emily Sutton. Learn how to bring nature drawings to life as Emily guides you through her astonishing artwork while Robert shares how the magic of nature can give us hope for the future and how we can all celebrate and protect the natural world.

Title: Malachy Tallack: That Beautiful Atlantic Waltz
Teaser: Malachy Tallack’s novel, That Beautiful Atlantic Waltz, is uniquely accompanied by an album of evocative songs. Join us tonight as those songs will be captivatingly performed by a full band (including Tallack)…
Description: Malachy Tallack’s novel, That Beautiful Atlantic Waltz, tells the story of Jack, a Shetlander growing steadily old inside the cottage where he’s always lived, listening to music and reflecting on the past until the rhythm of his life is profoundly disrupted. The book is uniquely accompanied by an album of evocative songs, ‘written’ by Jack. Tonight, those songs will be captivatingly performed by a full band (including Tallack). There’ll also be the first ever performance of two brand new songs, commissioned as a coda to the album by the Book Festival. The evening will be chaired by Louise Welsh.

Title: John Kay: Everything You Know About Business is Wrong
Teaser: The sometime academic, journalist, and governmental advisor joins us with The Corporation in the Twenty-First Century (a Financial Times and New Statesman book of 2024), discussing why our ideas about business need an update…
Description: Over leading economist John Kay’s decades-long career, the role of corporations in the economy has changed, even as public opinion of them has dwindled. Now, in the age of tech monopolies, pharma bros, and the destructive pursuit of shareholder value, the sometime academic, journalist, and governmental advisor joins us with The Corporation in the Twenty-First Century (a Financial Times and New Statesman book of 2024), discussing why our ideas about business need an update. Chaired by Mure Dickie.

Title: Thought Exercise: Josh Cohen
Teaser: Today’s guest is acclaimed author and psychoanalyst Josh Cohen who – in All the Rage – examines how anger has come to define so much of our social and political lives…
Description: Dig deeper with our Thought Exercise series. Hear from experts on urgent issues of our time, then join in on the discussion during a wide-ranging, interactive exchange. Today’s guest is acclaimed author and psychoanalyst Josh Cohen who – in All the Rage – examines how anger has come to define so much of our social and political lives. Together, discuss how anger shapes our world, what we should do with it, and whether it can ever be put to good use. Chaired by Ben Alderson-Day.

Title: Krystal Evans: From the Ashes
Teaser: Evans' memoir shares how she went from the ashes of disaster to centre stage in a true story that's dark, heartbreaking, inspiring, and hilarious (often all at once)…
Description: Escaping the house fire which tragically killed your sister and left you with PTSD at the age of 14 might not seem an obvious basis for a stand-up show, but Krystal Evans managed exactly that with her award-nominated hour, and now debut book, The Hottest Girl at Burn Camp. Evans' memoir shares how she went from the ashes of disaster to centre stage in a true story that's dark, heartbreaking, inspiring, and hilarious (often all at once). Chaired by Josie Long.

Title: Little Pufflings with Frances Stickley and Jo Weaver
Teaser: Little Puffling’s going on an adventure! Grab your pencils as wonderful illustrator Jo Weaver takes you through a special draw-along where you’ll learn how to draw puffins and other Scottish seabirds…
Description: Little Puffling’s going on an adventure! Grab your pencils as wonderful illustrator Jo Weaver takes you through a special draw-along where you’ll learn how to draw puffins and other Scottish seabirds. Bestselling children’s author Frances Stickley will join remotely and together they’ll introduce you to the adorable star of their new book, Fly High, Little Puffling.

Title: Join the Paper Chase with Julia Donaldson and Friends
Teaser: Get ready for the premiere of Julia’s new picture book, Paper Chase, and family favourites such as Zog, Superworm, and The Gruffalo. Prepare your singing voices and get out your dancing shoes - it's going to be a hit!…
Description: Join the incredible Julia Donaldson and friends for a show filled with stories, poems, and songs. Get ready for the premiere of Julia’s new picture book, Paper Chase, and family favourites such as Zog, Superworm, and The Gruffalo. Prepare your singing voices and get out your dancing shoes - it's going to be a hit!

Title: Words from the Wards: The Exhibition
Teaser: Following the success of the Words from the Wards project, we worked with Edinburgh College of Art students to illustrate the collected stories. Join us to view the stories and illustrations side by side in our new festival gallery…
Description: Last year, through our Words from the Wards project, we asked the people of Edinburgh to share stories about the former Royal Infirmary, to honour the experiences and memories that people connect with the building’s previous life. Following the success of the project, we worked with Edinburgh College of Art students to illustrate the collected stories. Join us to view the stories and illustrations side by side in our new festival gallery.

Title: YA Book Prize 2025: Meet the Shortlisted Writers
Teaser: Meet the incredible authors shortlisted for 2025’s YA Book Prize…
Description:
Meet the incredible authors shortlisted for 2025’s YA Book Prize. The award is organised by The Bookseller, and previous winners include Lex Croucher for Gwen and Art Are Not in Love, Danielle Jawando for When Our Worlds Collided, and Alice Oseman for Loveless. As always, this year's winners will be decided by a panel of experts and teenage judges. Come along to hear from some of the best voices in YA today, including Moira Buffini, Bea Fitzgerald, Danielle Jawando, and Margaret McDonald. (Note: this event takes place twice, with different shortlisted authors appearing each time.)

	This is a Schools event that is available for livestream only.

Title: Chris Brookmyre: Thirty, and Counting
Teaser: Chris Brookmyre’s offbeat brand of Scottish crime has been selling by the millions since his debut in 1996. He joins us now with his 30th novel, The Cracked Mirror, a deeply unusual detective caper that splices the tweedy with the hardboiled…
Description: Chris Brookmyre’s offbeat brand of Scottish crime has been selling by the millions since his debut in 1996. He joins us now with his 30th novel, The Cracked Mirror, a deeply unusual detective caper that splices the tweedy with the hardboiled. With Denise Mina, Brookmyre will discuss his unquenchable desire to push the limits of genre, and look back over his life in writing – and perhaps even his occasional football punditry and noir-ish cover band! You can also expect a special sneak peek of his next Jack Parlabane novel.

Title: Rowan Jaines, Louise Kenward & Alice Tarbuck: Redefining Nature Writing
Teaser: Moving Mountains is a new and compelling anthology of nature writing, from the perspective of disabled and chronically ill authors. Through 25 pieces, deftly edited by Louise Kenward, this is not a chronicle of overcoming and conquering, but rather of…
Description:
Moving Mountains is a new and compelling anthology of nature writing, from the perspective of disabled and chronically ill authors. Through 25 pieces, deftly edited by Louise Kenward, this is not a chronicle of overcoming and conquering, but rather of living with and connecting. Join Kenward and contributors, Rowan Jaines and Alice Tarbuck, for a mind-­opening conversation on how bringing diverse experiences to the fore will change the world of nature writing for good. Chaired by Roxani Krystalli.

	A recording of this event will be made available on demand after the Festival.

Title: Elaine Castillo, Chris McQueer & Catherine Prasifka: Virtually Reality
Teaser: An exploration of humanity at its most uncharted frontier. Today, we talk to Chris McQueer, Catherine Prasifka, and Elaine Castillo, who have each written compelling novels set in the parallel country of the internet…
Description: An exploration of humanity at its most uncharted frontier. Today, we talk to Chris McQueer (Hermit), Catherine Prasifka (This Is How You Remember It), and Elaine Castillo (Moderation), who have each written compelling novels set in the parallel country of the internet, many of whose inhabitants (including young men, children, anonymous moderators) are profoundly affected by its very different laws and norms. Hear the three authors in conversation with Rachelle Atalla.

Title: Melissa Lucashenko: Torching the Myths of Colonialism
Teaser: Meanjin, the traditional place name of modern-day Brisbane, was briefly known as Edenglassie, a portmanteau of Edinburgh and Glasgow. Melissa Lucashenko’s novel of the same name oscillates between 1800s Edenglassie and modern-day Brisbane, examining the…
Description: Meanjin, the traditional place name of modern-day Brisbane, was briefly known as Edenglassie, a portmanteau of Edinburgh and Glasgow. Melissa Lucashenko’s novel of the same name oscillates between 1800s Edenglassie and modern-day Brisbane, examining the lives of Indigenous people then and now. This is a rare opportunity to hear from one of Australia’s great contemporary authors. Hear Lucashenko unpacking this defiant, epic novel of past and present. Chaired by Yassmin Abdel-Magied.

Title: A Bedtime Adventure with Catherine Rayner
Teaser: Molly the hare, Dexter the fox, and Olive the owl love to play games and go on adventures together. But when night falls, strange shapes and sounds start to appear in their beloved oak tree. Can they conquer their fear of the dark? Come along to hear…
Description: Molly the hare, Dexter the fox, and Olive the owl love to play games and go on adventures together. But when night falls, strange shapes and sounds start to appear in their beloved oak tree. Can they conquer their fear of the dark? Come along to hear beloved author-illustrator Catherine Rayner share the new stories of Molly, Olive, and Dexter, and learn how to draw these beautiful characters in Catherine’s playful style.

Title: Susan Barker & Daisy Johnson: What We Fear, Who We Are
Teaser: Horror authors Susan Barker (Old Soul) and Daisy Johnson (The Hotel), join us to discuss how they go about writing thrilling reads that make readers keep coming back for more…
Description: Reading gothic horror can be heart-racing, hair-raising, and borderline hyperventilation-inducing. But how do you write a novel that grips the reader from start to finish? Lauded creators of beguiling page turners, horror authors Susan Barker (Old Soul) and Daisy Johnson (The Hotel), join Jane Flett to discuss how they go about writing thrilling reads that make readers keep coming back for more.

Title: Carrie Marshall & Gary West: God Save the Scene
Teaser: In this energising conversation, we bring together the authors of two fascinating books on Scotland's radical music past…
Description: In this energising conversation, we bring together the authors of two fascinating books on Scotland's radical music past. Scotsman Book of the Year­ winner Carrie Marshall shares Small Town Joy, unpacking how LGBTQ+ artists changed Scotland's soundtrack and celebrating the music that opened minds. Meanwhile, ethnologist and piper Gary West discusses Brave New Music, about the late Martyn Bennett whose blend of tradition and technology created an audacious new sound that was uniquely his own. Chaired by Alistair Braidwood.

Title: Pratyusha, Alycia Pirmohamed, Jessica J Lee & Nina Mingya Powles: Beautiful Experiments
Teaser: Described as a prose poem, a nature diary, and a poetic inquiry, this too is a glistening is the creation of four brilliant poets and writers…
Description: Described as a prose poem, a nature diary, and a poetic inquiry, this too is a glistening is the creation of four brilliant poets and writers. Pratyusha, Alycia Pirmohamed, Jessica J. Lee, and Nina Mingya Powles – otherwise known as ‘fieldnotes collective’ – wrote their pamphlet over the course of one weekend, and what they created is a tender reflection on nature, poetry, and collaboration. Today, the contributors discuss their genre-defying experiment with chair Shasta Hanif Ali.

Title: Kintsugi as Repair: A Workshop with Halle O’Neal
Teaser: In Japanese culture, there's a philosophy that imperfections should be embraced, and this is embodied in the centuries-old art of kintsugi, in which gold lacquer is used to repair ceramics. Rather than hiding the cracks, this visible act of mending…
Description: In Japanese culture, there's a philosophy that imperfections should be embraced, and this is embodied in the centuries-old art of kintsugi, in which gold lacquer is used to repair ceramics. Rather than hiding the cracks, this visible act of mending illuminates them, creating something beautiful out of what was once broken. Capturing imaginations across the world, this is your chance to absorb the history of kintsugi and its modern evolution with artist and academic Halle O'Neal as you enact the practice yourself. Kintsugi kits provided.

Title: One Button Benny with Alan Windram
Teaser: Join Alan Windram, author of the beloved Keven the Orange book series, as he introduces One Button Benny in this all-singing, all-dancing event – there might even be a special song you can learn…
Description: It’s party time in Robot Town! But what happens when One Button Benny accidentally wakes up a large angry dinosaur while practising his cool robotic dance moves? Join Alan Windram, author of the beloved Keven the Orange book series, as he introduces One Button Benny in this all-singing, all-dancing event – there might even be a special song you can learn.

Title: That's Not My Zoo with Vanessa Woolf
Teaser: Join Dog, T-Rex, Mermaid, Penguin, and lots of That’s Not My… friends for this sensory storytelling adventure for little ones. Led by Usborne’s incredible professional storyteller, Vanessa Woolf, with great songs, bubbles, and more – it will be SO MUCH…
Description: Join Dog, T-Rex, Mermaid, Penguin, and lots of That’s Not My… friends for this sensory storytelling adventure for little ones. Led by Usborne’s incredible professional storyteller, Vanessa Woolf, with great songs, bubbles, and more – it will be SO MUCH fun!

Title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
Teaser: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Check back soon to find out today's special guest…
Description: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Check back soon to find out today's special guest.

Title: Adam Buxton: I Love You, Byeee
Teaser: The ramblechats on Adam Buxton's smash-hit podcast are never predictable, but always charming and enlightening, and the same applies to the tales in his idiosyncratic new memoir, I Love You, Byeee…
Description: The ramblechats on Adam Buxton's smash-hit podcast are never predictable, but always charming and enlightening, and the same applies to the tales in his idiosyncratic new memoir, I Love You, Byeee. Grab your conversation coat, look out your talking hat, and join Buxton on a skip down memory lane as he shares equal parts hilarious and moving stories of comedy, adulthood, grief, and parenting (and, of course, Rosie the dog). The path might not be direct, but the ramble will be delightful. Chaired by Zoë Coombs Marr.

Title: Juano Diaz & Dominic Hoey: For the Dreamers and the Underdogs
Teaser: This event brings two authors of heartfelt, electric works about coming of age when you have so much stacked against you…
Description: This event brings two authors of heartfelt, electric works about coming of age when you have so much stacked against you. Slum Boy details author Juano Diaz’s life from a difficult childhood in Glasgow to discovering his sexuality and forging a successful creative path, while New Zealander Dominic Hoey’s third novel, 1985, illuminates poverty, crime, and dysfunctional family in Auckland with the author’s characteristic humour and style. Chaired by Andrés N Ordorica.

Title: Writing Social and Political Satire: A Workshop with Nussaibah Younis
Teaser: A well-crafted work of satire can interrogate complex political or social issues, be accessible to non-specialist audiences, and also be tremendously fun (to read and write!). Bring your novel ideas to this workshop with Dr Nussaibah Younis (author of 202…
Description: A well-crafted work of satire can interrogate complex political or social issues, be accessible to non-specialist audiences, and also be tremendously fun (to read and write!). Bring your novel ideas to this workshop with Dr Nussaibah Younis (author of 2025 Women’s Prize for Fiction-shortlisted Fundamentally) and explore the possibilities for improving their satirical power. Creator of a form that carefully balances humorous, character-driven plot with real world political insights, Younis will use her insights to offer practical creative advice.

Title: Shared Reading with Open Book
Teaser: Join Open Book Lead Readers for an informal and relaxed shared reading session. Each session will explore a chapter from a debut book from this year's Festival programme. No experience necessary, all reading materials will be provided on the day…
Description: Join Open Book Lead Readers for an informal and relaxed shared reading session. Each session will explore a chapter from a debut book from this year's Festival programme. No experience necessary, all reading materials will be provided on the day.

Title: Boro Inspired Slow Stitching Workshop
Teaser: Learn about the ancient Japanese craft of Boro and try it for yourself with textile artist and teacher, Sue Crawley. In this workshop, you’ll have the opportunity to patch clothes and household textiles, repairing the damages to create something new…
Description: Learn about the ancient Japanese craft of Boro and try it for yourself with textile artist and teacher, Sue Crawley. In this workshop, you’ll have the opportunity to patch clothes and household textiles, repairing the damages to create something new and beautiful, before finding out how you can use your finished piece. All materials provided.

Title: Nicholas P Money & Siôn Parkinson: The Possibilities of Mushrooms
Teaser: Mushrooms can be misunderstood, even feared, so when Margaret Atwood said at last year's Festival, 'mushrooms are going to be big in the future', we knew we needed to go deeper. They're used as food, building material, positive environmental disrupters……
Description: Mushrooms can be misunderstood, even feared, so when Margaret Atwood said at last year's Festival, 'mushrooms are going to be big in the future', we knew we needed to go deeper. They're used as food, building material, positive environmental disrupters, and have therapeutic use too; their spores may even affect local weather patterns and promote rainfall. Today, visual artist, composer, and author Siôn Parkinson (Stinkhorn) talks with mycologist Nicholas P Money (Molds, Mushrooms and Medicines) about the hidden role of fungi inside and all around us. Chaired by Hannah Rudman.

Title: The Art of Asking: A Workshop with Hattie Crisell
Teaser: Hone your interview skills with In Writing podcast host and author Hattie Crisell as she shares what she’s learnt from six years of interviewing writers, and many more besides, in journalism…
Description: Hone your interview skills with In Writing podcast host and author Hattie Crisell as she shares what she’s learnt from six years of interviewing writers, and many more besides, in journalism. Whether you’re researching a novel or hosting a live event, find out how to build an unmissable conversation, when to ask difficult questions, how to sensitively navigate someone else’s story, and where the line lies between controlling an interview and allowing surprises to unfold.

Title: Men with Pens
Teaser: Over the spring, award-winning poet, author and playwright Ross MacKay led a series of creative writing workshops for men living with mental health conditions. Working with groups at the AK Bell Library (Perth) and Granton Library (Edinburgh) the men……
Description: Over the spring, award-winning poet, author and playwright Ross MacKay led a series of creative writing workshops for men living with mental health conditions. Working with groups at the AK Bell Library (Perth) and Granton Library (Edinburgh) the men were paired anonymously and exchanged letters over four months. This celebratory event brings together the participants for the first time to meet each other and share the writing that developed over the project.

Title: Wendy Erskine & John Niven: Darkly Humorous Fiction
Teaser: Expect dark humour and keen insights into parenthood in this conversation with John Niven and Wendy Erskine…
Description: Expect dark humour and keen insights into parenthood in this conversation with John Niven and Wendy Erskine. Erskine's The Benefactors examines the lengths privileged parents will go to protect their children. Meanwhile, in Niven's The Fathers, two very different men meet for the first time in a maternity ward. Caoilinn Hughes talks with both about their unflinching portrayals of modern life, blended with a healthy dose of wit and empathy.

Title: Have You Seen a Jellyfish? with Justin Davies
Teaser: Voyage with award-winning author Justin Davies through the pages of his new book Firebloom, and discover how Tally Smuck seeks out the missing jellyfish…
Description: It’s time for Stormcliff’s annual jellyfish festival but there’s a problem… the jellies haven’t arrived. Voyage with award-winning author Justin Davies through the pages of his new book Firebloom, and discover how Tally Smuck seeks out the missing jellyfish. On the way, learn some jelly-tastic jellyfish facts and try your hand at telling fortunes the Stormcliff way. What future will you see in the shells?

Title: Harriet Baker & Philip Hoare: Creative Roots
Teaser: Sunday Times Charlotte Aitken Young Writer of the Year, Harriet Baker, and Baillie Gifford Prize-winning Philip Hoare are paired for an extraordinary discussion delving intimately into creative influences…
Description: Sunday Times Charlotte Aitken Young Writer of the Year, Harriet Baker, and Baillie Gifford Prize-winning Philip Hoare are paired for an extraordinary discussion delving intimately into creative influences. In Rural Hours, Baker focuses on Virginia Woolf, Sylvia Townsend Warner, and Rosamond Lehmann. Hoare’s William Blake and the Sea Monsters of Love meanwhile connects a long line of modern creatives to the Romantic visionary. Together, they’ll explore the transformative power of nature and of art with Peggy Hughes.

Title: Harriet Walter: Beyond The Bard
Teaser: Jackie Wylie talks to Walter (renowned for her Oliver Award-winning stage performances, and her many screen appearances including Succession and Killing Eve) about what it's like to step into Shakespeare's shoes…
Description: Harriet Walter has lived and breathed Shakespeare. Having brought many of his characters to sparkling life on stage, she knows them more intimately than most. She Speaks! is an audacious exercise of imagination and wit, where The Bard's female characters finally speak their minds. Jackie Wylie talks to Walter (renowned for her Oliver Award-winning stage performances, and her many screen appearances including Succession and Killing Eve) about what it's like to step into Shakespeare's shoes.

Title: Rewrite a Career in Books: Jan Van Der Veken
Teaser: Recognised as one of the most distinctive Belgian illustrators, Jan will discuss his career to date, his passion for art and illustration, and how there is no one path to getting into books…
Description: After studying graphic design and training as a pilot, Jan Van Der Veken is now recognised as one of the most distinctive Belgian illustrators. His retro-futurist style has graced covers for the New Yorker and most recently, illustrated titles for older children. Jan will discuss his career to date, his passion for art and illustration, and how there is no one path to getting into books. You can also try your hand at your own creative making!

Title: If I Were Prime Minister with Ella Okstad and Trygve Skaug
Teaser: Sharing their new book, If I Were Prime Minister, author Trygve Skaug and illustrator Ella Okstad will encourage you to dream big – and there’ll be some singing, dancing, and drawing too. Bring your pencils (and your imaginations)…
Description: If you were in charge of the UK, what would you do first? Maybe you’d make all the grown-ups come to nursery. Maybe you’d make cars run on giant legs instead of petrol. Sharing their new book, If I Were Prime Minister, author Trygve Skaug and illustrator Ella Okstad will encourage you to dream big – and there’ll be some singing, dancing, and drawing too. Bring your pencils (and your imaginations).

Title: How to Write a Comic with Neill Cameron
Teaser: Get your creativity flowing as you learn how to make your stories come alive in this event by author of the Mega Robo Bros series, Neill Cameron…
Description: Get your creativity flowing as you learn how to make your stories come alive in this event by author of the Mega Robo Bros series, Neill Cameron. With a little help from Neill you’ll turn your amazing ideas into even more amazing comics. There will also be a draw-along inspired by his latest book Donut Squad Take Over the World where you can recreate some of the hilarious characters or design some of your own.

Title: Eimear McBride: Ingredients for Intensity
Teaser: Eimear McBride (Women's Prize­winning author of A Girl is a Half-Formed Thing and The Lesser Bohemians) often dwells in dark, confronting subject matter, yet her writing style is infused with playfulness. Nouns become verbs, sentences fragment, time……
Description: Eimear McBride (Women's Prize­winning author of A Girl is a Half-Formed Thing and The Lesser Bohemians) often dwells in dark, confronting subject matter, yet her writing style is infused with playfulness. Nouns become verbs, sentences fragment, time jumps around. We're thrilled to welcome her back, today in conversation about The City Changes Its Face - a novel of boiling emotions set in 90s Camden right when a love affair faces its first major test. Chaired by Graeme Macrae Burnet.

Title: Ben Alderson-Day & Adam Zeman: The Science of Imagination
Teaser: Reading, reminiscing, planning, daydreaming - none of these activities is possible without the imagination. But how do our imaginations work? And how do our experiences differ?…
Description: Reading, reminiscing, planning, daydreaming - none of these activities is possible without the imagination. But how do our imaginations work? And how do our experiences differ? Join pioneering neuroscientist Adam Zeman (The Shape of Things Unseen) and lead researcher for Durham University's ReaderBank, Ben Alderson-Day, as they unpack the latest scientific discoveries relating to the brain's creative powers, from the phenomenon of 'aphantasia' to what happens in our minds as we imagine. Chaired by Dina Nayeri.

Title: Thought Exercise: John Kay
Teaser: Hear from experts on urgent issues of our time, then join in on the discussion during a wide-ranging, interactive exchange. Today's guest is leading British economist John Kay, sharing his incisive and provocative new book, The Corporation in the 21st…
Description: Dig deeper with our Thought Exercise series. Hear from experts on urgent issues of our time, then join in on the discussion during a wide-ranging, interactive exchange. Today’s guest is leading British economist John Kay, sharing his incisive and provocative new book, The Corporation in the 21st Century. Together, discuss how we might redefine what successful commercial activity and leadership looks like, and how businesses can – and do – add value to society. Chaired by Chris Birt.

Title: Get Drawing with Adeola Sokunbi
Teaser: Expect a colourful drawing session where you can unleash your own imagination to draw your very own friendly (or even scary) monsters…
Description: Get your pencils and sketchbooks at the ready for this INKTASTIC event! Adeola Sokunbi, author-illustrator of Destiny Ink: Birthday Secret (and more), introduces the wonderful world of Destiny – a girl who uses creativity to overcome her worries and heal friendships through artistic expression. Expect a colourful drawing session where you can unleash your own imagination to draw your very own friendly (or even scary) monsters.

Title: Find your Smile with Catherine Rayner
Teaser: Grab your party hats and get ready to celebrate all the things that make you smile in this fun, interactive event featuring lots of live-drawing from Catherine in her beautiful style…
Description: Augustus the tiger has lost his smile. Can you help him find it? Celebrate the 20th anniversary of Augustus and his Smile – the first book that now bestselling author-illustrator Catherine Rayner ever published, way back in 2005. Grab your party hats and get ready to celebrate all the things that make you smile in this fun, interactive event featuring lots of live-drawing from Catherine in her beautiful style.

Title: Build a Graphic Novel with Edward Ross
Teaser: The perfect workshop for budding artists and aspiring storytellers…
Description: The perfect workshop for budding artists and aspiring storytellers. Join comic artist Edward Ross as he dives into the building blocks of the creative process, based on his book Graphic Novel Builder, which guides readers on how to make their own comic. Learn how to plot out a story, create characters, build worlds, and level up your drawing skills in this fun, interactive workshop.

Title: Catherine Chidgey: Conscious Tissue
Teaser: Catherine Chidgey, the twice Women’s Prize-longlisted author of Pet, talks with us about her thrillingly unnerving dystopian vision, her magpie mind, and living in a world where some lives are valued less than others…
Description: Take your medicine, record your dreams, report your sins in The Book of Guilt. The triplet boys at the centre of celebrated Kiwi writer Catherine Chidgey’s ninth novel live a sheltered, closely monitored life. But questions about them, and their future, abound. The twice Women’s Prize-longlisted author of Pet talks with us about her thrillingly unnerving dystopian vision, her magpie mind, and living in a world where some lives are valued less than others. Chaired by Di Speirs.

Title: Can Dogs Speak Scots? with the Scots Language Centre
Teaser: Is your family pet a Scots speaker? Let’s find out! Join the Scots Language Centre’s Laura Green for a fun family session, as we teach our dogs Scots. Bairns are encouraged to bring along a soft toy to practise with, and there will be songs, stories…
Description: Is your family pet a Scots speaker? Let’s find out! Join the Scots Language Centre’s Laura Green for a fun family session, as we teach our dogs Scots. Bairns are encouraged to bring along a soft toy to practise with, and there will be songs, stories, arts, and crafts. It’s gan tae be braw!

Title: Richard Susskind: Navigating the AI Revolution
Teaser: Drawing on 40 years’ experience in the field, for Richard Susskind, balancing the benefits and threats of artificial intelligence is the defining challenge of our age…
Description: For Richard Susskind, balancing the benefits and threats of artificial intelligence is the defining challenge of our age. Drawing on 40 years’ experience in the field, his multidisciplinary book How to Think about AI: A Guide for the Perplexed demystifies AI’s ethical, economic, and social implications. Hear Susskind today, cutting through the still-unfolding maze of uncertainty to show us how to think responsibly about our technological future. Chaired by Shannon Vallor.

Title: Uilleam Blacker & Olesya Khromeychuk: The Ukraine Shelf
Teaser: As the war in Ukraine continues, The Ukraine Shelf podcast brings together leading authors, scholars, and journalists for lively and informed discussions about what we should be reading to better understand Ukraine and its place in the world during this…
Description: As the war in Ukraine continues, The Ukraine Shelf podcast brings together leading authors, scholars, and journalists for lively and informed discussions about what we should be reading to better understand Ukraine and its place in the world during this crucial period. This special live edition is hosted by the podcast's creators Olesya Khromeychuk (author The Death of a Soldier Told By His Sister and director of the Ukraine Institute London) and literary translator and Ukraine scholar, Uilleam Blacker. Today they are joined by poet Oksana Maksymchuk and international lawyer and author Philippe Sands.

Title: Jenny Kleeman, Ben Alderson-Day & Emily Postan: Mental Health in the Digital Age
Teaser: Join this insightful conversation with specialists in the field including Ben Alderson-Day and journalist Jenny Kleeman…
Description: As the world grapples with the ethics of digital technology, one area of medicine – mental health – is making fascinating strides in virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and artificial intelligence (AI) treatments. With foundations like Wellcome researching the benefits of tech solutions for mental health conditions, what moral considerations and safeguards are needed to embed these treatments in the mainstream? Join this insightful conversation with specialists in the field including Ben Alderson-Day, Emily Postan, and journalist Jenny Kleeman. Chaired by Mary Robson.

Title: Alexis Wright: All Time Is Important
Teaser: Hear this giant of Australian letters, joining us remotely from Queensland, discussing her astounding work and being a 'massive antidote' to short attention spans…
Description: One of Australia's most fearless writers, Alexis Wright (appearing remotely) is the only person to win both of Australia's most prestigious prizes (the Miles Franklin Award and Stella Prize) twice. Her panoramic new work, Praiseworthy, takes inspiration from the oral storytelling traditions of Waanyi people from the Gulf of Carpentaria as much as international writers, including Carlos Fuentes. Hear this giant of Australian letters, joining us remotely from Queensland, discussing her astounding work and being a 'massive antidote' to short attention spans. Chaired by Deirdre Osborne.

Title: Beyond the Archives with Doug Johnstone & Ewan Morrison
Teaser: Now in its centenary year, the National Library of Scotland is a treasure trove of Scotland's literary past - but did you know it also cares for the archives of our nation's contemporary writers? Today, we explore the idea of a 'living archive' with…
Description: Now in its centenary year, the National Library of Scotland is a treasure trove of Scotland's literary past - but did you know it also cares for the archives of our nation's contemporary writers? Today, we explore the idea of a 'living archive' with authors Doug Johnstone and Ewan Morrison. Join them for a conversation with Mary Paulson-Ellis about building an archive, the creative and curatorial choices involved, and discover the personal objects that fuel each writer's creative life.

Title: Solve Mysteries with Robin Stevens
Teaser: Dust off your trench coat and look out your magnifying glass! Whether you are part of the Detective Society, a Ministry member or just want to join the party, hear from brilliant author, Robin Stevens as she shares her new book, The Most Unladylike…
Description: Dust off your trench coat and look out your magnifying glass! Whether you are part of the Detective Society, a Ministry member or just want to join the party, hear from brilliant author, Robin Stevens as she shares her new book, The Most Unladylike Puzzle Book. Crack the code to Robin’s top tips for mystery-solving and take a look forward to what’s next in the Ministry of Unladylike Activity.

Title: A Memorable Storytime with Mike Nicholson
Teaser: Come join in on the chaos as you help Mike finish the story and remember all the things Granny brought (from hairy highland cows to sugary shortbread)…
Description: Enjoy a fun-packed event of singing, guessing, suggesting, and remembering, as author Mike Nicholson reads from his latest book based on the popular memory game, My Granny Went to Scotland and She Brought Back… Come join in on the chaos as you help Mike finish the story and remember all the things Granny brought (from hairy highland cows to sugary shortbread).

Title: Scots Bookbug
Teaser: Bring yer wee yins alang fir a Scots Bookbug wi sangs, rhymes, an stories. Abody’s welcome, whither ye’re a gallus Scots speaker or a wee feartie!…
Description: Bring yer wee yins alang fir a Scots Bookbug wi sangs, rhymes, an stories. Abody’s welcome, whither ye’re a gallus Scots speaker or a wee feartie!

Title: Nell Zink & Nicola Barker: Our Big, Strange World
Teaser: Great comic novels remind us that the world is bigger and weirder than we think. Camilla Grudovajoins two modern virtuosos of this enduring form: Nell Zink and Nicola Barker…
Description: Great comic novels remind us that the world is bigger and weirder than we think. Camilla Grudova joins two modern virtuosos of this enduring form: Nell Zink and Nicola Barker. Zink's Sister Europe takes us on a rambunctious, hedonistic tour of Berlin; Barker's TonyInterruptor pursues the truth of the titular disruptor. Both will remind you that fringe behaviour has much to say about us all - that's the crux of the comic spirit.

Title: An All Star Poetry Line Up
Teaser: Sometimes, only poetry will do. There’s something in the concentrated way poets see the world that can open us up to new ways of seeing, thinking, and hoping too…
Description: Sometimes, only poetry will do. There’s something in the concentrated way poets see the world that can open us up to new ways of seeing, thinking, and hoping too. We are joined by a dazzling cast of acclaimed poets performing their work side by side, featuring Zena Agha, Anthony Joseph, Len Lukowski, Ellen Renton, and Oluwaseun Olayiwola. A memorable event celebrating the breadth, depth and power of contemporary poetry awaits. Chaired by Hannah Lavery.

Title: Mona Arshi, Jackie Kay & Karen McCarthy Woolf: Nature Matters
Teaser: In an effort to decolonise the art of nature writing, Faber's Nature Matters anthology draws together work by nearly 80 different poets from the African, Asian, and Caribbean diaspora, on themes encompassing climate crisis, protest, Indigenous wisdom and…
Description: In an effort to decolonise the art of nature writing, Faber's Nature Matters anthology draws together work by nearly 80 different poets from the African, Asian, and Caribbean diaspora, on themes encompassing climate crisis, protest, Indigenous wisdom and alternative history. See the book's co-editors, Karen McCarthy Woolf and Mona Arshi, come together with contributor Jackie Kay to celebrate this landmark collection. Chaired by Sunnah Khan.

Title: Stress Test - Live
Teaser: A highlight of our annual programme, Stress Test (created by writers Joe Dunthorne and Ella Frears) sees poets and musicians join forces to create a brand-new song in front of your very eyes and ears… in just 15 minutes!…
Description: A highlight of our annual programme, Stress Test (created by writers Joe Dunthorne and Ella Frears) sees poets and musicians join forces to create a brand-new song in front of your very eyes and ears… in just 15 minutes! It might result in an absolute banger, or things could go completely off-piste – it’s all up to that mysterious muse. But what is guaranteed is a fun and fascinating hour of witnessing creativity in action with musician and special guest, Dan Wilson (Withered Hand).

Title: Mike Berners-Lee: Climate Action and the Power of Truth
Teaser: Global emissions are worse than ever. The ‘polycrisis’ we face reaches far beyond the climate. Why have we continued to fail when we have the means to succeed?…
Description: Global emissions are worse than ever. The ‘polycrisis’ we face reaches far beyond the climate. Why have we continued to fail when we have the means to succeed? Acclaimed researcher Mike Berners-Lee argues in A Climate of Truth that by focusing on the concept of honesty in our politics, media, and businesses, we can make a radical impact and have more efficiency than we thought possible. His conversation with us today will leave you energised for action. Chaired by Yassmin Abdel-Magied.

Title: 1995: Grrrls Aloud
Teaser: Murrayfield might be basking in Oasis nostalgia, but the mid-90s wasn't all blokes and Britpop. Join BBC broadcaster and A Kick Up the Arts host Nicola Meighan for a celebration of Scotland's femme-powered revolution, circa '95…
Description: Murrayfield might be basking in Oasis nostalgia, but the mid-90s wasn't all blokes and Britpop. Join BBC broadcaster and A Kick Up The Arts host Nicola Meighan for a celebration of the femme-powered revolution that was kicking off in Scotland, circa ‘95. It was the summer that Garbage released their debut album; that Annie Lennox ruled the charts with Medusa; that Glasgow's Delgados upturned the landscape with their songs, and label, Chemikal Underground. The band’s Emma Pollock reflects on that time - and its reverberations to this day - with Cora Bissett, Carrie Marshall, and Chitra Ramaswamy, soundtracked by a fired-up playlist, and live music from Hen Hoose Collective’s Cariss Crosbie. What’s the story? Oh, there’s always more than one…

Title: Catherine Chidgey & Laila Lalami: Dreaming Dangerously
Teaser: Master storytellers Catherine Chidgey and Laila Lalami have created two chilling new dystopian tales in which dreams are monitored for control and surveillance. The authors chat privacy, freedom, and speculative visions…
Description: Master storytellers Catherine Chidgey and Laila Lalami have created two chilling new dystopian tales in which dreams are monitored for control and surveillance. Chidgey’s Ishiguro-esque The Book of Guilt centres around triplet boys in a strange children’s home, while Lalami’s Women’s Prize-longlisted The Dream Hotel follows a woman detained at a border crossing because she has been deemed a ‘dangerous dreamer’. The authors chat privacy, freedom, and speculative visions. Chaired by Jane Flett.

Title: Surekha Davies, Omar El Akkad & Nicola Kelly: Who Counts as Human?
Teaser: Three writers grappling with the toxic rhetoric humans apply to one another explore how the boundaries of humanity are set to exclude certain communities…
Description: Three writers grappling with the toxic rhetoric humans apply to one another explore how the boundaries of humanity are set to exclude certain communities. Surekha Davies (Humans: A Monstrous History), Omar El Akkad (One Day Everyone Will Always Have Been Against This) and Nicola Kelly (Anywhere But Here) will provide their piercing insights in this must-see event for all who are interested in how we repair the polarisation of our fractured world. Chaired by Yassmin Abdel-Magied .

Title: Foday Mannah: The Search for Othella Savage
Teaser: Set within Scotland’s Sierra Leonean community, Foday Mannah’s The Search for Othella Savage, is a vibrant mystery. Today Mannah asks – can loyalty always prevail over power?…
Description: When a young woman dies after being found unconscious in the boot of her own car, then another disappears, a lethal struggle begins between corrupt political and religious institutions, personal faith, and the power of friendship. Set within Scotland’s Sierra Leonean community, Foday Mannah’s Mo Siewcharran Prize-winning debut, The Search for Othella Savage, is a vibrant mystery. Today Mannah asks – can loyalty always prevail over power? Chaired by Halla Mohieddeen.

Title: Blast Off! A Creative Workshop with Jan Van Der Veken
Teaser: Delve into the wonderful world of boats and space with Belgian illustrator Jan Van Der Veken, author of Boats, Steamers, Icebreakers, and Ghost Ships (translated by Kristen Gehrman)…
Description: Delve into the wonderful world of boats and space with Belgian illustrator Jan Van Der Veken, author of Boats, Steamers, Icebreakers, and Ghost Ships (translated by Kristen Gehrman). Explore the history and science of water and space travel, experiment with the science behind some of the rockets and boats by making your own versions, and get inspired to draw based on Jan’s signature retro-futurist style. Three – two – one – lift off!!

Title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
Teaser: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Appearing today: Lindsey Hirst…
Description: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Appearing today: Lindsey Hirst.

Title: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle with Polly Faber
Teaser: In this event for curious and climate-conscious minds, learn why recycling is important, what happens after we recycle, and the impact this all has on our planet. There’ll be fun and games, and brilliant ideas for how we can reuse stuff to make totally…
Description: Have you ever wondered where rubbish goes after you put it in the recycling bin? Well Polly Faber, author of Recycling Day, has the answers! In this event for curious and climate-conscious minds, learn why recycling is important, what happens after we recycle, and the impact this all has on our planet. There’ll be fun and games, and brilliant ideas for how we can reuse stuff to make totally not-rubbish things!

Title: Diana Henry: A Life in Food
Teaser: Diana Henry is one of the UK’s best loved food writers, celebrated for her vivid, nourishing essays and cookbooks. Join in this warm, inspiring conversation, chaired by Marjorie Lotfi, about the joy and power of good food…
Description: Diana Henry is one of the UK’s best loved food writers, celebrated for her vivid, nourishing essays and cookbooks. Henry has plentiful stories to share from over two decades travelling, writing, and, most importantly, eating her way across the globe, from the suburbs of Rome to the hillsides of Vermont. Reflecting on Crazy Water, Pickled Lemons, join this warm, inspiring conversation, chaired by Marjorie Lotfi, about the joy and power of good food.

Title: Ali Smith: Brave New Words
Teaser: Nimble, playful, canny, subversive – four-time Booker-shortlisted Ali Smith returns to the Festival with Gliff. Written with her singular blend of whimsy and gravitas, the novel is a near-future dystopia, meditating on themes of resistance, the making of…
Description: Nimble, playful, canny, subversive – four-time Booker-shortlisted Ali Smith returns to the Festival with Gliff. Written with her singular blend of whimsy and gravitas, the novel is a near-future dystopia, meditating on themes of resistance, the making of meaning, and how we can confront dark times with hope. Hear one of fiction's finest voices talking about a novel that, according to The Bee Sting author Paul Murray, is both 'pitch-black' and 'tender, hilarious, and ultimately uplifting'. Chaired by Sarah Wood.

Title: Multisolving: A Workshop with Alex Pearson
Teaser: Multisolving is a growing movement around the world, encouraging people to work together across sectors to address multiple problems with a single policy or investment…
Description: Multisolving is a growing movement around the world, encouraging people to work together across sectors to address multiple problems with a single policy or investment. It’s a way to look at the whole picture and help everyone, but it isn’t always easy or simple. Join Alex Pearson, author of Curious, Creative, Connected, to explore the radical potential of multisolving across a range of issues, investments, and policies; benefit from research, tools, and stories; and understand how to approach multisolving in our own lives.

Title: A L Kennedy: Small Kind Details
Teaser: Kennedy (author, comedian, and longtime BBC radio writer and host) joins us to discuss the real heart of her novel: the nature of justice and mercy, and the power of hope and kindness…
Description: Spanning love and resilience in the face of a callous state, and abuses of patriarchal power by government, police, and those closer to home - A L Kennedy's latest novel, Alive in the Merciful Country, could hardly feel more timely. Kennedy (author, comedian, and longtime BBC radio writer and host) joins Zoe Venditozzi to discuss the real heart of her novel: the nature of justice and mercy, and the power of hope and kindness.

Title: Mark Billingham & Clare Mackintosh: Murder Series Uncovered
Teaser: What does it take to write a thrilling murder mystery series? Join us as the authors sit down together to dissect how to create multi-faceted characters who live in the minds of readers…
Description: What does it take to write a thrilling murder mystery series? No one knows better than Clare Mackintosh, author of the bestselling DC Morgan series and Sunday Times bestselling author Mark Billingham. Join us as they sit down together to dissect how to create multi-faceted characters who live in the minds of readers across multiple books and labyrinthine plots. Chaired by Bryan Burnett.

Title: Maggie Nelson & Oluwaseun Olayiwola: Embodied Interiority
Teaser: Our relationships with our bodies can be both intimate and alien at once. How can we feel at home in them? Together, genre-defying writer Maggie Nelson (Pathemata) and poet and choreographer Oluwaseun Olayiwola (Strange Beach) explore how our bodies can…
Description: Our relationships with our bodies can be both intimate and alien at once. How can we feel at home in them? Together, genre-defying writer Maggie Nelson (Pathemata) and poet and choreographer Oluwaseun Olayiwola (Strange Beach) explore how our bodies can be the sites of agony and unbridled pleasure. How might we cultivate the courage to open ourselves to new ideas of what our bodies can give and receive for the limited time that we inhabit them? Chaired by Mairi Oliver.

Title: Thought Exercise: Laurie Bristow
Teaser: Dig deeper with our Thought Exercise series. Hear from experts on urgent issues of our time, then join in on the discussion during a wide-ranging, interactive exchange…
Description: Dig deeper with our Thought Exercise series. Hear from experts on urgent issues of our time, then join in on the discussion during a wide-ranging, interactive exchange. Today’s guest, falling on the 4th anniversary of the fall of Kabul to the Taliban, is Laurie Bristow (Kabul: Final Call), the last British ambassador to Afghanistan (2021) and former ambassador to Russia (2016-2020). Together, you’ll take part in a fascinating conversation on geopolitics and deterrence, as you discuss the crucial role of diplomacy in times of global political unrest. Chaired by Liz Lloyd.

Title: Creative Repair: A Junk Journals Workshop with Rachel Hazell
Teaser: Explore the Festival's overarching theme of Repair through the art of junk journaling: transforming discarded ephemera into beautiful books. This hands-on workshop with bookbinder Rachel Hazell invites you to engage in mindful making through collage…
Description: Explore the Festival's overarching theme of Repair through the art of junk journaling: transforming discarded ephemera into beautiful books. This hands-on workshop with bookbinder Rachel Hazell invites you to engage in mindful making through collage. Materials are provided, though you're invited to bring your own 'found handwriting' (from crumpled shopping lists to old birthday cards) allowing you to uncover new personal stories from within their recycled fragments.

Title: Leila Aboulela & Karen Campbell: Watch Me Begin Again
Teaser: What would you do if you were given a second chance? An opportunity to start again and do things differently? Join us for this heartwarming event celebrating the Festival's theme of Repair…
Description: What would you do if you were given a second chance? An opportunity to start again and do things differently? Leila Aboulela's A New Year and Karen Campbell's This Bright Life explore what happens when we are forced to rebuild our lives. Join us for this heartwarming event celebrating the Festival's theme of Repair. Chaired by Claire Urquhart.

Title: Poetry Pharmacy with Deborah Alma
Teaser: Hear Deborah today as she reflects on the ways poetry can inspire, comfort, and heal us – it’s a much-needed balm for our busy lives…
Description: The Poetry Prescription series, compiled by Deborah Alma, is the perfect antidote to life’s ailments. Hear Deborah today as she chats with Nadine Aisha Jassat, reflecting on the ways poetry can inspire, comfort, and heal us – it’s a much-needed balm for our busy lives. After the event, you’ll have the chance to receive your very own ‘poetry pill’, because there really is a poem for everything.

Title: Jim Swire & Peter Biddulph: Fighting for the Truth
Teaser: The 1988 bombing of Pan Am Flight 103 has resurged in public consciousness following Sky's recent drama Lockerbie: A Search for Truth. Dr Jim Swire's daughter Flora was killed on the ground, and The Lockerbie Bombing: A Father's Search for Justice…
Description: The 1988 bombing of Pan Am Flight 103 has resurged in public consciousness following Sky's recent drama Lockerbie: A Search for Truth. Dr Jim Swire's daughter Flora was killed on the flight, and The Lockerbie Bombing: A Father's Search for Justice, co-authored with Peter Biddulph, details his moving fight for the truth of how the tragedy was able to happen, and who was ultimately responsible for the largest loss of lives in a single event in modern British history. He and Biddulph speak today to Allan Little.

Title: Kelly Weinersmith: To Boldly Go?
Teaser: Hear Weinersmith chat with us about this hilarious, wise, deeply-researched project that makes us glad to still live on our third rock from the sun. Plus, find out which books made 2025’s prize shortlist…
Description: Last year, Zach and Kelly Weinersmith’s A City on Mars won the Royal Society Science Book Prize, a book asking one of humanity’s biggest questions: will we (and how would we, and should we actually maybe not) ever live in space? Hear Weinersmith chat with Steve Brusatte about this hilarious, wise, deeply-researched project that makes us glad to still live on our third rock from the sun. Plus, find out which books made 2025’s prize shortlist.

Title: Nell Zink: Grow Up, Get Old, Get Down
Teaser: Nell Zink joins us in Edinburgh, talking about Sister Europe: a worldly hangout novel of 21st century manners set against the backdrop of a hedonistic night out in Berlin…
Description: 'Her work insistently raises the possibility that the world is larger and stranger than the world you think you know,' says Jonathan Franzen of Nell Zink. Today she joins us in Edinburgh, talking about Sister Europe: a worldly hangout novel of 21st century manners set against the backdrop of a hedonistic night out in Berlin. Today, join a novelist who's increasingly known as one the sharpest satirists of our time. Chaired by Helen McClory.

Title: Stig Abell: Letters from a Murderer
Teaser: A love letter to the crime genre, The Burial Place explores what happens when a retired city detective, a group of archaeologists, and a murderer descend upon a small idyllic town. Writer and broadcaster Stig Abell’s event is for crime lovers everywhere…
Description: Archaeology is the art of revealing and discovering human history so we can learn and grow into the future. But sometimes, things are meant to stay buried and remain lost beneath the earth’s surface. A love letter to the crime genre, The Burial Place explores what happens when a retired city detective, a group of archaeologists, and a murderer descend upon a small idyllic town. Writer and broadcaster Stig Abell’s event is for crime lovers everywhere. Chaired by Lee Randall.

Title: Gabriel Weston: An Alternative Anatomy
Teaser: Aged 20, surgeon Gabriel Weston enrolled in a pioneering degree programme encouraging arts students to become doctors. She joins us to discuss our fragile, frightening, miraculous bodies…
Description: Aged 20, surgeon Gabriel Weston enrolled in a pioneering degree programme encouraging arts students to become doctors. She quickly realised that by presenting organs in isolation, separate from the bodies they exist in, anatomical textbooks were missing a holistic view of illness. In her insightful new book, Alive, Weston delves into the role our organs play on our emotions, highlighting the importance of treating the whole patient. She joins us to discuss our fragile, frightening, miraculous bodies. Chaired by Kirsty Lang.

Title: Halle O’Neal: The Buddhist Approach to Healing
Teaser: Healing practices - physical, emotional, or spiritual - are part of what make us human; they're also key tenets of Buddhism. Join Dr Halle O'Neal, co-director of the Edinburgh Centre for Buddhist Studies, for this special discussion on the myriad forms…
Description: Healing practices - physical, emotional, or spiritual - are part of what make us human; they're also key tenets of Buddhism. They come in a wide range of inventive options, including interacting with relics, repairing broken objects, even eating slips of scripture! Join Dr Halle O'Neal, co-director of the Edinburgh Centre for Buddhist Studies, for this special discussion on the myriad forms of repair and healing offered by Buddhism across history and cultures, including for everyday challenges like illness, childbirth, and life after death.

Title: Simon Armitage: Dwell
Teaser: Inspired by Cornwall’s Lost Gardens of Heligan – an ambitious restoration project which reawakened a landscape of woods and meadows to offer a fertile realm for all sorts of creatures – Dwell, by Poet Laureate Simon Armitage, is a beautifully illustrated…
Description: Inspired by Cornwall’s Lost Gardens of Heligan – an ambitious restoration project which reawakened a landscape of woods and meadows to offer a fertile realm for all sorts of creatures – Dwell, by poet laureate Simon Armitage, is a beautifully illustrated collection about the importance of restoring nature’s balance. Join Armitage as he reflects with Nick Barley, director of the National Poetry Centre, on the fragility and power of nature, and what humans must do to repair and protect it.

Title: MC Grammar Live!
Teaser: The official and only World Book Day ambassador is bringing his debut book The Adventures of Rap to Edinburgh for the first time…
Description: The official and only World Book Day ambassador is bringing his debut book The Adventures of Rap to Edinburgh for the first time. Get ready to read, rap and party hard with social media sensation and best selling author MC Grammar.

Title: Fresh Words: A Writing Chance
Teaser: It's lunchtime, and (hallelujah!) there's no need to doomscroll over a sad desk salad. Be the first to discover the literary stars of the future, instead. In partnership with Scottish Book Trust and other leading talent spotters across the UK, this…
Description: It's lunchtime, and (hallelujah!) there's no need to doomscroll over a sad desk salad. Be the first to discover the literary stars of the future, instead. In partnership with Scottish Book Trust and other leading talent spotters across the UK, this lively lunchtime event showcases electrifying new voices, so grab your seat before everyone else does. Today, we partner with Audible and New Writing North's A Writing Chance, hearing readings from writers including Henry Bell, Sarah Forbes Stewart, Debora Maité, Julie Rea, and Sophie Underwood.

Title: Sprog Rock
Teaser: Returning to rock the Book Festival for the fifth year, it’s Sprog Rock! Dust off your dancing shoes and get ready for a rocking and (nursery) rhyming extravaganza, as the group bring their unique, catchy songs back to our Spiegeltent. Fun for…
Description: Returning to rock the Book Festival for the fifth year, it’s Sprog Rock! Dust off your dancing shoes and get ready for a rocking and (nursery) rhyming extravaganza, as the group bring their unique, catchy songs back to our Spiegeltent. Fun for under-fives, their grown-ups, friends, and families.

Title: Hamish Hawk: Life in a Scotch Sitting Room, Vol. 0
Teaser: Join local indie songwriter Hamish Hawk in a rare, lyrical homage to Scotland's pre-eminent poet-eccentric: Ivor Cutler. A celebration of Cutler's dreich spoken-word masterpiece, Life in a Scotch Sitting Room, Hawk presents new stories and songs inspired…
Description:
Join local indie songwriter Hamish Hawk in a rare, lyrical homage to Scotland's pre-eminent poet-eccentric: Ivor Cutler. A celebration of Cutler's dreich spoken-word masterpiece, Life in a Scotch Sitting Room, Hawk presents new stories and songs inspired by his own childhood home in Edinburgh, alongside unique reworkings of Cutler's original works. Joined by friends and armed with Cutler's original harmonium, this performance - a special Book Festival commission - promises an evening of wit, warmth, and words, sure to make fans of the uninitiated. Introduced by Nicola Meighan.

	Note: This performance will also take place on Saturday 16 August at 21:00.

Title: Chris Barkley & Douglas Skelton: Intrigue on the Scottish Isles
Teaser: The beautiful Scottish Isles are remote, picturesque and the perfect backdrop for a murder mystery…
Description: The beautiful Scottish Isles are remote, picturesque and the perfect backdrop for a murder mystery. Chris Barkley's debut, The Man on the Endless Stair, and Douglas Skelton's latest in the Rebecca Connolly series, The Other Side of Fear, each feature writers with mysteries to solve. They chat today about their roots, whether their own lives are as thrilling as their wordsmith characters', and the power of landscape in a good mystery. Chaired by Lee Randall.

Title: Edwin Morgan: A Legacy from Translation to Liberation
Teaser: Edwin Morgan was many things: the first Makar of Scotland, a prolific writer (with over 60 published works), a passionate translation advocate, and a person with a kaleidoscopic range of interests. Although sensationally generous with his words and…
Description: Edwin Morgan was many things: the first Makar of Scotland, a prolific writer (with over 60 published works), a passionate translation advocate, and a person with a kaleidoscopic range of interests. Although sensationally generous with his words and spirit, he did not publicly come out as a gay man until he was 70, bringing new meaning to his previous work and a sense of liberation to what came after. Today, writers including Colin Bramwell, Ellen McAteer, and Gregory Woods talk about poetry, queerness, translation, and freedom. Chaired by Ishbel McFarlane.

Title: Stuart Murdoch: Late Developer
Teaser: Taking time away from his prolific band Belle and Sebastian, singer Stuart Murdoch has penned a stunning debut novel which fictionalises his own experience with ME (a chronic fatigue illness)…
Description: Taking time away from his prolific band Belle and Sebastian, singer Stuart Murdoch has penned a stunning debut novel which fictionalises his own experience with ME (a chronic fatigue illness). Nobody’s Empire is set against the backdrop of a group of friends in early 1990s Glasgow and California. Hear Murdoch talking about his decision to write a novel rather than a memoir, and hope that the book will be an inspiration to other people with chronic illness. Chaired by James Yorkston.

Title: Olia Hercules: A Taste of Ukrainian History
Teaser: When Russia launched its most recent invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Ukrainian chef Olia Hercules decided it was finally time to tell her story…
Description: When Russia launched its most recent invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Ukrainian chef Olia Hercules decided it was finally time to tell her story. Yet her book, Strong Roots, reaches far beyond her own life span. It's by turns a memoir, a family history, a recipe guide, and an ode to Ukraine, brimming with grief and hope. Today she joins Roxani Krystalli to discuss the deep connection between food, resilience, and the idea of home.

Title: Big Feelings with Debi Gliori
Teaser: Much loved foxes, Large and Small, are back in Debi Gliori’s latest picture book No Matter What. Join Debi to think about what might help and learn that love is one feeling that never changes…
Description: Much loved foxes, Large and Small, are back in Debi Gliori’s latest picture book No Matter What. With a special picnic planned, Small can’t help but be disappointed when a raincloud spoils their day. What makes you happy when you are feeling big, sad emotions? Can you help Large cheer up Small when the rain comes? Join Debi to think about what might help and learn that love is one feeling that never changes.

Title: Potties for Beginners with Tracey Corderoy
Teaser: Become a potty super-star with Tracey Corderoy and Miss Dotty!…
Description: It’s potty-training time – and Miss Dotty’s here to show you how. Join brilliant and hilarious author Tracey Corderoy to say goodbye to nappies and learn to love potties instead. Full of fun and giggles (and reassurances that accidents can happen), Tracey will introduce you to the cast of cute animal characters in Miss Dotty’s Potty School and celebrate toilet training time with drawing and games. Everyone’s a potty super-star at Miss Dotty’s Potty School!

Title: Lucía Lijtmaer & Monika Radojevic: Fuelled by Rage
Teaser: Sharp writing and incisive perspectives are the hallmarks of Lucía Lijtmaer (Cautery) and Monika Radojevic (A Beautiful Lack of Consequence). Join them for a vital conversation about the pressures and the possibilities of female experiences…
Description: Sharp writing and incisive perspectives are the hallmarks of Lucía Lijtmaer and Monika Radojevic. In Lijtmaer’s Cautery, we meet two women, 400 years apart, both of whom share a fantasy: burning it all down and beginning again. Radojevic’s A Beautiful Lack of Consequences is a fierce, funny short story collection about female desire and the weight of societal expectations. Join them for a vital conversation about the pressures and the possibilities of female experiences. Chaired by Anahit Behrooz.

Title: Sam Heughan: On the Rocks
