Teaser: Nothing marks a special occasion better than a stunning cocktail, and this event is a special one indeed as Outlander actor, founder of Sassenach Spirits, and local lad Sam Heughan launches his new book, The Cocktail Diaries…
Description:
Age limit: 18+

	Nothing marks a special occasion better than a stunning cocktail, and this event is a special one indeed as Outlander actor, founder of Sassenach Spirits, and local lad Sam Heughan launches his new book, The Cocktail Diaries. Journey around the world with Heughan as he shares his favourite cocktails, the stories behind them, and the memories they made. Join us for a truly spirited and intimate evening (and there might even be a wee tipple). Sláinte! Chaired by Nicola Roy.

Title: Jessica J Lee & Jason Allen-Paisant: Taking Root
Teaser: Join two writers who have turned their pens towards nature and belonging…
Description: Join two writers who have turned their pens towards nature and belonging. In Jhalak Prize-longlisted Dispersals, Jessica J Lee examines how plants and people come to belong in a place, considering how tightly we’re entwined with Earth’s flora. And T.S. Eliot Prize-winner Jason Allen-Paisant’s The Possibility of Tenderness is a lyrical personal history of migration, exploring how the plants and people of home offer different ways of living in a new country. Chaired by Hannah Lavery.

Title: Oi Dinosaurs! with Kes Gray
Teaser: So… Velociraptors didn’t sit on plug adaptors? And Triceratops didn’t sit on lollipops? Well, what did dinosaurs sit on then? Join bestselling (and hilarious!) author Kes Gray for the ultimate dino-packed event with Oi Dinosaurs!…
Description: So… Velociraptors didn’t sit on plug adaptors? And Triceratops didn’t sit on lollipops? Well, what did dinosaurs sit on then? Join bestselling (and hilarious!) author Kes Gray for the ultimate dino-packed event with Oi Dinosaurs! in the next instalment of the brilliant Frog and Friends series. Frog, Cat, and Dog are ready for oodles of prehistoric rhyming fun packed with dinosaurs, mammoths and – of course – frogs!

Title: Old Town Bookshop Tour: Meander and Mingle with the Bookshop Crawl UK
Teaser: Amid the crowds and chaos of Edinburgh in August, does calmly exploring the city’s Old Town and quaint bookshops with likeminded people sound more like your cup of tea? If so, we’ve got the perfect tour for you…
Description: Amid the crowds and chaos of Edinburgh in August, does calmly exploring the city’s Old Town and quaint bookshops with likeminded people sound more like your cup of tea? If so, we’ve got the perfect tour for you. Join our partners the Bookshop Crawl UK on a specially curated walking tour, where you’ll meander through cobbled streets, browse a range of local bookshops, and mingle with fellow readers – with some special treats along the way!

Title: Dawn O’Porter: Friendship Forever
Teaser: Growing up in Guernsey had a deep impact on Sunday Times bestseller Dawn O’Porter, with island life seeping into her writing…
Description: Growing up in Guernsey had a deep impact on Sunday Times bestseller Dawn O’Porter, with island life seeping into her writing. In Honeybee – the third of her Renée and Flo novels – the childhood friends, now in their early 20s, return to Guernsey to face their past and work out what being an adult really means. Join O’Porter today for a lively chat about friendship, islanders, and those heady years of early adulthood. Chaired by Denise Mina.

Title: Adrian Tchaikovsky: The Darkness Looked Back
Teaser: Science fiction has always had a unique capacity to address the big philosophical questions, especially those asking us to extend our purview beyond a human-centric view. In Bee Speaker and Shroud, Arthur C Clarke Award-winning writer Adrian Tchaikovsky…
Description: Science fiction has always had a unique capacity to address the big philosophical questions, especially those asking us to extend our purview beyond a human-centric view. In Bee Speaker and Shroud, Arthur C Clarke Award-winning writer Adrian Tchaikovsky gives us two novels doing just that. Back after a knockout event with us last year, don't miss Tchaikovsky chatting with Doug Johnstone about everything from bioethics and insects to how we might communicate the incommunicable.

Title: Sarah Moss: Exits and Entrances
Teaser: The author of Summerwater and Ghost Wall joins the Festival with Ripeness: a decades spanning story meditating on severed family ties and the decisions that define our lives. Explore themes of migration, belonging, new beginnings, and the idea of home…
Description: The immaculate novels of Sarah Moss frequently investigate family dynamics and how people react when pushed to their limits. An expert at creating subtle tension with an extraordinary knack for telling the truth, the author of Summerwater and Ghost Wall joins the Festival with Ripeness: a decades spanning story meditating on severed family ties and the decisions that define our lives. Hear Moss in conversatioin with Eleanor Catton as she unpacks themes of migration, belonging, new beginnings, and the idea of home.

Title: Friends, Fortune-tellers and Ferocious beasts with Radhika Sanghani and RAMZEE
Teaser: Authors Radhika Sanghani and RAMZEE know a thing or two about solving life’s daily worries. Hear them chat all things popularity and friendships, with some fortune-telling and hunting for beasts thrown in!…
Description: Authors Radhika Sanghani and RAMZEE know a thing or two about solving life’s daily worries. In Radhika’s latest book How to Get Magically Popular, Sabina is desperate to fit in but her magical powers keep making her stand out. While RAMZEE’s The Cheat Book (Vol.2), is packed full of life-hacks for literally any occasion… even escaping wild animals. Hear them chat all things popularity and friendships, with some fortune-telling and hunting for beasts thrown in! Chaired by Siân Bevan.

Title: Aja Barber: You Don’t Need More Stuff
Teaser: Join Aja Barber today for a hard-hitting, solutions-focussed look consumption culture, the ways we can break out of it, and why saying no to more 'stuff' is a stance of power…
Description: Aja Barber wants change. And her powerful book Consumed – about the intersections between fast-fashion, climate, and colonialism – will make you believe that it might actually be possible. A stylist, model, and sustainability consultant, Barber speaks with much-needed frankness about the mess we’ve got ourselves into. But she also approaches the subject with humour, compassion, and – perhaps most compellingly – hope. Join her today, in conversation with Anahit Behrooz, for a hard-hitting, solutions-focussed look consumption culture, the ways we can break out of it, and why saying no to more 'stuff' is really a stance of power.

Title: David Szalay: What Makes a Life?
Teaser: Ranging from communist Hungary to the London of the super-rich, David Szalay's Flesh unravels a man via a story collection hiding inside a novel. Today, meet an already garlanded writer; one blessed with rare authority when dealing with the most…
Description: Ranging from communist Hungary to the London of the super-rich, David Szalay's Flesh unravels a man via a story collection hiding inside a novel. Today, meet an already garlanded writer; one blessed with rare authority when dealing with the most compelling of subjects: life in glorious technicolour. And it's all there to be discussed: masculinity, sex, desire, attainment, money, success, and prosperity equating to success - and the fallacy of it all. Chaired by Michael Magee.

Title: Mary Costello & Elaine Garvey: Push and Pull
Teaser: The disquiet of modern life, a feeling of the past living alongside the present, the push and pull of rural places calling you home - each are overlapping preoccupations of award-winning author Mary Costello's new story collection, Barcelona, and Elaine……
Description: The disquiet of modern life, a feeling of the past living alongside the present, the push and pull of rural places calling you home - each are overlapping preoccupations of award-winning author Mary Costello's new story collection, Barcelona, and Elaine Garvey's The Wardrobe Department (picked as best debut of the year by the Financial Times). In this mesmerising event, hear the authors of these haunting new Irish works in conversation today. Chaired by Emma Collins.

Title: Blast to the Past with Maisie Chan
Teaser: Come hear Maisie chat about this period of history and the real-life inspiration behind her writing…
Description: What do you get when you combine flying roast chickens, Chinese New Year, and…karaoke? Maisie Chan’s newest book, Nate Yu’s Blast from the Past, that’s what! When Nate gets hold of an artefact from the First World War, it sparks a friendship he doesn’t see coming – because his new friend is a ghost. Come hear Maisie chat about this period of history and the real-life inspiration behind her writing.

Title: Linder & Adele Patrick: Gimme Danger
Teaser: Linder is one of Britain's great pop­culture provocateurs: a post-punk musician and widely exhibited photocollage artist…
Description: Linder is one of Britain's great pop­-culture provocateurs: a post-punk musician and widely exhibited photocollage artist (infamously on the sleeve of the Buzzcocks' 'Orgasm Addict' single). Here she’ll collide in discussion with the amazing Adele Patrick – a coach, mentor, writer, and co-founder of the iconic Glasgow Women’s Library, Patrick has collaborated with, curated and commissioned works from some of the most significant feminist artists working today including Linder. Hear both of these powerful creatives discussing feminism, fashion, creativity, building upon the release of the Linder’s retrospective, Danger Came Smiling. Chaired by Edinburgh Art Festival director Kim McAleese.

Title: Vincenzo Latronico & Ayşegül Savaş: Modern Life Under the Microscope
Teaser: Leading lights of international fiction Vincenzo Latronico and Ayşegül Savas join us with two very different novels, both subjecting millennial couples and their lives to the microscope. Latronico's International Booker-shortlisted Perfection delivers a……
Description: Leading lights of international fiction Vincenzo Latronico and Ayşegül Savaş join us with two very different novels, both subjecting millennial couples and their lives to the microscope. Latronico's International Booker-shortlisted Perfection delivers a scathing satire of aspirational consumerism, while Savaş' impeccable The Anthropologists is an intimate celebration of ordinary moments and watching life go by. Hear the authors talk about the modern pursuit of authenticity and how to live a meaningful life. Chaired by Adam Biles.

Title: Anthony Delaney & Alice Loxton: Cobwebs Not Included
Teaser: Ah, history… musty, stuffy, cobwebby stuff, right? Wrong – with Anthony Delaney’s Queer Georgians and Alice Loxton’s Eighteen, you’re getting history that’s as fizzing with verve and wit as its authors. Join two of the brightest young historians today…
Description: Ah, history… musty, stuffy, cobwebby stuff, right? Wrong – with Anthony Delaney’s Queer Georgians and Alice Loxton’s Eighteen, you’re getting history that’s as fizzing with verve and wit as its authors. Join two of the brightest young historians to uncover the hidden, unwritten lives of the pioneers of queer culture, and an eclectic cast of eighteen historically significant 18-year-olds. This is without question history at its most original, relevant, and contemporary. Chaired by Dr Jean Menzies.

Title: Paula Akpan: Histories Rewritten
Teaser: Join When We Ruled author Paula Akpan as she shares the gripping stories of twelve African queens and warriors. Some were brave and noble, others unpredictable and volatile, but all shaped the African continent - so why don't we all know their names?…
Description: You might think you know your queens, but what about Queen Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba and her brilliant military tactics? Maybe Makobo Modjadji VI, Rain Queen of Balobedu? Or Ranavalona I, Queen of Madagascar (and ruthless dictator)? Join When We Ruled author Paula Akpan as she shares the gripping stories of twelve African queens and warriors. Some were brave and noble, others unpredictable and volatile, but all shaped the African continent - so why don't we all know their names? Chaired by Carmen Thompson.

Title: The Essentials of Fiction: A Workshop with Sarah Shin
Teaser: ‘An awareness of what your own writing sounds like is an essential skill for a writer,’ commented the legendary Ursula K Le Guin’s in Steering the Craft: A 21st Century Guide to Sailing the Sea of Story. Today’s workshop uses this title as a guide for…
Description: ‘An awareness of what your own writing sounds like is an essential skill for a writer,’ commented the legendary Ursula K Le Guin’s in Steering the Craft: A 21st Century Guide to Sailing the Sea of Story. Today’s workshop uses this title as a guide for practicing your writing, focussing on the sound of language. Join writer, editor and researcher Sarah Shin for a relaxed session, using Le Guin’s favourite examples of lively, well-paced, beautiful prose as a springboard for your own creative work.

Title: Elmer with Mama G and Marysia Milewski
Teaser: When ice starts to melt at the North Pole, a polar bear sets off on an adventure that takes him all the way to Elmer’s jungle! But how will the polar bear get home? Pantomime dame Mama G and illustrator Marysia Milewski share songs, drawings, and a brand-…
Description: When ice starts to melt at the North Pole, a polar bear sets off on an adventure that takes him all the way to Elmer’s jungle! But how will the polar bear get home? Pantomime dame Mama G and illustrator Marysia Milewski share songs, drawings, and a brand-new Elmer story, Elmer and the White Bear, in an inclusive storytime that will inspire the next generation of climate activists.

Title: Tim Key: L.A. Baby!
Teaser: Comedian, writer, actor, and Taskmaster task consultant Tim Key is a sell-out. But the good kind…
Description: Comedian, writer and actor Tim Key is back after a sell-out event with us in 2024. He returns to share L.A. Baby! – his new poetry collection. Created with his long-time design collaborator, Emily Juniper, discover Key’s Hollywood adventures and moments of existential crisis against a backdrop of laundrettes, dive bars, and shoe-scuffed sidewalk stars, as he tries to keep himself sane amongst the unparalleled madness of Tinsel Town.

Title: OU/UKLA Edinburgh Teachers’ Reading Group Launch
Teaser: Interested in developing your practice on Reading for Pleasure? Keen to share ideas with colleagues in a supportive environment? Come along to find out about the OU/UKLA Teachers' Reading Groups (TRG), hear how you can get involved, and get access to a……
Description: Interested in developing your practice on Reading for Pleasure? Keen to share ideas with colleagues in a supportive environment? Come along to find out about the OU/UKLA Teachers' Reading Groups (TRG), hear how you can get involved, and get access to a range of free resources and evidence-based tools. There will be the opportunity to hear from local TRG group leaders and author Nadine Aisha Jassat, as well as the chance to network with other learning professionals.

Title: Fresh Words: Jenny Brown Debut Writers Over 50
Teaser: Be the first to discover the literary stars of the future. In partnership with Scottish Book Trust and other leading talent spotters across the UK, this lively lunchtime event showcases electrifying new voices, so grab your seat before everyone else does…
Description: It's lunchtime, and (hallelujah!) there's no need to doomscroll over a sad desk salad. Be the first to discover the literary stars of the future, instead. In partnership with Scottish Book Trust and other leading talent spotters across the UK, this lively lunchtime event showcases electrifying new voices, so grab your seat before everyone else does. Today, we partner with the Jenny Brown Associates Debut Writers Over 50 Award and are joined by Susan Kemp, Margherita Still, Caroline Grebbell, Jade Mitchell and Robbie MacLeòid.

Title: Opening Gala: Repair
Teaser: Celebrate the opening of this year's Festival in this special Gala event. We'll bring you a kaleidoscope of perspectives and provocations from a diverse line-up of stellar writers including Najwan Darwish, Jenni Fagan, Amitav Ghosh, Rachel Kushner, and…
Description: Celebrate the opening of this year's Festival in this special Gala event. We'll bring you a kaleidoscope of perspectives and provocations from a diverse line-up of stellar writers, including Najwan Darwish, Jenni Fagan, Amitav Ghosh, Rachel Kushner, andRobert Macfarlane, as they each read a newly-commissioned piece of writing, responding to our 2025 theme of Repair. Hosted by Festival director Jenny Niven.

Title: Deborah Baker, Gabriel Gatehouse & Leor Zmigrod: Against Misinformation
Teaser: With the US Capitol attack, the Charlottesville riots, and far-right ideology infiltrating the media, should we - indeed, could we - have seen things coming? Today we interrogate this far-reaching topic with authors Deborah Baker, Gabriel Gatehouse, and…
Description: With the US Capitol attack, the Charlottesville riots, and far-right ideology infiltrating the media, should we - indeed, could we - have seen things coming? In a modernity that often feels like a frightening maelstrom of disinformation, conspiracy theories, and dark impulses, if ever a conversation could be described as urgent - this is it. Today we interrogate this far-reaching topic with authors Deborah Baker (Charlottesville), Gabriel Gatehouse (The Coming Storm), and Leor Zmigrod (The Ideological Brain). Chaired by Maddison Connaughton.

Title: Future Library: Time & Wild Clocks
Teaser: Norway's Future Library is a powerful gesture of hope for a world beyond our lifetime. Every year, for 100 years, an author writes a new book to be placed inside its walls; every text remains unread until 2114…
Description: Time & Wild Clocks invites us to explore the tensions between nature’s rhythms and the human-made constructs of time. At the heart of the conversation is Norway’s Future Library, a century-long artwork that plants ideas for a future none of us will see. Each year, a writer contributes a manuscript to be sealed away until 2114. In a special Book Festival event, artist Katie Paterson, creator of the Future Library, joins writer David Farrier and the yet-to-be-revealed 12th author, who will be announced live at the event, in a conversation moderated by Anne Beate Hovind.

Title: Will Hutton: National Remedies
Teaser: How Britain has gone wrong is a frequent conversational gambit, but it's seldom followed up with concrete solutions. These are just what political economist and former Observer editor­-in-chief, Will Hutton, offers in This Time No Mistakes…
Description: How Britain has gone wrong is a frequent conversational gambit, but it's seldom followed up with concrete solutions. These are just what political economist and former Observer editor­-in-chief, Will Hutton, offers in This Time No Mistakes. Discussing with Yuan Yang the failures of both Left and Right over the last 50 years, Hutton outlines a radical (but achievable) future where capitalism is repurposed and democracy reformed, to create a society that supports us all.

Title: Saba Sams & Alessandra Thom: Exciting New Forms
Teaser: Winner of the BBC National Short Story Award, Saba Sams joins us with Gunk, her pacey debut novel about love, family, and messily complex relationships. Joining her is Alessandra Thom, winner of 2023's Scottish Book Trust New Writers Award. Thom's…
Description: Winner of the BBC National Short Story Award, Saba Sams joins us with Gunk, her pacey debut novel about love, family, and messily complex relationships. Joining her is Alessandra Thom, winner of 2023's Scottish Book Trust New Writers Award. Thom's Edinburgh-set debut, Summer Hours, is a sizzling story of what happens when the lines of friendship are blurred. Sams and Thom sit down to discuss their sparky new novels with Beth Cochrane.

Title: Rachel Kushner & James Rebanks: These Days
Teaser: Sometimes writers share a commonality of genre or style and a passion for one another's work. So it is with James Rebanks (The Place of Tides) and Rachel Kushner (Creation Lake), who come together today to discuss being inspired by their unconventional…
Description: Sometimes writers share a commonality of genre or style. Sometimes they share a passion for one another's work. So it is with James Rebanks (The Place of Tides) and Rachel Kushner (Creation Lake), who come together today to discuss being inspired by their unconventional origins, and the challenges and revelations of writing about contemporary society in the context of what's gone before, in both the US and UK. Chaired by Malachy Tallack.

Title: Arifa Akbar & Dan Richards: Because the Night Belongs to Us
Teaser: Take a journey into the darkness with two authors whose latest books explore the way the nocturnal hours shape us. In Wolf Moon, by Guardian theatre critic and Consumed author Arifa Akbar, and Overnight, by Dan Richards, this hinterland of nightmares and…
Description: Take a journey into the darkness with two authors whose latest books explore the way the nocturnal hours shape us. In Wolf Moon, by Guardian theatre critic and Consumed author Arifa Akbar, and Overnight, by Dan Richards, this hinterland of nightmares and possibility is revealed with a personal touch. Join them as they discuss the hidden working, creative, and personal lives which carry on while the world sleeps. Chaired by Lamorna Ash.

Title: Jean-Baptiste Andrea: Love Lost and Found
Teaser: Recipient of France's most prestigious literary award, Jean-Baptiste Andrea's Watching Over Her is one of the best selling Prix Goncourt winners in the prize's 121-year history and is now being adapted for film. This sweeping novel charts a tumultuous…
Description: Recipient of France's most prestigious literary award, Jean-Baptiste Andrea's Watching Over Her is one of the best selling Prix Goncourt winners in the prize's 121-year history and is now being adapted for film. This sweeping novel charts a tumultuous love story between an impoverished sculptor and wealthy heiress set against the rise of fascism in Italy. Today, he'll discuss the inspiration for this engrossing yet profound 'story of love, friendship, and revenge' with Nicole Abadee.

Title: After Word with Callum Easter
Teaser: Celebrate the final weekend of the festival and the release of Irvine Welsh’s new novel Men in Love with Leith’s own Callum Easter as he brings his soul-punk charisma to the Spiegeltent stage in this special performance, accompanied by his band the…
Description: Celebrate the final weekend of the festival and the release of Irvine Welsh’s new novel Men in Love with Leith’s own Callum Easter. The singer brings his soul-punk charisma to the Spiegeltent stage in this special performance, accompanied by his band The Roulettes. Followed by an uplifting DJ set by Discotia, inspired by Welsh’s new soul and disco album, named after, and accompanying the book.

Title: Yiyun Li: A New Alphabet, A New Vocabulary
Teaser: Yiyun Li is one of our most important authors, whose life has been touched by unthinkable tragedy. In this impactful conversation she'll reflect on finding words to say the difficult things, how grief transforms time, and the power of the verb 'to be'…
Description: How do we coexist with unimaginable loss? Yiyun Li is one of our most important authors, whose life has been touched by unthinkable tragedy. In Things in Nature Merely Grow, she uses her astonishing gifts as a writer to process the suicides of her two teenage sons. In this impactful conversation with Roxani Krystalli she'll reflect on finding words to say the difficult things, how grief transforms time, and the power of the verb 'to be'.

Title: Conn Iggulden: Return to Rome
Teaser: As British Book Award-winner and the first person to top the UK fiction and non-fiction charts at the same time, Conn Iggulden is a superstar of historical writing. Join us today to hear how Iggulden interweaves fiction with fact to create page-turning…
Description: As British Book Award-winner and the first person to top the UK fiction and non-fiction charts at the same time, Conn Iggulden is a superstar of historical writing. Tyrant, his latest novel in the bestselling Nero trilogy, returns to ancient Rome to find newly crowned Emperor Nero defending his position by becoming the most feared ruler in Roman history. Join us today to hear how Iggulden interweaves fiction with fact to create page-turning stories

Title: Irene Revell, Sarah Shin & Alice Vincent: Hearing and Listening, Profoundly
Teaser: Join us for a fascinating event exploring the art and politics of listening. Bodies of Sound, an anthology edited by Irene Revell and Sarah Shin, brings together poets, musicians, and writers to offer new insights into how we listen and hear. Alice……
Description: Join us for a fascinating event exploring the art and politics of listening. Bodies of Sound, an anthology edited by Irene Revell and Sarah Shin, brings together poets, musicians, and writers to offer new insights into how we listen and hear. Alice Vincent's Hark: How Women Listen will open readers' minds to how sound and self interconnect. Together, they'll delve into feminist perspectives on how we perceive, interpret, and understand sound in our noisy world. Chaired by Arusa Qureshi.

Title: Xiaolu Guo: A Whale of a Retelling
Teaser: Writer, artist, and filmmaker Xiaolu Guo is critically acclaimed in every medium she touches. Her novel Call Me Ishmaelle is a bold, playful, gender-swapping retelling of Moby Dick that reinvigorates Melville’s classic…
Description: Writer, artist, and filmmaker Xiaolu Guo is critically acclaimed in every medium she touches. Her novel Call Me Ishmaelle is the most recent incarnation of her astonishingly varied vision and talent – a bold, playful, gender-swapping retelling of Moby Dick that reinvigorates Melville’s classic. She chats today about challenging conventions, our relationship to the natural world, and trying to fit the whole world on a whaling ship. Chaired by Barry Pierce.

Title: Anthony Joseph: Precious and Impossible
Teaser: What a delight to welcome Anthony Joseph – one of our greatest living poets – back to the Festival for 2025, sharing his lyrical, incisive new collection, Precious and Impossible: Selected Poems…
Description: What a delight to welcome Anthony Joseph – one of our greatest living poets – back to the Festival for 2025. Sharing his lyrical, incisive new collection, Precious and Impossible: Selected Poems, the T.S. Eliot Award-winning poet (and novelist, musician, academic, and more besides) chats to Colin Grant about his three-decade-long career and how he believes that poets have become the ‘historians and biographers of people’. Chaired by Colin Grant.

Title: Enter the Escape with Christopher Edge
Teaser: Welcome to The Escape – an epic new world full of puzzles and peril to beat before time runs out…
Description: Welcome to The Escape – an epic new world full of puzzles and peril to beat before time runs out. Join author Christopher Edge on a heart-racing journey as he brings the levels of the game to life with his mind-bendingly brilliant novel, Escape Room: Game Zero. Anything is possible and nothing is as it seems; can you uncover the secrets of The Escape and save the world, before it’s too late?

Title: Close Read: Tender Buttons by Gertrude Stein
Teaser: Today, Francesca Wade, a true authority on the life and works of the mighty Gertrude Stein, excavates fresh new meaning from Stein's collection of experimental poetry, Tender Buttons. Expect meaningful discussion and a deeper understanding of this…
Description: In our popular Close Read series, a leading author guides you through a deep-diving discussion of a classic text or genre that's inspired them. Think of it as an event blending friendly book club vibes with insightful study notes. Today, Francesca Wade, a true authority on the life and works of the mighty Gertrude Stein, excavates fresh new meaning from Stein's collection of experimental poetry, Tender Buttons. Expect meaningful discussion and a deeper understanding of this legendary writer's craft.

Title: Tony Tulathimutte: Loser’s Manifesto
Teaser: Tony Tulathimutte’s Rejection – a National Book Award-longlisted novel-in-stories – is so gratuitously of-the-moment it hurts. Garth Greenwell has called it ‘a book of mad, madcap genius’ – it’s sex and relationships through a prism of identity, memes……
Description: Tony Tulathimutte’s Rejection – a National Book Award-longlisted novel-in-stories – is so gratuitously of-the-moment it hurts. Garth Greenwell has called it ‘a book of mad, madcap genius’ – it’s sex and relationships through a prism of identity, memes, and internet lore. In this boundary-pushing conversation, presented in partnership with the award-winning ESEA Lit Fest, hear Maria Garbutt-Lucero get to grips with Tulathimutte’s audacious mind as he unpacks his hilariously grotesque work.

Title: Orian Brook, Dave O’Brien & Mark Taylor: Is Culture Bad For You?
Teaser: The benefits of culture to health, education and community are championed, but can culture ever do wrong? First published in 2020, academics and creative industry experts Orian Brook, Dave O'Brien and Mark Taylor's Culture is Bad for You breaks down the…
Description: The benefits of culture to health, education and community are championed, but can culture ever do wrong? First published in 2020, academics and creative industry experts Orian Brook, Dave O'Brien and Mark Taylor's Culture is Bad for You breaks down the heated debate around arts work in Britain, its systems of precarity, and the exclusion of women, people of colour, and working-class people. Freshly updated for the post-Covid era, its concerns have only grown more urgent. Chaired by Morvern Cunningham.

Title: Philippe Sands: Bringing Evil to Justice
Teaser: Philippe Sands' career as a leading international lawyer has been complemented by his writing, not least his 2016 Baillie Gifford Prize-winner, East West Street. 38 Landres Street is another fine example of his singular blend of memoir, travelogue…
Description: Philippe Sands' career as a leading international lawyer has been complemented by his writing, not least his 2016 Baillie Gifford Prize-winner, East West Street. 38 Londres Street is another fine example of his singular blend of memoir, travelogue, detective story, and courtroom drama, this time focusing on Sands' experiences working for the prosecution of Chilean dictator Augusto Pinochet and the investigation into an exiled Nazi with ties to Pinochet's regime. Chaired by Gavin Francis.

Title: Gaelic Daleks with Shelagh Campbell
Teaser: If you had to dress up as a Gaelic speaking character for Halloween, which would you pick? 8-year-old Ailig chooses a Dalek from Dr Who. Only… Daleks can’t speak Gaelic, so he goes on a hunt to find the Gaelic word for ‘exterminate’ – will he find one?…
Description: If you had to dress up as a Gaelic speaking character for Halloween, which would you pick? 8-year-old Ailig chooses a Dalek from Dr Who. Only… Daleks can’t speak Gaelic, so he goes on a hunt to find the Gaelic word for ‘exterminate’ – will he find one? Find out with award-winning Gaelic writer Shelagh Campbell, author of Ailig agus an Dalek Gàidhlig, in this lively event celebrating the magic of the Gaelic language.

Title: That's Not My Zoo with Vanessa Woolf
Teaser: Join Dog, T-Rex, Mermaid, Penguin, and lots of That’s Not My… friends for this sensory storytelling adventure for little ones. Led by Usborne’s incredible professional storyteller, Vanessa Woolf, with great songs, bubbles, and more – it will be SO MUCH…
Description: Join Dog, T-Rex, Mermaid, Penguin, and lots of That’s Not My… friends for this sensory storytelling adventure for little ones. Led by Usborne’s incredible professional storyteller, Vanessa Woolf, with great songs, bubbles, and more – it will be SO MUCH fun!

Title: Michelle de Kretser and Linn Ullmann: Creativity in the Messy Gaps
Teaser: Join inventive writers, Michelle de Kretser and Linn Ullmann, discussing their category-defying works that so searingly explore power, womanhood, and memory…
Description: I no longer wanted to write novels that read like novels,’ wrote Theory & Practice author Michelle de Kretser. ‘...I wanted a form that allowed for formlessness and mess. It occurred to me that one way to find that form might be to tell the truth.’ This search for truth using unconventional forms is shared by Linn Ullmann, whose Girl, 1983 is a genre-defying quest through the past. Join these inventive writers  discussing their category-defying works that so searingly explore power, womanhood, and memory. Chaired by Ali Millar.

Title: Food, Friendship, and Fun with Selina Brown and Maxwell A. Oginni
Teaser: The world is full of wonderful rice recipes but how do we know which one reigns supreme? Join Selina Brown as she helps answer this question with a fun interactive event that celebrates friendship, food, and different cultures through her funny new book…
Description: The world is full of wonderful rice recipes but how do we know which one reigns supreme? Join Selina Brown as she helps answer this question with a fun interactive event that celebrates friendship, food, and different cultures through her funny new book, My Rice is Best. Share your ultimate favourite dishes and hear about new cuisines as Selina takes you on a mesme-ricing food journey alongside illustrator Maxwell A Oginni.

Title: Beyond Borders: Women in Conflict
Teaser: The Women in Conflict programme funded by the Scottish Government and run by international dialogue and cultural exchange platform Beyond Borders Scotland - brings together women from all over the world who are working at the frontlines of peace-­making…
Description: The Women in Conflict 1325 Fellowship Programme programme funded by the Scottish Government and run by international dialogue and cultural exchange platform Beyond Borders Scotland in partnership with the University of Edinburgh Law School - brings together women from all over the world who are working at the frontlines of peace-­making and conflict resolution. Today we are joined by Kate Akello, Noor Al-Naser, and Ameya Kilara. Hear some of their remarkable stories, connecting the dots between conflict resolution, climate, and human rights, and explore Scotland's ambitions to bring together organisations involved in peace and reconciliation.

Title: Strike a Chord with the Instrument Library
Teaser: Songwriting is the magical place where poetry and music meet. Join Hannah to learn some chords on the ukulele and write a song together. Instruments will be provided from Edinburgh Libraries – where you can borrow an instrument, just like borrowing a…
Description: Songwriting is the magical place where poetry and music meet. Join Hannah to learn some chords on the ukulele and write a song together. Instruments will be provided from Edinburgh Libraries – where you can borrow an instrument, just like borrowing a book!

Title: Gaelic Bookbug
Teaser: Halò a h-uile duine! Join our friends from Scottish Book Trust for Gaelic songs, rhymes and stories in this special Gaelic Bookbug Session. This session will feature the books included in the Gaelic Bookbug Bags. All welcome, no prior knowledge of Gaelic…
Description: Halò a h-uile duine! Join our friends from Scottish Book Trust for Gaelic songs, rhymes and stories in this special Gaelic Bookbug Session. This session will feature the books included in the Gaelic Bookbug Bags. All welcome, no prior knowledge of Gaelic language necessary!

Title: Meet Supertato
Teaser: Meet everyone’s favourite veggie superhero and join in with some songs, rhymes, and games. Supertato will also be hap-pea to share high fives, cuddles and pose for photos. See you there!…
Description: Supertato is back from fighting off Evil Pea! Meet everyone’s favourite veggie superhero and join in with some songs, rhymes, and games. Supertato will also be hap-pea to share high fives, cuddles and pose for photos. See you there!

Title: Invent a Story with Niall Moorjani
Teaser: Award winning storyteller Niall Moorjani invites you to hear an array of traditional and invented tales, told with joy, kindness, and a huge amount of joining in. Expect dragons, kelpies, heroes, adventures, and much more. Perfect for families…
Description: Award winning storyteller Niall Moorjani invites you to hear an array of traditional and invented tales, told with joy, kindness, and a huge amount of joining in. Expect dragons, kelpies, heroes, adventures, and much more. Perfect for families.

Teaser: In the Children’s Tent today you’ll find Dads Rock with activities to keep your wee ones busy, just drop in between 13:00 and 14:00 to see what’s going on!…
Description: In the Children’s Tent today you’ll find Dads Rock with activities to keep your wee ones busy, just drop in between 13:00 and 14:00 to see what’s going on!

Title: Pop in and Play with Edinburgh for Under Fives
Teaser: The team from Edinburgh for Under Fives is back to entertain little ones with a story and art activity to take home. Drop in any time and all are welcome!…
Description: The team from Edinburgh for Under Fives is back to entertain little ones with a story and art activity to take home. Drop in any time and all are welcome!

Title: Meet Princess with The Unicorn Experience
Teaser: Meet real-life unicorn, Princess, and try some magical crafting!…
Description:
Have you ever wished you could be like Sophia and meet a real-life unicorn? For one afternoon only, step into the magic with Princess the Unicorn and the Unicorn Experience, including the opportunity to leave Princess a wish in her very own Wish Jar.

	Also don't miss out on a special screening of Unicorn Academy: Legendary Summer with unicorn arts, crafts, and activities. It’s going to be magical! Booking separately.

	Princess will be greeting families between 1pm and 2.30pm so make sure you arrive on time and are prepared to queue. Please note that due to unicorn welfare, Princess may need unexpected breaks. If you arrive too late to meet Princess, we suggest leaving her a wish and heading to our special unicorn craft session and screening of Unicorn Academy at 2.45pm.

Title: Unleash your Imagination with Craigmillar Literacy Trust
Teaser: Katie Swann from Craigmillar Literacy Trust invites you to reimagine the world and repair what’s broken – are you in?…
Description: Katie Swann from Craigmillar Literacy Trust invites you to reimagine the world and repair what’s broken – are you in? We’ll share some of our favourite picture books featuring inventors and take part in a colourful activity bringing your creations to life. This fun, hands-on event is for children and their grown-ups to explore, learn, and be creative together.

Title: Sensory Storytelling with Ailie Finlay
Teaser: Join storyteller Ailie Finlay for an inclusive session with sensory stories, art, activities, and games. This is a fun and engaging session for everyone but particularly suitable for children with additional needs and their families and friends…
Description: Join storyteller Ailie Finlay for an inclusive session with sensory stories, art, activities, and games. This is a fun and engaging session for everyone but particularly suitable for children with additional needs and their families and friends.

Title: Teddy Bear Picnic with Simon Radcliffe
Teaser: Roll out your picnic blankets and bring along your furry friends, for a special storytime featuring some well-known and loved bears! Storyteller Simon Radcliffe will share stories, rhymes, and songs in this bear-y fun event, perfect for all the family…
Description: Roll out your picnic blankets and bring along your furry friends, for a special storytime featuring some well-known and loved bears! Storyteller Simon Radcliffe will share stories, rhymes, and songs in this bear-y fun event, perfect for all the family.

Title: Meet Pikachu
Teaser: Pikachu, I choose YOU! Come along and meet everyone’s favourite electric-type Pokémon for a special appearance at the Book Festival. Don’t miss the opportunity to give Pikachu a wave or pose like a Pokémon trainer for a photo!…
Description: Pikachu, I choose YOU! Come along and meet everyone’s favourite electric-type Pokémon for a special appearance at the Book Festival. Don’t miss the opportunity to give Pikachu a wave or pose like a Pokémon trainer for a photo!

Title: Pop in and Play with Cròileagan Dhùn Èideann
Teaser: Would you like to introduce your wee one to Gaelic? Join the playleaders from Cròileagan Dhùn Èideann, Edinburgh’s Gaelic playgroup for 0-5s, to learn some simple Gaelic words and phrases together with your child, through songs, stories, and play. A…
Description: Would you like to introduce your wee one to Gaelic? Join the playleaders from Cròileagan Dhùn Èideann, Edinburgh’s Gaelic playgroup for 0-5s, to learn some simple Gaelic words and phrases together with your child, through songs, stories, and play. A relaxed and fun-filled session; no prior knowledge of Gaelic required.

Title: Bookbug with Edinburgh Libraries
Teaser: Join Edinburgh Libraries for songs, stories, and rhymes in this fun, interactive Bookbug event, part of Scottish Book Trust's Early Years Programme. Then meet Bookbug for cuddles, high-fives, and photos…
Description: Join Edinburgh Libraries for songs, stories, and rhymes in this fun, interactive Bookbug event, part of Scottish Book Trust's Early Years Programme. Then meet Bookbug for cuddles, high-fives, and photos.

Title: Frankenstein Cabaret: It’s Alive!
Teaser: Frankenstein is having its biggest year since 1818, with a reissue with a new introduction by Jenni Fagan, and two Hollywood films reawakening Shelley’s gothic classic and its deeply Scottish roots…
Description: Frankenstein is having its biggest year since 1818, with a reissue featuring a new introduction by Jenni Fagan, and two Hollywood films reawakening Shelley’s gothic classic and its deeply Scottish roots. Tonight, Fagan has stitched together a very-much-alive line-up of writers, musicians, and artists to celebrate, pull apart, and reanimate the ideas, invention, and sheer gothicness of the indelible tale that spawned a thousand other creations. Featuring fabulous host and MC Mystika Glamoor and readings from Jenni Fagan, Ever Dundas & David Bishop, Janette Ayachi, Harry Josephine Giles, and Kirstin Innes.

Title: Mark Haddon: Curious, Different, Human
Teaser: Mark Haddon, who gave us the genre-­defying The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time, has always thought outside the box. That's especially true of his latest collection of stories, Dogs and Monsters: eclectic retellings of Greek myths wherein…
Description: Mark Haddon, who gave us the genre-defying The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time, has always thought outside the box. That's especially true of his latest collection of stories, Dogs and Monsters: eclectic retellings of Greek myths wherein the ancient speaks to the contemporary. In conversation with Chris Power, Haddon asks what it is that makes some stories, myths, and parables persevere (and adapt) across millennia.

Title: Angus Peter Campbell: Rhymes and Reels
Teaser: The worlds of words and music coalesce in this special family affair featuring award-winning poet and novelist Angus Peter Campbell and his daughters, Brìghde, Ciorstaidh, and Steaphanaidh Chaimbeul, all professional musicians. Expect tales drawn from…
Description: The worlds of words and music coalesce in this special family affair featuring award-winning poet and novelist Angus Peter Campbell and his daughters, Brìghde and Ciorstaidh Chaimbeul, all professional musicians. Join Campbell as he presents readings from his works, in both English and Gaelic, interspersed with musical accompaniment from the small pipes, clarsach, accordion, piano, and more. Expect tales drawn from Hebridean mythology and folklore, Scottish history, and magic realism, alongside the sounds of contemporary trad and folk music.

Title: There's a Bear on my Chair with Ross Collins
Teaser: A bear has settled in Mouse’s favourite chair, and that chair isn’t big enough for both of them to share. Come along to this hilarious event hosted by Ross Collins, author-illustrator of There’s a Bear in My Chair and find out all the ways Mouse tries to…
Description: A bear has settled in Mouse’s favourite chair, and that chair isn’t big enough for both of them to share. Come along to this hilarious event hosted by Ross Collins, author-illustrator of There’s a Bear in My Chair and find out all the ways Mouse tries to get the big bear to move. A laugh-out-loud event celebrating the 10th anniversary of this wonderful book.

Title: Repair Cafe Edinburgh
Teaser: Got something that’s broken? Want to try fixing it but not sure how? Repair Cafes are free community events where you can bring your item and volunteer fixers will guide you through your repair…
Description:
Got something that’s broken? Want to try fixing it but not sure how? Repair Cafes are free community events where you can bring your item and volunteer fixers will guide you through your repair.

	Not everything's fixable at our events - we're limited by time, spare parts, safety, capacity.

	If you’ve got something that you want to fix, email us at repaircafeedinburgh@gmail.com to confirm suitability and to reserve your place.

	For more details, visit Repair Cafe.

Title: Amitav Ghosh: The Spaces We Inhabit
Teaser: Best known for his Ibis trilogy, Amitav Ghosh is a colossus of postcolonial literature. Today, the venerated writer joins us to discuss Wild Fictions, an extraordinary collection of his writing from the last 25 years…
Description: Best known for his Ibis trilogy, Amitav Ghosh is a colossus of postcolonial literature. Today, the venerated writer joins us to discuss Wild Fictions, an extraordinary collection of his writing from the last 25 years. Covering a sweeping gamut of urgent and compelling themes relating to the ways in which we understand and interact with our world, this is a conversation not to be missed. Chaired by Bee Rowlatt.

Title: Richard Lloyd Parry & Andrey Kurkov: How to Resist
Teaser: Political fiction helps us to make sense of, interrogate, and criticise the realities of enforced political systems on our daily lives. Today, we meet two eminent authors, Richard Lloyd Parry and Andrey Kurkov, to question - resistance at what cost?…
Description: Political fiction helps us to make sense of, interrogate, and criticise the realities of enforced political systems on our daily lives. The venerable Times foreign correspondent Richard Lloyd Parry brings us the Conrad-esque In the Green Heart; and with The Stolen Heart, one of Ukraine's greatest living writers, Andrey Kurkov, embodies his country's irrepressible spirit of improvisational anarchy. Today, we meet these two eminent authors to question - resistance at what cost? Chaired by Nick Barley.

Title: Open House
Teaser: You're invited to our Open House! Bring your friends and join Festival director Jenny Niven as she takes you through highlights of the Festival…
Description: You're invited to our Open House! Bring your friends and join Festival director Jenny Niven as she takes you through highlights of the Festival: from the themes underpinning the programme and the stories behind our fantastic commissions, to this year's hidden gems. There's so much to take in, so let Niven be your helpful guide across the next two weeks. Join her in conversation with Yassmin Abdel-Magied and Jenny Colgan.

Title: Spark Exhibition
Teaser: Young people from the Alternative School at Spartans Community Foundation are back at the festival for the third year, with their brand-new exhibition, Spark. Our writer in residence Owen Sutcliffe has been working with the young people to spark their…
Description: Young people from the Alternative School at Spartans Community Foundation are back at the festival for the third year, with their brand-new exhibition, Spark. Our writer in residence Owen Sutcliffe has been working with the young people to spark their imaginations, ask big questions and get their creative juices flowing. Join us to see their funny, provocative and sparky creative work.

Title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
Teaser: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Appearing today: Tom Percival…
Description: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Appearing today: Tom Percival.

Title: Rachel Charlton-Dailey: The Ongoing Fight for Disability Rights
Teaser: This year marks 30 years since the Disability Discrimination Act. To mark this significant anniversary, activist Rachel Charlton-Dailey joins Caro Clarke to discuss Ramping Up Rights which brings together inspiring stories of over 100 years of disability…
Description: This year marks 30 years since the Disability Discrimination Act. At the time, this milestone in legislation made it illegal to discriminate against someone because of their disability. To mark this significant anniversary, activist Rachel Charlton-Dailey joins Caro Clarke to discuss Ramping Up Rights which brings together inspiring stories of over 100 years of disability activism.

Title: Derek Thompson: More to Go Around
Teaser: Leading US commentator Derek Thompson is an author, podcaster, and journalist at the Atlantic, and a self-­described progressive. His first book, Hit Makers: How to Succeed in an Age of Distraction was a bestseller, and in Abundance - co-authored with…
Description: Leading US commentator Derek Thompson is an author, podcaster, former journalist at the Atlantic, and a self-­described progressive. His first book, Hit Makers: How to Succeed in an Age of Distraction was a bestseller, and in Abundance - co-authored with New York Times columnist Ezra Klein - he argues that the current method of governance in the US is broken. Today, in conversation with Liz Lloyd, he explains his belief that bolder, more dynamic government can counter the fear-driven politics driven by perceptions of scarcity and ensure there's plenty to go around.

Title: Michelle de Kretser: Beautiful, Radical Ideas
Teaser: Michelle de Kretser’s books smash through all preconceived notions about fiction, blending artful social observation with forms fizzing with brainy playfulness…
Description: Michelle de Kretser’s books smash through all preconceived notions about fiction, blending artful social observation with forms fizzing with brainy playfulness. Today, the Rathbones Folio Prize-winning author of Scary Monsters discusses Theory & Practice: her latest boundary-breaking work that’s part novel, essay, and memoir. Talking with Chitra Ramaswamy, the celebrated Australian writer muses on the antics of critical theory, her creative process of ‘questing, jesting, testing’, and coming to acknowledge the shortcomings of Virginia Woolf.

Title: Empowered Voices with Bea Fitzgerald & Manjeet Mann
Teaser: Celebrating female narratives and the triumphs of women, be prepared to feel empowered and inspired by women's voices in this special panel event with the House of YA…
Description: What does it mean to be a feminist storyteller? Join Manjeet Mann, the award-winning author of The Crossing, and Bea Fitzgerald, the Sunday Times bestselling author of Girl, Goddess, Queen, in conversation with Cynthia Murphy as they discuss their new novels Roar and A Beautiful Evil. Celebrating female narratives and the triumphs of women, be prepared to feel empowered and inspired by women's voices in this special panel event with the House of YA.

Title: Brilliant Little Beasties with Yussef Rafik
Teaser: They may be small, but you’d be surprised how useful bugs and minibeasts are to our planet. They’re just so amazing too – did you know some bugs can lift over 1,000 times their weight? Hear Yussef Rafik share loads of fun bug facts with his latest book…
Description: They may be small, but you’d be surprised how useful bugs and minibeasts are to our planet. They’re just so amazing too – did you know some bugs can lift over 1,000 times their weight? Hear Yussef Rafik share loads of fun bug facts with his latest book, Don’t Squish a Slug, and learn why it’s time we change how we think about beasties – and why we definitely shouldn’t squish them!

Title: Global Ink: Edinburgh International Book Festival’s International Industry Day
Teaser: Discover the Power of International Collaboration at Global Ink…
Description:
Global Ink is the Edinburgh International Book Festival’s flagship industry event, bringing together industry professionals from Scotland, the UK, and around the world. Taking place on Tuesday 12 August, it’s a must-attend for authors, publishers, translators, festival organisers, and anyone passionate about working across borders. Join us for an afternoon of bold ideas and global perspectives, with two thought-provoking panel discussions featuring leading international figures from across the literary world. Afterwards, continue the conversation at our Global Ink Social – a relaxed networking reception where you can enjoy a drink, connect with peers, and celebrate the spirit of international collaboration.

	Programme

	14:30 – 15:00
	Registration

	Arrive, check in, and start making early connections with fellow attendees before the first session.

	


	15:00 – 16:00

	Panel One: Books That Travel

	In partnership with Publishing Scotland
	What’s selling across global markets—and how can UK publishers and curators tap into it? Join a powerhouse panel of international publishers from Europe to North America to explore what’s working in translation, which genres are trending, and how decisions are made about what crosses borders. With a particular focus on how Scottish books are being sold, marketed, and received abroad, the session offers vital insight into the export potential of Scottish and UK voices, and what makes a title resonate internationally. A timely, focused discussion for anyone programming, writing, publishing, or promoting books beyond their home market.

	Chaired by: 
	James Crawford (Scotland), Chair, Edinburgh International Book Festival 

	Speakers: 
	• Andrea Morstabilini (Italy), Writer and Foreign Non-Fiction Editor, Iperborea 
	• Julia Eisele (Germany), Founder and Publisher, Eisele Verlag 
	• Iris Tupholme (Canada), Senior Vice-President and Executive Publisher, HarperCollins Canada

	


	16:00 – 16:30
	Break – Time to Connect

	Take time to recharge and reflect on the first session. This is a key opportunity to network, share contact details, and continue the conversation over light refreshments - tea and coffee will be available.

	


	16:30–17:30

	Panel Two: Born Digital – Web Novels and the Global Reading Revolution

	Once considered niche, web novels have become a global cultural force—redefining how stories are written, shared, and consumed. First popularised in East Asia, particularly China, South Korea, and Japan, these digital-first narratives are transforming the publishing and storytelling landscape, spawning new genres, and serving as inspiration for blockbuster film, TV, and gaming adaptations.

	Join this timely discussion exploring the rise of web-first storytelling and what it reveals about the future of reading and publishing. How are new technologies, platforms, and fan communities changing the rules of literary success? And what might traditional publishers, editors, and writers learn from this dynamic space?

	Chaired by:
	Alastair Horne, Lecturer in Publishing Studies, University of Stirling

	Speakers:
	• Vicky Wei, Representative of Beijing International Book Fair
	• Seunghye Sun, Ph.D. FRSA, Director, Korean Cultural Centre UK

	


	17:30 – 18:15
	Break & Room Reset

	Take a short break and continue conversations informally elsewhere while we reset the room for the evening reception.

	


	18:15–20:00

	Global Ink Social – International Networking Reception
	Venue: The Lounge (Room 2.55), Level 2

	Conclude the day with our Global Ink Social, a relaxed gathering to reflect on the day’s insights and network with fellow attendees over drinks and canapés.

Title: Gabriel Gatehouse: The Conspiracy That Could Bring Down Democracy
Teaser: Conspiracy theories are a scourge of online life, but how have they been weaponised to distort reality for political gain? BBC Newsnight’s former international editor, Gabriel Gatehouse, talks to Festival director Jenny Niven about the threat technology…
Description: Conspiracy theories are a scourge of online life, but how have they been weaponised to distort reality for political gain? BBC Newsnight’s former international editor, Gabriel Gatehouse, was shortlisted for the Orwell Prize for Journalism and won a Broadcasting Press Guild award for his The Coming Storm podcast, which goes down the rabbit hole of conspiracies upending US politics, and became a vital book. He talks to Festival director Jenny Niven about the threat technology poses to democracy itself.

Title: Aja Barber, Alena Ivanova & Anna Freemantle-Zee: Wear and Repair
Teaser: We all know to shop second-hand, avoid microplastic fibres, and celebrate re-wearing – but is this enough to make fashion sustainable? How much power do we really have as consumers? Today Aja Barber (author of Consumed), Anna Freemantle-Zee (founder of……
Description: We all know to shop second-hand, avoid microplastic fibres, and celebrate re-wearing – but is this enough to make fashion sustainable? How much power do we really have as consumers? Today Aja Barber (author of Consumed), Anna Freemantle-Zee (founder of Edinburgh International Fashion Festival and Regenerative Textiles Scotland), and Alena Ivanova (campaigns and activism lead at Labour Behind the Label) gather for a hopeful but frank discussion on the global fast fashion and overproduction crises, exploring a range of possible solutions. Chaired by Ruth MacGilp.

Title: Esther García Llovet & Rosa Ribas: Queens of Spanish Noir
Teaser: Join two of Spain’s most exciting contemporary writers to discover how, even in the blazing Spanish sun, they’ve found dark corners for secrets to lurk within…
Description: Esther García Llovet’s Spanish Beauty follows a magnetic police officer – born of an English gangster father and flamenco dancing mother – with a rather unorthodox relationship to the law. And in Far, Rosa Ribas tells the atmospheric story of two conflicting communities living within, and creeping towards, an unfinished luxury living development. Join two of Spain’s most exciting contemporary writers to discover how, even in the blazing Spanish sun, they’ve found dark corners for secrets to lurk within. Chaired by Anna Bogutskaya.

Title: Mini Dragon Mayhem with George Webster
Teaser: From much-loved CBeebies star, George Webster, comes a rip-snorting series in George and the Mini Dragon, full of fun, adventure and dragon mayhem!…
Description: When George wishes for a pet dragon, the last thing he expects is for one to appear at the end of the garden. Now he must conceal its antics at school and to his parents – but Lava has other ideas! From much-loved CBeebies star, George Webster, comes a rip-snorting series in George and the Mini Dragon, full of fun, adventure and dragon mayhem! This event is delivered in partnership with PAMIS.

Title: Gettin Stairtit wi Writin Scots: A Workshop with Harry Josephine Giles
Teaser: Today, Orcadian poet and novelist Harry Josephine Giles (Deep Wheel Orcadia and Them!) leads a series of exercises for folk looking for a way into working with Scots…
Description: In all its glorious forms, Scots is a rich and descriptive language - how can you make it your own? Today, Orcadian poet and novelist Harry Josephine Giles (Deep Wheel Orcadia and Them!) leads a series of exercises for folk looking for a way into working with Scots. Join in to open up the language, play games, learn words, and discover Scots anew. Suitable for anyone with a healthy beginner's mindset.

Title: Donna Ashworth: An Ode to Women
Teaser: Daughters, lovers, sisters, friends - relationships take many forms, but perhaps most important are the ones women have with themselves. To the Women is the latest inspirational poetry collection from Donna Ashworth, a writer who took the internet by…
Description: Daughters, lovers, sisters, friends - relationships take many forms, but perhaps most important are the ones women have with themselves. To the Women is the latest inspirational poetry collection from Donna Ashworth, a writer who took the internet by storm back in 2020 when her poem 'History Will Remember When the World Stopped' went viral. She joins Sam Baker, talking about her project to celebrate the power, strength, and passion of women.

Title: Gabriela Cabezón Cámara & Xiaolu Guo: Revisionist Reinventions
Teaser: Acclaimed author and filmmaker Xiaolu Guo joins International Booker Prize-shortlisted Gabriela Cabezón Cámara for an entrancing event exploring gender-blending historical narratives…
Description: Acclaimed author and filmmaker Xiaolu Guo joins International Booker Prize-shortlisted Gabriela Cabezón Cámara for an entrancing event exploring gender-blending historical narratives. Guo’s Call Me Ishmaelle reimagines Moby Dick narrated by a cross-dressing female sailor, while Cabezón Cámara’s We Are Green and Trembling fictionalises the life of Antonio de Erauso, a trans man associated with the Spanish conquest of South America. They’ll discuss identity, transformation, and subverting stories to shift perspectives with Sasha de Buyl.

Title: YA Book Prize 2025: Award Ceremony
Teaser: Exciting news! We’re collaborating with magazine The Bookseller again to host 2025’s YA Book Prize award ceremony. Come along to discover the best Young Adult fiction coming from the UK and Ireland right now. Hosted by Laura Bates…
Description: Exciting news! We’re collaborating with magazine The Bookseller again to host 2025’s YA Book Prize award ceremony. Come along to discover the best Young Adult fiction coming from the UK and Ireland right now. Previous winners include Lex Croucher with Gwen and Art Are Not in Love (2024), Danielle Jawando with When Our Worlds Collided (2023), and Alice Oseman with Loveless (2021). Hear this year’s shortlisted authors read from their books before one of them is crowned winner. Hosted by Laura Bates.

Title: ReaderBank: Unlocking the Mind and Mental Health
Teaser: ReaderBank is an ambitious attempt to create the world's largest study of reading, imagination, and mental health.A collaboration between our Festival and researchers from Durham University, ReaderBank returns with new insights about what happens when we…
Description: ReaderBank is an ambitious attempt to create the world's largest study of reading, imagination, and mental health. A collaboration between our Festival and researchers from Durham University, ReaderBank returns with new insights about what happens when we read. Join lead researcher Ben Alderson-Day for a workshop focused on the findings so far, what they tell us about the science of the imagination, and how reading unlocks new frontiers for mental health, psychological therapy, and neurodiversity.

Title: Ewan Morrison: Digital Immortality
Teaser: Scottish Book of the Year-winner Ewan Morrison brings his latest high concept techno-thriller to this year’s Festival…
Description: Scottish Book of the Year-winner Ewan Morrison brings his latest high concept techno-thriller to this year’s Festival. For Emma is a ghost in the machine tale of bereavement that dives headfirst into the complicated love between a daughter and her father. Morrison joins us to discuss this pacy new novel that asks readers to consider essential questions about the acceleration of technology, AI, resistance, and what it is to be human. Chaired by Georgina Godwin.

Title: Natasha Brown & Hari Kunzru: Fiction for a Fractured World
Teaser: Come along for a compelling discussion between two incisive minds on the complex power dynamics in our rapidly changing world…
Description: Natasha Brown and Hari Kunzru certainly don't shy away from the creeping anxiety of our times in their latest books. In Universality and Blue Ruin, they each grapple with big ideas about beauty, power, and capitalism and, today, they join Chitra Ramaswamy to unpack these themes. Come along for a compelling discussion between two incisive minds on the complex power dynamics in our rapidly changing world.

Title: An Evening with David Olusoga
Teaser: The chronicler of often overlooked or understudied areas of British history, David Olusoga tonight shares the highlights and challenges not just from his impressive career, but his own personal story…
Description: David Olusoga is an author, broadcaster, and one of Britain’s best known and well-loved historians. Born in Lagos in Nigeria, Olusoga grew up in Gateshead, where his family were one of very few non-white residents, until racism and attacks from the National Front forced them to leave the area. As a writer, his titles include Black and British: A Forgotten History, and Black History for Every Day of the Year. He has also presented acclaimed BBC series including Britain’s Forgotten Slave Owners, A House Through Time, Our NHS: A Hidden History, and Union with David Olusoga. The chronicler of often overlooked or understudied areas of British history, Olusoga tonight shares the highlights and challenges not just from his impressive career, but his own personal story. Chaired by Allan Little.

Title: Under the London Sky with Anna Woltz & Michele Hutchison
Teaser: London, September 1940. Deep in the tunnels of the Underground, hidden from the bombs, four teenagers meet. Brought together by the Blitz and telling their story of strength and survival comes the exclusive launch of Under the London Sky: a thrilling new…
Description: London, September 1940. Deep in the tunnels of the Underground, hidden from the bombs, four teenagers meet. Brought together by the Blitz and telling their story of strength and survival comes the exclusive launch of Under the London Sky: a thrilling new historical adventure from bestselling author Anna Woltz and translator Michele Hutchison. Prepare to be moved by the unwavering bond of friends navigating a key moment in our history as Anna and Michele take you on a journey back in time.

Title: Michael Amherst & John Patrick McHugh: Growing Up
Teaser: There are as many boyhoods and young-­man-hoods as there are boys and young men, each distinct and complex; today we meet the chroniclers of two. Expect discussion of alternative masculinities of sensitivity, honesty, and frailty…
Description: There are as many boyhoods and young­man-hoods as there are boys and young men, each distinct and complex; today we meet the chroniclers of two. With the quietly devastating The Boyhood of Cain, Michael Amherst charts the first painful rite of passage: from boy to adolescent. And with the darkly comic Fun and Games, John Patrick McHugh charts the second: from adolescence to manhood. Expect discussion of alternative masculinities of sensitivity, honesty, and frailty. Chaired by Michael Lee Richardson.

Title: Learn to Write Good: A Workshop with Dominic Hoey
Teaser: Bestselling New Zealand novelist Dominic Hoey leads an accessible introduction to the craft of storytelling today. This workshop is open to everyone — no previous writing experience needed…
Description: Bestselling New Zealand novelist Dominic Hoey (Poor People with Money) leads an accessible introduction to the craft of storytelling today. Through practical exercises and real-world examples, Hoey guides you through the building blocks of writing compelling prose. This workshop is open to everyone — no previous writing experience needed. Whether you're just starting out or coming back to the page after a break, you’ll gain new tools, fresh ideas, and a better understanding of how to shape your stories.

Title: Writing Fantasy: A Workshop with Catherine Prasifka
Teaser: When you write fantasy, you open yourself up to the idea that anything could happen. This workshop with author Catherine Prasifka will outline different approaches to fantasy writing, covering plot structure, world building, and what happens when things…
Description: When you write fantasy, you open yourself up to the idea that anything could happen. More than a genre, it’s a way of approaching storytelling by asking, ‘what if?’ – it has the power to take the reader to places they never could have imagined. This workshop with author Catherine Prasifka (This Is How You Remember It) will outline different approaches to fantasy writing, covering plot structure, world building, and what happens when things start to get weird.

Title: Dream Big with Rob Biddulph
Teaser: What do you want to be when you grow up? Explore all the things you can be with amazing author and illustrator Rob Biddulph in his newest book, When I Grow Up I’d Like to Be……
Description: Join bestselling and multi award-winning author and illustrator Rob Biddulph for a fun packed event for all the family. Rob will bring to life his award-winning books, including his brand-new picture book When I Grow Up I'd Like to Be... and the latest in his Draw With Rob series: Fantastic Food! And of course, there will be a chance to join in live with his draw-along. Pencils at the ready!

Title: Daisy Buchanan & Hattie Crisell: Shelf-Help
Teaser: Hit podcasters Daisy Buchanan and Hattie Crisell bring us two must-read books shining a light on the wonderful world of reading and creativity. In this brilliantly bookish event, the authors share some of the wise, funny, and reassuring insights their…
Description: Hit podcasters Daisy Buchanan and Hattie Crisell bring us two must-read books shining a light on the wonderful world of reading and creativity. Crissell's In Writing is a perceptive and smart insider's guide to the creative process, while Buchanan's Read Yourself Happy is a thoughtful handbook for alleviating anxiety through reading. In this brilliantly bookish event, the authors share some of the wise, funny, and reassuring insights their volumes contain with Lee Randall.

Title: Drawing Elmer with Marysia Milewski
Teaser: Colouring-in pencils at the ready as Marysia Milewski takes you through an illustration workshop based on everyone’s favourite patchwork elephant: Elmer…
Description: Colouring-in pencils at the ready as Marysia Milewski takes you through an illustration workshop based on everyone’s favourite patchwork elephant: Elmer. Marysia is the illustrator of the new book, Elmer and the White Bear, written by her friend, the late David McKee. In it, Elmer meets a mysterious bear whose home has started to melt. Come and create, draw, and explore how we can protect the planet in this interactive event.

Title: Stories and Scran
Teaser: Stories and Scran celebrates the dynamic and thought-provoking work created by communities across Edinburgh and beyond. Expect diverse and creative talent from the Book Festival’s own Adults Writing Group and Citizen Collective, plus a special……
Description: Stories and Scran celebrates the dynamic and thought-provoking work created by communities across Edinburgh and beyond. Expect diverse and creative talent from the Book Festival’s own Adults Writing Group and Citizen Collective, plus a special performance from Dance Base’s Prime Elders Dance Company. And Scran Academy are back to serve up a delicious, sweet treat you can enjoy during the event.

Title: Elisa Levi & Sara Mesa: Spain’s New Literary Horizons
Teaser: Discover two bold new voices from Spain, recently published in English for the first time. Writing in the tradition of the Spanish literary greats, Elisa Levi and Sara Mesa’s fiction blend themes of belonging, coming of age, power dynamics, and rural…
Description: Discover two bold new voices from Spain, recently published in English for the first time. Writing in the tradition of the Spanish literary greats, Elisa Levi and Sara Mesa’s fiction blend themes of belonging, coming of age, power dynamics, and rural isolation. This fascinating discussion will explore Levi’s That’s All I Know, and Mesa’s Un Amor and Four by Four, three novels of sensational talent and unapologetic vitality. Chaired by Lilidh Kendrick.

Title: Emma Healey & Charlotte Runcie: The Sweet Taste of Revenge
Teaser: They say revenge is a dish best served cold, but does it really make us feel better? Is getting our own back on the person who scorned us the best way to get even? Obsession, toxic-love, and power dynamics are at the core of both Sweat by Emma Healey…
Description: They say revenge is a dish best served cold, but does it really make us feel better? Is getting our own back on the person who scorned us the best way to get even? Obsession, toxic-love, and power dynamics are at the core of both Sweat by Emma Healey (also author of modern classic Elizabeth is Missing), and Charlotte Runcie's debut novel, Bring the House Down. Join them today for this thrilling event. Chaired by Casi Dylan.

Title: Our Mother Tongues
Teaser: To celebrate his inaugural year as Makar, Peter Mackay brings together poets working in Scotland today who showcase the range of languages being spoken and written in across the country…
Description: To celebrate his inaugural year as Makar, Peter Mackay brings together poets working in Scotland today who showcase the range of languages being spoken and written in across the country. From English to Gaelic and from Polish to Arabic (and beyond!), this special event will weave together a tapestry of multi-language poetry, featuring performances from: Colin Bramwell, Roshni Gallagher, Niall O'Gallagher, Andres N Ordorica, Anne Pia, and Gabriela Milkova Robins.

Title: History's Most Epic Fails with Athena Kugblenu
Teaser: History’s full of daring deeds, mighty heroes, and incredible inventions. But it’s also full of huge FAILS! Discover the truths behind the world’s biggest howlers with comedian and CBBC Horrible Histories writer, Athena Kugblenu, author of History’s Most…
Description: History’s full of daring deeds, mighty heroes, and incredible inventions. But it’s also full of huge FAILS! Discover the truths behind the world’s biggest howlers with comedian and CBBC Horrible Histories writer, Athena Kugblenu, author of History’s Most Epic Fails. Whether it’s silly mishaps that changed the course of history or mistakes that did us all a favour, Athena will take you on a riotous ride through history.

Title: Wear the Crown with Lauryn Hamilton Murray & A B Poranek
Teaser: Prepare to be enchanted with debut author Lauryn Hamilton Murray and the bestselling author of Where the Dark Stands Still, A B Poranek…
Description: Prepare to be enchanted with debut author Lauryn Hamilton Murray and the bestselling author of Where the Dark Stands Still, A B Poranek, as they share their dazzling new YA novels, Heir of Storms and A Treachery of Swans in conversation with Katja Kaine. Bound to be your new romantasy obsession, featuring slow burn sapphic pining to elemental magic and brought to you specially by the House of YA – it’s going to be electrifying!

Title: How It All Works with Maddie Moate
Teaser: Ever wondered what happens behind a dishwasher door, why a duvet keeps you warm, or how x-rays take pictures of our bones? To celebrate the release of her new book, How Does It Work?, BAFTA-winning children’s TV presenter, YouTuber, and author Maddie…
Description: Ever wondered what happens behind a dishwasher door, why a duvet keeps you warm, or how x-rays take pictures of our bones? To celebrate the release of her new book, How Does It Work?, BAFTA-winning children’s TV presenter, YouTuber, and author Maddie Moate invites you to explore the workings of everyday objects in an event that will leave you itching to find out more about how the things around you actually work.

Title: Coorie Doon with Jackie Kay and Jill Calder
Teaser: Coorie in for an empowering event celebrating the melodies we carry with us throughout our lives…
Description: Coorie in for an empowering event celebrating the melodies we carry with us throughout our lives. Acclaimed poet and former Makar of Scotland, Jackie Kay, and renowned Scottish artist, Jill Calder, share their beautiful book, Coorie Doon. Legendary folk singer Claire Brown will be joining to sing songs that feature in the story. A marvellous medley of song, Scots and storytelling... Wee and big bairns alike will be invited to draw their memories and hopes for the future and share some songs together. Dinna fash – it’s sure to be braw!

Title: John MacKay: A Life in the News
Teaser: One of Scotland's most recognisable broadcasters, John MacKay celebrated his 30th anniversary with STV in 2024. He joins us today, with his memoir Scotland Today and Yesterday - republished in an updated version to celebrate the occasion…
Description: One of Scotland's most recognisable broadcasters, John MacKay celebrated his 30th anniversary with STV in 2024. He joins us today, with his memoir, Scotland Today and Yesterday - republished in an updated version to celebrate the occasion. Hear MacKay cast a definitive, first-hand eye over the changes and big news stories he's covered, and reflect on an illustrious career both in and beyond journalism. Chaired by Shereen Nanjiani.

Title: Julian Clary: Behind the Curtain
Teaser: The inimitable Julian Clary is a bona fide British national treasure - an actor, comedian, presenter, and writer for adults and kids, he can truly do it all. Today he joins us with his latest mystery romp, Curtain Call to Murder, set during a show at the…
Description: The inimitable Julian Clary is a bona fide British national treasure - an actor, comedian, presenter, and writer for adults and kids, he can truly do it all. Today he joins us with his latest mystery romp, Curtain Call to Murder, set during a show at the London Palladium. No stranger to theatre, hear how Clary channelled his dramatic experience into his writing alongside his fabulously vicious wit. Chaired by Susan Calman.

Title: Suzanne O'Sullivan: The Age of Diagnosis
Teaser: In her gripping book, The Age of Diagnosis, leading neurologist Suzanne O’Sullivan explores the increasingly blurry boundaries between sickness and health…
Description: With powerful search engines at our fingertips, it’s never been easier to access medical advice – and potentially dangerous misinformation. In her gripping book, The Age of Diagnosis, leading neurologist Suzanne O’Sullivan explores the increasingly blurry boundaries between sickness and health. This will be a vital exploration of how to begin to navigate it all, in conversation with Gavin Francis.

Title: Thought Exercise: Danny Dorling
Teaser: Dig deeper with our Thought Exercise series. Hear from experts on urgent issues of our time, then join in on the discussion during a wide-ranging, interactive exchange. Today's guest is Danny Dorling, professor of Human Geography and author of Seven…
Description: Dig deeper with our Thought Exercise series. Hear from experts on urgent issues of our time, then join in on the discussion during a wide-ranging, interactive exchange.
