Today's guest is Danny Dorling, professor of Human Geography and author of Seven Children, an eye-opening investigation into childhood inequality in post-pandemic Britain, and The Next Crisis, unpacking polling data to reveal our global crises are often very different from what's in the headlines. Together, discuss how we might reverse the trends that so concern us all. Chaired by Susan Murray.

Title: Olga Wojtas: Never Underestimate a Librarian
Teaser: Described in The Scotsman as having 'Jane Austen stylings and Stella Gibbons satirical wit', we're thrilled that Olga Wojtas is returning to the Festival…
Description: Described in the Scotsman as having 'Jane Austen stylings and Stella Gibbons satirical wit', we're thrilled that Olga Wojtas is returning to the Festival. In this fifth instalment of her beloved Shona McMonagle series, Miss Blaine's Prefect and the Uncharted Island, our favourite librarian is spinning off to a remote island in the Baltic Sea during the 15th century. Join us for an adventurous event as Wojtas chats pirates, Krakens, and other magical monsters. Chaired by Susan Mansfield.

Title: The Big Draw-Off with Chanté Timothy and Jim Smith
Teaser: On your marks, get set, draw! Brace yourself for a Draw-Off with author illustrator Chanté Timothy and Jim Smith as they head-to-head in this epic interactive event…
Description: On your marks, get set, draw! Brace yourself for a draw-off with author-illustrators Chanté Timothy and Jim Smith as they head-to-head in this epic interactive event. Hear about Chanté’s new novel Supa Nova, featuring the adventures of genius kid Nova and Jim Smith’s latest book about all kinds of viruses in Genuis Kid Goes Viral. Then sit back and enjoy the drawing battle of a lifetime, one genius against another – who will reign victorious?

Title: Anna Bogutskaya, Nicholas Jubber & Stuart McHardy: Monstrous Mythologies
Teaser: Even in a world of apps, Al, and the metaverse, humans still are drawn to the dark underbelly of our collective imagination, through folklore, myth, and monsters. Join Anna Bogutskaya, Nicholas Jobber, and Stuart McHardy as they unravel the stories…
Description: Even in a world of apps, Al, and the metaverse, humans still are drawn to the dark underbelly of our collective imagination, through folklore, myth, and monsters. Anna Bogutskaya (Feeding the Monster), Nicholas Jobber (Monsterland), and Stuart McHardy (Scotland's Sacred Goddess) each mine their fields of film, folklore, and history to examine why. Join them as they unravel the stories, beliefs, and trends that shape our obsession with the uncanny and extraordinary. Chaired by Ann Landmann.

Title: Marcus du Sautoy: Creativity by Numbers
Teaser: Some brains are creative while others are more inclined towards mathematics and logic, and the two shall never overlap - right? Wrong, according to mathematician, broadcaster, and prolific author Marcus du Santoy, whose new book, Blueprints, investigates…
Description: Some brains are creative while others are more inclined towards mathematics and logic, and the two shall never overlap - right? Wrong, according to mathematician, broadcaster, and prolific author Marcus du Santoy, whose new book, Blueprints, investigates the mathematical concepts underpinning everything from painting and poetry to the music of Mozart and the defining contemporary architecture of Zaha Hadid. Join him today as he discusses new ways of understanding creativity. Chaired by Suzy Glass.

Title: Thriller Night with Benjamin Dean, Ravena Guron & Busayo Matuluko
Teaser: What do a sleepy hometown, a student party house, and a wedding have in common? They’re all the perfect setting for twisted murder mysteries!…
Description: What do a sleepy hometown, a student party house, and a wedding have in common? They’re all the perfect setting for twisted murder mysteries! Join bestselling authors Benjamin Dean (Bury Your Friends), Ravena Guron (Mondays Are Murder), and Busayo Matuluko (‘Til Death) as they discuss their deadly new YA thrillers today. How do they come up with their twisty tales (and how do they sleep at night)? Chaired by Selina Brown.

Title: Island Hopping with Yuval Zommer
Teaser: Calling all young explorers and budding environmentalists! Join incredible author-illustrator Yuval Zommer and come face-to-face with awesome creatures from giant tortoises to leaping lemurs…
Description: Calling all young explorers and budding environmentalists! Join incredible author-illustrator Yuval Zommer and come face-to-face with awesome creatures from giant tortoises to leaping lemurs. Through Yuval’s newest book, Our Islands, you’ll visit wonders of the world – both natural and man-made – and take a breathtaking tour of our planet’s most remarkable islands. There will be the opportunity to flex your creative skills and learn lots along the way.

Title: Writing Sex: A Workshop with Jeremy Atherton Lin
Teaser: Join author Jeremy Atherton Lin to explore how we can express authentic intimacy on the page. How can we depict sex as meaningful, even political – and sometimes pretty funny?…
Description: Join author Jeremy Atherton Lin (described in the New York Times as having ‘a five-octave, Mariah Carey-esque range for discussing gay sex’) to explore how we can express authentic intimacy on the page. How can we depict sex as meaningful, even political – and sometimes pretty funny? Can we honour, not exploit, our lovers? Atherton Lin will share novels and memoirs that have inspired his own work, and hone in on the craft of the close encounter. Participants of all gender identities and sexual orientations welcome.

Title: You're Invited to Acorn Wood!
Teaser: It’s time for a dance in Acorn Wood! Join Hare and all her friends for a party to remember as we celebrate 25 years of the beloved interactive board book series by iconic duo, author Julia Donaldson and illustrator Axel Scheffler…
Description: It’s time for a dance in Acorn Wood! Join Hare and all her friends for a party to remember as we celebrate 25 years of the beloved interactive board book series by iconic duo, author Julia Donaldson and illustrator Axel Scheffler. There will be fun with stories, rhymes, and songs – and maybe even a visit from Postman Bear.

Title: Becky Manawatu: Family Drama
Teaser: In 2022, Aotearoa-New Zealand author Becky Manawatu broke through with her international bestselling debut novel, Aue, a multi-perspective exploration of a family’s relationship with violence and grief…
Description: In 2022, Aotearoa-New Zealand author Becky Manawatu broke through with her international bestselling debut novel, Aue, a multi-perspective exploration of a family’s relationship with violence and grief. Having won the Jann Medlicott Acorn Prize for Fiction, Manawatu continues the story in her powerful sequel Kataraina, and speaks to us today about moving through a past of familial trauma towards the hope presented by a new generation. Chaired by Robyn Marsack.

Title: Michael Mullen & Len Pennie: Sparkling Scottish Poetry
Teaser: Two effervescent new voices in Scots poetry have burst onto the scene in recent years with joyous impact. Join us for a special event exploring two clever new collections and the rude health of the Scottish poetry scene…
Description: Two effervescent new voices in Scots poetry have burst onto the scene in recent years with joyous impact: Sunday Times bestseller Len Pennie and Edwin Morgan Award-winning Michael Mullen. Pennie’s Poyums Annaw and Mullen’s Goonie demonstrate the fun, versatility, and depth possible in contemporary Scots. Join us for a special event exploring two clever new collections and the rude health of the Scottish poetry scene. Chaired by Beth Cochrane.

Title: Anne Sebba: The Woman’s Orchestra of Auschwitz
Teaser: In 1943, 50 women and girls were drafted into an orchestra within the Auschwitz-Birkenau death camp by the same Nazi officers who were killing their families and friends…
Description: In 1943, 50 women and girls were drafted into an orchestra within the Auschwitz-Birkenau death camp by the same Nazi officers who were killing their families and friends. Though the musicians’ participation may have aided their survival, in The Woman’s Orchestra of Auschwitz historian Anne Sebba explores the deep moral complexity and personal impact of offering art to those perpetrating genocide. Hear Sebba talking to James Naughtie about this fascinating, troubling new book.

Title: Ekow Eshun: Meet the Strangers
Teaser: In The Strangers, journalist, broadcaster, and curator Ekow Eshun challenges the public preconception of ‘the Black male as outsider’ with tender, insightful profiles of five fascinating men…
Description: In The Strangers, journalist, broadcaster, and curator Ekow Eshun challenges the public preconception of ‘the Black male as outsider’ with tender, insightful profiles of five fascinating men: 19th century playwright and Shakespearean actor Ira Aldridge, Arctic explorer Matthew Henson, psychiatrist and political philosopher Frantz Fanon, the great activist Malcolm X, and Justin Fashanu – the first openly gay professional footballer. Today, hear Eshun speaking with Colin Grant, unpacking how their lives reveal unseen perspectives on Black art, culture, and history.

Title: Alexis Okeowo: Deep in the Heart of America
Teaser: America has two powerfully competing stories: the home of Liberty which welcomes all, and the isolationist nation which fears difference. Join New Yorker staff writer, PEN Award-winner, and daughter of Nigerian immigrants, Alexis Okeowo, to discuss…
Description: America has two powerfully competing stories: the home of Liberty which welcomes all, and the isolationist nation which fears difference. Join New Yorker staff writer, PEN Award-winner, and daughter of Nigerian immigrants, Alexis Okeowo, to discuss Blessings and Disasters: a surprising, personal journey through the auto plants and Amazon warehouses of her home state, Alabama, where we might better understand both sides of an unseen America which has global importance. Chaired by James West.

Title: Scots Fairytales with Ashley Douglas and Kate Osmond
Teaser: The Lass and The Quine is a fairytale for the modern day, a story that challenges the tales you already know – and it’s all in Scots!…
Description: The Lass and The Quine is a fairytale for the modern day, a story that challenges the tales you already know – and it’s all in Scots! Flex your imagination and writing skills in this fun, creative workshop with author Ashley Douglas and illustrator Kate Osmond. Hear them share the inspiration behind the story, then get ready to write your own Scots poem. Whit ever will ye come up wae?

Title: Samuel Fisher & Will Rees: Illness – Real and Imagined
Teaser: Some of the most gripping Book Festival conversations are those blending fiction and non-fiction. Here, we bring together two writers whose work addresses illness…
Description: Some of the most gripping Book Festival conversations are those blending fiction and non-fiction. Here, we bring together two writers whose work addresses illness. Will Rees’ essay Hypochondria grapples with the phantom malady that preoccupied Kafka, Didion, Sontag, and Melville. Meanwhile, Samuel Fisher’s novel, Migraine, sees London decimated by an epidemic of weather-induced migraines. What would society look like if it were organised around chronic pain? Chaired by Sarah Manavis.

Title: The Women’s Prize for Fiction at 30
Teaser: Over three decades the Women's Prize for Fiction has established itself as one of the greatest celebrations of female creativity in the world. Join us to look back on the prize's pioneering origins, and consider its lasting legacy…
Description: Over three decades the Women's Prize for Fiction has established itself as one of the greatest celebrations of female creativity in the world. Scan your bookshelves and you are guaranteed to spot a former winner, from Barbara Kingsolver to Zadie Smith. Join this year's chair of judges Kit de Waal, author and judge Diana Evans, and two-time longlisted author Laila Lalami as they talk to Sam Baker, and look back on the prize's pioneering origins, and consider its lasting legacy.

Title: Open Book Shared Reading
Teaser: Join Open Book Lead Readers for an informal and relaxed shared reading session…
Description: Join Open Book Lead Readers for an informal and relaxed shared reading session. Each session will explore a chapter from a debut book from this year’s Festival programme. No experience necessary, and all reading materials will be provided on the day

Title: And Midnight Never Come - A Performance
Teaser: Queen of Crime, the iconic Val McDermid, is bringing her forensic gaze to bear on one of the theatre's most enduring mysteries - the death of Christopher Marlowe in Deptford in 1593. A forbidden love story, a double-crossing spy story, or Shakespeare's…
Description: Queen of Crime, the iconic Val McDermid, is bringing her forensic gaze to bear on one of the theatre's most enduring mysteries - the death of Christopher Marlowe in Deptford in 1593. A forbidden love story, a double-crossing spy story, or Shakespeare's inspiration? This special reading of McDermid's playscript is directed by Philip Howard and is presented in partnership with Pitlochry Festival Theatre.

Title: How the Earth Works with Dr Lucia Perez-Diaz
Teaser: Are you a budding scientist, keen to learn more about Planet Earth? Unlock the clues about Earth’s history with writer, illustrator, and scientist Dr Lucia Perez-Diaz, author of How the Earth Works…
Description: Are you a budding scientist, keen to learn more about Planet Earth? Unlock the clues about Earth’s history with writer, illustrator, and scientist Dr Lucia Perez-Diaz, author of How the Earth Works. You’ll learn what our planet was like long ago, how humans are affecting the Earth, and ways we can repair the planet to ensure a bright future.

Title: First Edition: Local News Direct
Teaser: In our First Edition events you can join leading journalists from across the media (and the world) as they discuss the day’s breaking news over a cup of coffee…
Description: Start your day with the facts. High quality, thorough, and trustworthy journalism has never been more important in helping us understand the world as it really is, so in our First Edition events you can join leading journalists from across the media (and the world) as they discuss the day’s breaking news over a cup of coffee. Today we are joined by Rhiannon Davies and Neill McIntosh. Chaired by The Edinburgh Minute's Michael MacLeod.

Title: Mahmoud Muna & Matthew Teller: This Is Gaza
Teaser: Mahmoud Muna and Matthew Teller join us to discuss Daybreak in Gaza, an anthology they have co-edited which illuminates in vivid detail the extraordinary individuals, meaningful places, and incredible richness of a people, culture, and heritage…
Description: Today, Mahmoud Muna and Matthew Teller join us to discuss Daybreak in Gaza, an anthology they have co-edited which illuminates in vivid detail the extraordinary individuals, meaningful places, and incredible richness of a people, culture, and heritage undergoing traumatic devastation. Through vignettes of writers and artists, but also farmers, doctors, students, athletes, shopkeepers, and teachers, Daybreak in Gaza offers unforgettable stories of hope, life, loss, and survival, and of communities determined to resist and prevail. This is Gaza, evoked by the voices of the people of Gaza themselves. Chaired by Selma Dabbagh.

Title: Imani Erriu and Samantha Shannon: The Art of Fantasy
Teaser: Join these talented authors as they reveal to Alwyn Hamilton how they create their remarkable fantasy worlds…
Description: New York Times bestselling author Samantha Shannon returns with the fifth instalment in her epic Bone Season series, The Dark Mirror. In this richly penned fantasy, Paige Mahoney makes a discovery that changes the war between humans and immortal forever. While in Imani Erriui’s cosmic romantasy, Heavenly Bodies, Elara finds herself caught between warring gods playing dangerous games. Join these talented authors as they reveal to Alwyn Hamilton how they create their remarkable fantasy worlds.

Title: Dylan Jones, Miranda Sawyer & Arusa Qureshi: Music Across the Decades
Teaser: It’s been said that writing about music is like dancing about architecture. Yet there are writers who manage to capture something of the feeling of listening, the way it moves and shapes us…
Description: It’s been said that writing about music is like dancing about architecture – it needs to be experienced to be understood. Yet there are writers who manage to capture something of the feeling of listening, the way it moves and shapes us. Today, Dylan Jones (1975), Miranda Sawyer (Uncommon People), and DJ, programmer, and writer Arusa Qureshi (Flip the Script) chat about era-defining artists and songs of the 70s, 90s, and 2000s, and how we might express what music does to us. Chaired by Alistair Braidwood.

Title: Barbara Demick: Separation and Reunion in China
Teaser: Barbara Demick’s international reporting has won the Robert F Kennedy Journalism Award and the Baillie Gifford Prize for Non-Fiction, plus nominations for a National Book Award and Pulitzer Prize…
Description: Barbara Demick’s international reporting has won the Robert F Kennedy Journalism Award and the Baillie Gifford Prize for Non-Fiction, plus nominations for a National Book Award and Pulitzer Prize. Today, she joins us with Daughters of the Bamboo Grove which tells the heartrending story of identical twins – from the forced adoption of one of the girls to their reunion – and opens out to encompass an investigation into China’s infamous former one-child policy. Chaired by Lijia Zhang.

Title: Guadalupe Nettel & Ayşegül Savaş: The Extraordinary Ordinary
Teaser: The art of the story is to say much with less, and today Roxani Krystalli talks to the authors of two perceptive new collections speaking volumes…
Description: The art of the story is to say much with less, and today Roxani Krystalli talks to the authors of two perceptive new collections speaking volumes. Both Guadalupe Nettel’s The Accidentals and Ayşegül Savas’ Long Distance mine contemporary life and relationships to bring us electrifying stories of connection and disconnection, the familiar and the strange. Hear these luminous talents (and friends!) talk about what preoccupies them as writers and their shared eye for precision.

Title: Kirsty Logan: Love Over Time
Teaser: Festival favourite Kirsty Logan is back with another beautiful collection of short stories, No & Other Love Stories, exploring the intricacies and complexities of female desire against a backdrop that spans centuries…
Description:
Age guidance: 18+

	Festival favourite Kirsty Logan is back with another beautiful collection of short stories, No & Other Love Stories, exploring the intricacies and complexities of female desire against a backdrop that spans centuries. From a medieval convent to a 1990s high school, has the way women love and the relationships they find themselves in really changed? Chaired by Rebecca Tamás.

Title: Bee Wilson: The Stories in Our Kitchen
Teaser: Why does a chipped old mug or plate passed on to us by a loved one hold such special appeal? Join Bee Wilson for a heartwarming and inspiring conversation today, central to our Repair theme…
Description: Why does a chipped old mug or plate passed on to us by a loved one hold such special appeal? In her latest book The Heart-Shaped Tin, food writer, historian, and Wall Street Journal columnist Bee Wilson draws on her own and others’ experiences of divorce, dementia, trauma, and loss of home to examine why we find such an emotional connection with our favourite kitchen objects. Join her for a heartwarming and inspiring conversation with Simon Preston, central to our Repair theme.

Title: Something Gorey
Teaser: From Maurice Sendak to Edward Scissorhands, Edward Gorey’s surreal and gothic fingers are all over a particular corner of 20th century art…
Description: From Maurice Sendak to Edward Scissorhands, the late Edward Gorey’s surreal and gothic fingers are all over a particular corner of 20th century art. We celebrate the iconic American illustrator and writer’s centenary with Gregory Hischak – the director of the Edward Gorey House in Massachusetts and author of the forthcoming E is for Edward who will share insights into Gorey. Chaired by Hannah McGill with New Media Scotland.

Title: Ilan Pappé & Avi Shlaim: The Long and the Short of Israel and Palestine
Teaser: Ilan Pappé and Avi Shlaim have decades of experience in analysing Israel and Palestine, and their impact on individuals, the region, and the rest of the world. Expect a progressive and insightful discussion as these fellow 'New Historians' explore the…
Description: Ilan Pappé (A Very Short History of the Israel-Palestine Conflict, Lobbying for Zionism) and Avi Shlaim (Genocide in Gaza: Israel's Long War on Palestine) have decades of experience in analysing Israel and Palestine, and their impact on individuals, the region, and the rest of the world. Expect a progressive and insightful discussion as these fellow 'New Historians' explore the long history of war and the possibility of peace.

Title: Liu Zhenyun: Behind the Mask of Humour
Teaser: This is how Liu Zhenyun, one of China’s finest and most decorated writers, accounts for the humour in his work. Today, he’ll discuss his exquisite analyses of Chinese society with Lijia Zhang…
Description: 'The Chinese attitude towards tragedy is a little unusual: it’s humorous, it’s forgetful. We make it into comedy.’ This is how Liu Zhenyun, one of China’s finest and most decorated writers, accounts for the humour in his work. His acclaimed novels include I Did Not Kill My Husband and Someone to Talk To, each renowned for their cultural and philosophical significance. Chaired by Esther Tyldesley.

Title: Children's Creativity and AI with SCWBI and Chloe Savage
Teaser: Join award-winning illustrator and author Chloë Savage (Library Lion, The Search for the Giant Arctic Jellyfish) in this thought-provoking session exploring the ethics of Artificial Intelligence and how it could be used as a force for good. Discover how……
Description: Join award-winning illustrator and author Chloë Savage (Library Lion, The Search for the Giant Arctic Jellyfish) in this thought-provoking session exploring the ethics of Artificial Intelligence and how it could be used as a force for good. Discover how AI can support the next generation of young creators as opposed to replacing the magic of human imagination. Hosted by Tibo Torelli from the Society of Children's Books Writers and Illustrators.

Title: The Wonderful World of Jacqueline Wilson
Teaser: From Tracey Beaker, Hetty Feather, and now to Daisy, Lily, and Scruff, how does Jacqueline create the characters that fill her many stories? Find out from the beloved author herself as she chats about her remarkable books and life as a writer…
Description: Can you imagine writing 100 books? Jacqueline Wilson doesn’t have to imagine: she’s done just that! In fact, The Seaside Sleepover is book number one-hundred-and-thirty-something. From Tracey Beaker, Hetty Feather, and now to Daisy, Lily, and Scruff, how does Jacqueline create the characters that fill her many stories? Find out from the beloved author herself as she chats about her remarkable books and life as a writer.

Title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
Teaser: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Appearing today: Alastair Chisholm…
Description: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Appearing today: Alastair Chisholm.

Title: Meet Cute
Teaser: A bookish (and platonic!) speed-dating game where you can matchmake a new pal every two minutes by asking them your most pressing questions…
Description: A bookish (and platonic!) speed-dating game where you can matchmake a new pal every two minutes by asking them your most pressing questions.

Title: Vince Cable: Twilight of the West?
Teaser: Former Secretary of State for Business and leader of the Liberal Democrats, the astute economist Vince Cable has settled into life after frontline politics as a prolific author on global affairs and the world economy. Today, he talks to us about…
Description: Former Secretary of State for Business and leader of the Liberal Democrats, the astute economist Vince Cable has settled into life after frontline politics as a prolific author on global affairs and the world economy. Today, he talks to us about Eclipsing the West: China, India and the Forging of a New World, in which he turns his formidable expertise on the superstates mapping out a new economic order. Chaired by Douglas Fraser.

Title: Hamish Hawk: Life in a Scotch Sitting Room, Vol. 0
Teaser: Join local indie songwriter Hamish Hawk in a rare, lyrical homage to Scotland’s pre-eminent poet-eccentric: Ivor Cutler…
Description:
Join local indie songwriter Hamish Hawk in a rare, lyrical homage to Scotland’s pre-eminent poet-eccentric: Ivor Cutler. A celebration of Cutler’s dreich spoken-word masterpiece, Life in a Scotch Sitting Room, Hawk presents new stories and songs inspired by his own childhood home in Edinburgh, alongside unique reworkings of Cutler’s original works. Joined by friends and armed with Cutler’s original harmonium, this performance – a special Book Festival commission – promises an evening of wit, warmth, and words, sure to make fans of the uninitiated. Introduced by Nicola Meighan.

	Note: This performance will also take place on Sunday 17 August at 21:00.

Title: A C Grayling: Disagreeing Agreeably?
Teaser: Sometimes it feels like we can’t talk about anything without further polarising opinions. Join author and philosopher A C Grayling as he seeks the middle-ground in an incendiary debate…
Description: Sometimes it feels like we can’t talk about anything without further polarising opinions. Join author and philosopher A C Grayling as he seeks the middle-ground in an incendiary debate. Drawing from his new book, Discriminations: Making Peace in the Culture Wars, Grayling shares a fresh take on how we might navigate the messy politics of cultural conflict by recognising the nuance between competing rights and interests.

Title: Find Your Super Power with Tracey Baptiste and Dapo Adeola
Teaser: Fly into an empowering event with bestselling author Tracey Baptiste and award-winning illustrator Dapo Adeola as they introduce Super Goat Girl. Find out what makes you super in this funny, heartwarming event full of drawing and finding joy in who you…
Description: It’s hard to fit in when you’re the new kid at superhero school! After all, what kind of superhero doesn’t have a fancy costume or funky cape? Fly into an empowering event with bestselling author Tracey Baptiste and award-winning illustrator Dapo Adeola as they introduce Super Goat Girl. Find out what makes you super in this funny, heartwarming event full of drawing and finding joy in who you are.

Title: In the Spotlight with Elle McNicoll
Teaser: Hear from the brilliant Elle McNicoll as she exclusively launches her latest title Role Model, in a special in-conversation event with us today. Get a sneak peek before anyone else!…
Description: From Festival favourite and author of the beloved award-winning A Kind of Spark, Keedie, and Like a Charm, comes a brand-new story, featuring an authentic neurodivergent voice, about being thrust into the spotlight. Hear from the brilliant Elle McNicoll as she exclusively launches her latest title Role Model, in a special in-conversation event with Aimée Felone. Get a sneak peek before anyone else!

Title: Close Read: The Long Song by Andrea Levy
Teaser: In our popular Close Read series, a leading author guides you through a deep-diving discussion of a classic text or genre that’s inspired them…
Description: In our popular Close Read series, a leading author guides you through a deep-diving discussion of a classic text or genre that’s inspired them. Think of it as an event blending friendly book club vibes with insightful study notes. Today, continuing our celebration of the remarkable author Andrea Levy, Désha Osborne (chancellor’s fellow in English Literature at Edinburgh University) turns her appreciative eye on Levy’s final novel, The Long Song. In partnership with the Andrea Levy Scholarship.

Title: First Edition: We Are Not Numbers
Teaser: Start your day with the facts. Today’s guests include Palestinian journalist Ahmed Alnaouq, co-founder and director of We Are Not Numbers…
Description: Start your day with the facts. High quality, thorough, and trustworthy journalism has never been more important in helping us understand the world as it really is, so in our First Edition events you can join leading journalists from across the media (and the world) as they discuss the day’s breaking news over a cup of coffee. Today’s guests include Palestinian journalist Ahmed Alnaouq, co-founder and director of We Are Not Numbers.

Title: Being Brave with Anu Adebogun
Teaser: Learn to be brave, bold, and audacious as author Anu Adebogun gives you the tools to live your best life…
Description: Learn to be brave, bold, and audacious as author Anu Adebogun gives you the tools to live your best life. Taking extracts from her latest book It’s a Brave Young World: a guide for teenagers on everything from crushes to mental health. Anu will provide valuable life lessons to help repair confidence and promote well-being for everyone navigating the depths of teenagedom.

Title: Spark Exhibition
Teaser: Young people from the Alternative School at Spartans Community Foundation are back at the festival for the third year, with their brand-new exhibition, Spark. Our writer in residence Owen Sutcliffe has been working with the young people to spark their…
Description: Young people from the Alternative School at Spartans Community Foundation are back at the festival for the third year, with their brand-new exhibition, Spark. Our writer in residence Owen Sutcliffe has been working with the young people to spark their imaginations, ask big questions and get their creative juices flowing. Join us to see their funny, provocative and sparky creative work.

Title: Spark Exhibition
Teaser: Young people from the Alternative School at Spartans Community Foundation are back at the festival for the third year, with their brand-new exhibition, Spark. Our writer in residence Owen Sutcliffe has been working with the young people to spark their…
Description: Young people from the Alternative School at Spartans Community Foundation are back at the festival for the third year, with their brand-new exhibition, Spark. Our writer in residence Owen Sutcliffe has been working with the young people to spark their imaginations, ask big questions and get their creative juices flowing. Join us to see their funny, provocative and sparky creative work.

Title: That's Not My Zoo with Vanessa Woolf
Teaser: Join Dog, T-Rex, Mermaid, Penguin, and lots of That’s Not My… friends for this sensory storytelling adventure for little ones. Led by Usborne’s incredible professional storyteller, Vanessa Woolf, with great songs, bubbles, and more – it will be SO MUCH…
Description: Join Dog, T-Rex, Mermaid, Penguin, and lots of That’s Not My… friends for this sensory storytelling adventure for little ones. Led by Usborne’s incredible professional storyteller, Vanessa Woolf, with great songs, bubbles, and more – it will be SO MUCH fun!

Title: Supertato Silliness with Sue Hendra
Teaser: Sue Hendra, co-creator of the bestselling Supertato picture books, returns to celebrate the latest adventures of everyone’s favourite supermarket superhero…
Description: Sue Hendra co-creator of the bestselling Supertato picture books, returns to celebrate the latest adventures of everyone’s favourite supermarket superhero. If you’re looking for fun and giggles galore, this veggie adventure-fest is the family show for you. There will be stories, silliness and everyone will get a chance to make their own veggie super-hero to take home!

Title: James Runcie & Fenella Humphreys: Life After Love, Love After Love
Teaser: After his wife – theatre director and radio producer, Marilyn Imrie – died, author James Runcie wrote the intensely moving memoir, Tell Me Good Things. Runcie offers his poignant reflections on loss, bereavement, memory, and what it means to love again…
Description: After his wife – theatre director and radio producer, Marilyn Imrie – died, author James Runcie wrote the intensely moving memoir, Tell Me Good Things. In this singular and incredibly special event to mark the fifth anniversary of her passing, Runcie offers his poignant reflections on loss, bereavement, memory, and what it means to love again. He’s joined by dazzling violinist Fenella Humphreys, one of Britain’s most versatile musicians, playing an array of Scots, classical, and contemporary music.

Title: Retelling Myths with Nikita Gill: A Workshop Inspired by Hekate
Teaser: Join bestselling poet Nikita Gill for a powerful writing workshop inspired by her new book, Hekate - a fierce retelling in verse of the Greek goddess of witchcraft and necromancy…
Description: Join bestselling poet Nikita Gill for a powerful writing workshop inspired by her new book, Hekate - a fierce retelling in verse of the Greek goddess of witchcraft and necromancy. Explore how myth can be reimagined to tell contemporary stories of power, rage, and transformation. Through guided prompts and creative exercises, Nikita will help you unlock forgotten voices in mythology and craft your own poetic retellings. Whether you're new to writing or experienced, this is your invitation to reclaim ancient stories, and your own. Limited spaces available: book now to begin your mythic journey.

Title: Rowe Irvin, Florence Knapp & Roisín O'Donnell: Places of Refuge
Teaser: We bring together three debut novelists whose new works have grasped the attention of readers and critics alike…
Description: We bring together three debut novelists whose new works have grasped the attention of readers and critics alike. Rowe Irvin (Life Cycle of a Moth), Florence Knapp (The Names), and Roisin O'Donnell (Nesting) each probe the boundaries of what home, family, and control mean. Ultimately they ponder the question: what are humans capable of? Join them for a conversation about the fraught and fragile times they are writing in, about, and around. Chaired by Cailean Steed.

Title: Nick Makoha: Making Myth a Reality
Teaser: 'Like Dante entering hell through a rip in the universe, Makoha enters history.' So wrote the Guardian about Nick Makoha, winner of the Ivan Juritz and Poetry London Prizes. He joins us to discuss how his latest collection was partly inspired by his time……
Description: 'Like Dante entering hell through a rip in the universe, Makoha enters history.' So wrote the Guardian about Nick Makoha, winner of the Ivan Juritz and Poetry London Prizes. He joins us to discuss how his latest collection was partly inspired by his time as poet-in-residence at the ICA in London, the 'exploded' collages of Jean-Michel Basquiat, his own childhood escape from Idi Amin's Uganda, and the myth of lcarus. Chaired by Kevin Williamson.

Title: You're Joking! with the Listies
Teaser: Join comedians The Listies for a high-speed comedy-writing workshop based on This Book Is a Joke, all about making absurd adverts for completely made-up things…
Description: Ever wanted a box of cereal made entirely of toenails? A deodorant for your feelings? Tickets to a zoo of interestingly shaped rocks? Join comedians The Listies for a high-speed comedy-writing workshop based on This Book Is a Joke, all about making absurd adverts for completely made-up things. You’ll become a junior LOL-vertising executive, imagining ridiculous products, writing hilarious slogans, and pitching your creations in the silliest ad breaks ever made.

Title: Simone Seales and Mele Broomes: Dearest
Teaser: Cellist Simone Seales' Dearest (a debut poetry and music album with an accompanying zine) is a reflection on the warmth and nostalgia of first love, drawing on Patricia Highsmith's classic romance, Carol…
Description: Cellist Simone Seales' Dearest (a debut poetry and music album with an accompanying zine) is a reflection on the warmth and nostalgia of queer first love, drawing on Patricia Highsmith's classic romance, Carol. In this special performance, Seales' tender and insightful poetry is read by multidisciplinary artist Mele Broomes while Seales performs on the cello. Chaired by Titilayo Farukuoye.

Title: Words from the Wards: The Exhibition
Teaser: Following the success of the Words from the Wards project, we worked with Edinburgh College of Art students to illustrate the collected stories. Join us to view the stories and illustrations side by side in our new festival gallery…
Description: Last year, through our Words from the Wards project, we asked the people of Edinburgh to share stories about the former Royal Infirmary, to honour the experiences and memories that people connect with the building’s previous life. Following the success of the project, we worked with Edinburgh College of Art students to illustrate the collected stories. Join us to view the stories and illustrations side by side in our new festival gallery.

Title: Sad Ghost Zine Workshop with Lize Meddings
Teaser: In this cosy zine-making workshop, Lize will help you draw original characters to express your feelings, including your very own Sad Ghost…
Description: The world can be a lonely place sometimes, and author-illustrator Lize Meddings is on a mission to make it less so with her Sad Ghost Club comic book community. In this cosy zine-making workshop, Lize will help you draw original characters to express your feelings, including your very own Sad Ghost.

Title: Paul French: Wallis Simpson’s Lost Years in China
Teaser: For her unimpeachable fashion sense, her role in the abdication of her husband, and her shameful connection with Adolf Hitler - fascination with Wallis Simpson continues unabated nearly 40 years after her death. Now, award-winning historian Paul French…
Description: For her unimpeachable fashion sense, her role in the abdication of her husband, and her shameful connection with Adolf Hitler - fascination with Wallis Simpson continues unabated nearly 40 years after her death. Now, discussing Wallis Simpson: Her Lotus Year in 1920s China, award-winning historian Paul French talks about the thrilling experiences which made her in a fractious foreign land among the hustle of 1920s Shanghai and the high chinoiserie of that intriguing era. Chaired by Isabel Hilton.

Title: That's Not My Zoo with Vanessa Woolf
Teaser: Join Dog, T-Rex, Mermaid, Penguin, and lots of That’s Not My… friends for this sensory storytelling adventure for little ones. Led by Usborne’s incredible professional storyteller, Vanessa Woolf, with great songs, bubbles, and more – it will be SO MUCH…
Description: Join Dog, T-Rex, Mermaid, Penguin, and lots of That’s Not My… friends for this sensory storytelling adventure for little ones. Led by Usborne’s incredible professional storyteller, Vanessa Woolf, with great songs, bubbles, and more – it will be SO MUCH fun!

Title: Richard Flanagan: A Question of Consequence
Teaser: 'That it is a masterpiece is without question' is how the Observer described Question 7: Richard Flanagan's 12th book, winner of 2024's Baillie Gifford Prize for Non-Fiction. Today the multitalented author shares with Chris Power how he brought together…
Description: 'That it is a masterpiece is without question' is how the Observer described Question 7: Richard Flanagan's 12th book, winner of 2024's Baillie Gifford Prize for Non-Fiction. Today the multitalented author shares with Chris Power how he brought together seemingly disparate events - including the atomic bomb, H G Wells' affair with Rebecca West, and his own near-death experience - to create a hypnotic blend of memoir and auto-fiction exploring the chain reactions that occur when we make a choice about love.

Title: Karen Downs-Barton: What it Means to Belong
Teaser: Has anywhere sounded more ominous than the 'Home for Crying Children'? Join Karen Downs-Barton, whose playful new poetry collection Minx effortlessly blends forms in a lyrically vivid evocation of a childhood distinctly less ordinary…
Description: Has anywhere sounded more ominous than the 'Home for Crying Children'? Join Karen Downs-Barton, whose playful new poetry collection Minx effortlessly blends forms in a lyrically vivid evocation of a childhood distinctly less ordinary. From a multi-racial Romani background, Downs-Barton explores growing up on the edges of society, and asks where one can really belong if caught between cultures whose traditions don't match. Chaired by Shasta Hanif Ali.

Title: Tessa Hadley: The Cusp of Something
Teaser: Master chronicler of the heart’s hidden desires, Tessa Hadley (author of Late in the Day and After the Funeral) discusses her first novella…
Description: Master chronicler of the heart’s hidden desires, Tessa Hadley (author of Late in the Day and After the Funeral) discusses her first novella. Following two sisters coming of age in post-war Bristol, The Party takes place over a weekend that bristles with yearning. Hear Hadley reflect on the way short-lived encounters can shock and release us into a new phase of life – how do we become who we are? Chaired by Georgina Godwin.

Title: Defying Destiny with Molly X Chang
Teaser: Two kingdoms on the brink of battle. One prophesied empress to unite them…
Description: Two kingdoms on the brink of battle. One prophesied empress to unite them. Inspired by Chinese myth and history, YA superstar Molly X Chang’s epic romantasy, The Nightblood Prince, sees a reckless princess form a close bond with a runaway prince from a rival kingdom who commands an army of vampires. Join Molly as she chats about her newest title which Xiran Jay Zhao has called ‘beautifully written and brimming with defiance’. Chaired by Nikita Gill.

Title: Singing and Stories with Mr Men and Little Miss
Teaser: Join storyteller George in a gentle Mr Men and Little Miss story journey. Perfect for young children, you’ll find lots of live music, nursery rhymes, sensory participation, action, and movement – and classic characters from the much-loved Mr Men and……
Description: Join storyteller George in a gentle Mr Men and Little Miss story journey. Perfect for young children, you’ll find lots of live music, nursery rhymes, sensory participation, action, and movement – and classic characters from the much-loved Mr Men and Little Miss universe. Get ready to dance, play, and join in with the fun.

Title: Jenny Kleeman: Life and Worth
Teaser: What’s the true value of a human life? Journalist and documentary maker Jenny Kleeman’s The Price of Life delves into the ethical and economic complexities of this profound question…
Description: What’s the true value of a human life? Journalist and documentary maker Jenny Kleeman’s The Price of Life delves into the ethical and economic complexities of this profound question. In a world obsessed with data, Kleeman’s voice and insights are an essential part of the conversation. Talking to global public health researcher and professor Devi Sridhar, hear Kleeman discuss the technologies and industries that are reshaping our understanding of mortality and worth.

Title: Reading to repair: Inspiring the Next Generation with SCWBI and Will Sliney
Teaser: How can children’s books help repair a troubled world and support young minds in the process? Join Will Sliney, Marvel artist and creator of Sky Arts’ Draw with Will, for a powerful conversation on how storytelling and illustration can inspire empathy……
Description: How can children’s books help repair a troubled world and support young minds in the process? Join Will Sliney, Marvel artist and creator of Sky Arts’ Draw with Will, for a powerful conversation on how storytelling and illustration can inspire empathy, build resilience, and promote wellbeing. Discover how reading can help the next generation imagine and create a kinder, more hopeful future. Hosted by Lynwen Pirie from the Society of Children's Books Writers and Illustrators.

Title: Adventuremice Draw Along with Sarah McIntyre and Phillip Reeve
Teaser: Storytelling superstars Sarah McIntyre and Philip Reeve return to the Festival to introduce you to a tiny mouse named Pedro…
Description: Storytelling superstars Sarah McIntyre and Philip Reeve return to the Festival to introduce you to a tiny mouse named Pedro. Join Pedro as he searches for big adventures around the world: diving under the sea, skating across ice and even rocketing to the moon! Based on their latest book, Adventuremice: Mice, Camera, Action! expect an event full of fun, art and adventure. And a draw-along!

Title: Dive into Dragons with Cressida Cowell
Teaser: Join superstar author Cressida Cowell for the launch of How to Train Your Dragon School, the first novel in her Dragon World series for over 10 years!…
Description:
Join superstar author Cressida Cowell for the launch of How to Train Your Dragon School, the first novel in her Dragon World series for over 10 years! Hear all about Hiccup Horrendous Haddock the Third and his dragons as they get up to hilarious hijinks and learn some epic writing and drawing tips from Cressida as she shares her secrets, chats about what inspires her, and reveals some exclusive behind the scenes stories from the new live action film.

	This is a Schools event that is available for livestream only. Please see Dragon Training with Cressida Cowell for our public event.

Title: Caroline O’Donoghue: Sentimental Garbage – Live
Teaser: Novelist Caroline O’Donoghue’s wildly popular Sentimental Garbage podcast is an emotionally-invested, quick-witted celebration of cultural and social topics which may seem frivolous, but hold huge meaning in our hearts, and live rent-free in our brains…
Description: Novelist Caroline O’Donoghue’s wildly popular Sentimental Garbage podcast is an emotionally-invested, quick-witted celebration of cultural and social topics which may seem frivolous, but hold huge meaning in our hearts, and live rent-free in our brains. From 2005’s Pride & Prejudice film adaptation, through the works of Nora Ephron, to Taylor Swift’s epic Eras tour, join O’Donoghue and special guest Cat Cohen, author of the poetry collection God I Feel Modern, for an open-hearted, laughterfilled evening discussing things we love (but won’t always admit to).

Title: Dragon Training with Cressida Cowell
Teaser: Join Cressida Cowell for the launch of How to Train Your Dragon School, the latest novel in her Dragon World series! Hear all about Hiccup Horrendous Haddock the Third and his dragons and learn some epic writing and drawing tips from Cressida…
Description: Join Cressida Cowell for the launch of How to Train Your Dragon School, the latest novel in her Dragon World series! Hear all about Hiccup Horrendous Haddock the Third and his dragons and learn some epic writing and drawing tips from Cressida as she chats about what inspires her and reveals some exclusive behind the scenes stories from the new live action film based on the smash-hit book series.

Title: Peter Godwin: Love, Loss, and Occasional Wars
Teaser: As an author, journalist, and former PEN America president, Peter Godwin has faced conflict with courage throughout his 30-year career. Winning the Orwell Prize with his debut title, Mukiwa, his fourth book, Exit Wounds, sees Godwin face a more personal…
Description: As an author, journalist, and former PEN America president, Peter Godwin has faced conflict with courage throughout his 30-year career. Winning the Orwell Prize with his debut title, Mukiwa, his fourth book, Exit Wounds, sees Godwin face a more personal struggle following his divorce and the death of his mother. Today, he shares his journey of recovery - using a range of different, and sometimes hallucinogenic, strategies - alongside powerful reflections on the singular losses and grief felt by exiles and refugees. Chaired by Ali Millar.

Title: Writing as Grief Practice: A Workshop with Halle O'Neal
Teaser: What can we learn from how people of the past confronted grief? Writing as a grief practice has comforted people across time and cultures, including in Japan where Buddhist writing rituals were thought to positively influence the Karma of your ancestors…
Description: What can we learn from how people of the past confronted grief? Writing as a grief practice has comforted people across time and cultures, including in Japan where Buddhist writing rituals were thought to positively influence the Karma of your ancestors, repairing karmic deficits while consoling the living. Practice this fascinating and ancient art yourself with Japanese Buddhist Art scholar, Halle O'Neal. Participants are welcome to bring cherished letters and objects to the workshop to weave into the practice. Material will also be provided.

Title: Sprog Rock
Teaser: Returning to rock the Book Festival for the fifth year, it’s Sprog Rock! Dust off your dancing shoes and get ready for a rocking and (nursery) rhyming extravaganza, as the group bring their unique, catchy songs back to our Spiegeltent. Fun for…
Description: Returning to rock the Book Festival for the fifth year, it’s Sprog Rock! Dust off your dancing shoes and get ready for a rocking and (nursery) rhyming extravaganza, as the group bring their unique, catchy songs back to our Spiegeltent. Fun for under-fives, their grown-ups, friends, and families.

Title: Close Read: Dear Senthuran by Akwaeke Emezi
Teaser: In our popular Close Read series, a leading author guides you through a deep-diving discussion of a classic text or genre that’s inspired them…
Description: In our popular Close Read series, a leading author guides you through a deep-diving discussion of a classic text or genre that’s inspired them. Think of it as an event blending friendly book club vibes with insightful study notes. Today, join Edwin Morgan Poetry Award-winning poet Titilayo Farukuoye, co-director of the Scottish BPOC Writers Network, as they share their passion for the work of writer and artist Akwaeke Emezi, discussing today Dear Senthuran: A Black Spirit Memoir.

Title: Think, See, and Draw with Candice Purwin
Teaser: Your brain is full of wild, strange, and brilliant things, and we’re going to draw them out. Get ready to rip up the rule book and learn to fold, write, and draw a short comic book all your own in this comics workshop with graphic novelist Candice Purwin…
Description: Your brain is full of wild, strange, and brilliant things, and we’re going to draw them out. Get ready to rip up the rule book and learn to fold, write, and draw a short comic book all your own in this comics workshop with graphic novelist Candice Purwin. All abilities welcome and materials will be provided.

Title: Words from the Wards: The Exhibition
Teaser: Following the success of the Words from the Wards project, we worked with Edinburgh College of Art students to illustrate the collected stories. Join us to view the stories and illustrations side by side in our new festival gallery…
Description: Last year, through our Words from the Wards project, we asked the people of Edinburgh to share stories about the former Royal Infirmary, to honour the experiences and memories that people connect with the building’s previous life. Following the success of the project, we worked with Edinburgh College of Art students to illustrate the collected stories. Join us to view the stories and illustrations side by side in our new festival gallery.

Title: Words from the Wards: The Exhibition
Teaser: Following the success of the Words from the Wards project, we worked with Edinburgh College of Art students to illustrate the collected stories. Join us to view the stories and illustrations side by side in our new festival gallery…
Description: Last year, through our Words from the Wards project, we asked the people of Edinburgh to share stories about the former Royal Infirmary, to honour the experiences and memories that people connect with the building’s previous life. Following the success of the project, we worked with Edinburgh College of Art students to illustrate the collected stories. Join us to view the stories and illustrations side by side in our new festival gallery.

Title: Spark Exhibition
Teaser: Young people from the Alternative School at Spartans Community Foundation are back at the festival for the third year, with their brand-new exhibition, Spark. Our writer in residence Owen Sutcliffe has been working with the young people to spark their…
Description: Young people from the Alternative School at Spartans Community Foundation are back at the festival for the third year, with their brand-new exhibition, Spark. Our writer in residence Owen Sutcliffe has been working with the young people to spark their imaginations, ask big questions and get their creative juices flowing. Join us to see their funny, provocative and sparky creative work.

Title: James Kelman: Your Stories are Your Own
Teaser: Join lifelong literary radical James Kelman, whose commitment to the power and truth of 'ordinary' life - sometimes tragic, but always inspiringly tender and human - remains undimmed. Talking today about his new collections of short fiction (The Story of…
Description: Join lifelong literary radical James Kelman, whose commitment to the power and truth of 'ordinary' life - sometimes tragic, but always inspiringly tender and human - remains undimmed. Talking with us about his new collections of short fiction (The Story of the Stone) and selected interviews (All We Have is the Story), the Booker Prize-winner asks us to remember that language and the freedom to create belongs to us all - so, how might we use it? Chaired by Scott Hames.

Title: Susan Choi & Youssef Rakha: Geopolitics and Family Life
Teaser: Author of the acclaimed Trust Exercise, Susan Choi's Flashlight is a twisting, character-driven mystery about the tensions of family life, spanning the Korean diaspora, Japan, and ultimately the US. And Youssef Rakha's hallucinatory The Dissenters…
Description: Author of the acclaimed Trust Exercise, Susan Choi's Flashlight is a twisting, character-driven mystery about the tensions of family life, spanning the Korean diaspora, Japan, and ultimately the US. And Youssef Rakha's hallucinatory The Dissenters explores the unexpected history of a woman who shifted identities alongside the evolution of her homeland, Egypt, and her children's attempt to reconcile them. Together, talking with Mohamed Tonsy, they reflect on the liminal spaces - and conflicts - created and inhabited by the tangled roots of dispersed families.

Title: Breaking Boundaries: A Creative Writing Workshop with Ashley Hickson-Lovence
Teaser: Let loose your inner writer in this innovative workshop, led by Carnegie Medal for Writing-nominated performance poet and writer, Ashley Hickson-Lovence. Ashley draws on key themes from his YA verse-novel, Wild East, to help you write stories, poems, and…
Description: Let loose your inner writer in this innovative workshop, led by Carnegie Medal for Writing-nominated performance poet and writer, Ashley Hickson-Lovence. Ashley draws on key themes from his YA verse-novel, Wild East, to help you write stories, poems, and even song lyrics with flair and no fear. Wake up your creativity, discover how to use words for maximum impact, and create something boundary-breaking on the page.

Title: We Love Gardens with Joseph Coelho and Fiona Lumbers
Teaser: Join beloved author Joseph Coelho (who was Waterstones Children’s Laureate 2022-2024) and amazing illustrator Fiona Lumbers to celebrate the joy of gardening…
Description: Join beloved author Joseph Coelho (who was Waterstones Children’s Laureate 2022-2024) and amazing illustrator Fiona Lumbers to celebrate the joy of gardening. They’ll share their beautiful new book, Luna Loves Gardening – the fifth in the Luna Loves series – and show how plants and nature connect us to the world and our communities.

Title: Shared Reading with Open Book
Teaser: Join Open Book Lead Readers for an informal and relaxed shared reading session. Each session will explore a chapter from a debut book from this year’s Festival programme. No experience necessary, all reading materials will be provided on the day……
Description: Join Open Book Lead Readers for an informal and relaxed shared reading session. Each session will explore a chapter from a debut book from this year’s Festival programme. No experience necessary, all reading materials will be provided on the day.

Title: Rock the Boat: Open Mic Poetry
Teaser: Whether you’re ready to hit the mic or just keen to soak up the vibes, this event has you covered. Our friends at Push the Boat Out host a special edition of their vibrant monthly open mic to celebrate dynamic contemporary poetry and performance…
Description:
Whether you’re ready to hit the mic or just keen to soak up the vibes, this event has you covered. Our friends at Push the Boat Out, including Julia Sorensen and Catherine Wilson Garry, host a special edition of their vibrant monthly open mic to celebrate dynamic contemporary poetry and performance. So, sit back and enjoy – or take to the stage and showcase your own work.

	Register here if you'd like to be take part. 

	Please note: To ensure we have time for as many poets to read as possible, we are asking all readers to share only one poem that is a maximum 3 minutes.

Title: Robert Crawford: New Words for an Old World
Teaser: Poet, critic and literary historian Robert Crawford nimbly traverses the globe in his new poetry collection, Old World, in this special launch event. Crawford is one of Scotland's most esteemed poets and thinkers, deftly weaving between different poetic…
Description: Poet, critic and literary historian Robert Crawford nimbly traverses the globe in his new poetry collection, Old World, in this special launch event. Crawford is one of Scotland's most esteemed poets and thinkers, deftly weaving between different poetic forms, from haiku to riddle. Join us for an enlivening discussion on the issues afflicting an ailing planet - from climate change to AI - and poetry's role in our fragile modern society. Chaired by Robyn Marsack.

Title: Rose Keating & So Mayer: Beyond Reality
Teaser: Everything is not as it seems in Rose Keating and So Mayer's unique and lively new short story collections. Join them for a discussion with Sasha de Buyl about their playful, provocative forms, storytelling, and bringing fresh new perspectives to the…
Description: Everything is not as it seems in Rose Keating and So Mayer's unique and lively new short story collections. Keating's Oddbody is bold and unsettling, confronting themes of desire, fear and shame. Mayer's Truth & Dare is a queer and propulsive tour through what was, what is, and what could have been. Join them for a discussion with Sasha de Buyl about their playful, provocative forms, storytelling, and bringing fresh new perspectives to the human condition.

Title: Draw New Worlds with Beth Suzanna
Teaser: Are you fascinated by the night sky? Or are you more interested in what lurks at the bottom of the ocean? Get ready to make a splash in a colour-filled, joyful drawing workshop with illustrator Beth Suzanna, inspired by her newest book, See For Yourself…
Description: Are you fascinated by the night sky? Or are you more interested in what lurks at the bottom of the ocean? Get ready to make a splash in a colour-filled, joyful drawing workshop with illustrator Beth Suzanna, inspired by her newest book, See For Yourself. It follows Harry and his dad who are from a family of amazing inventors. Explore worlds that we’re yet to discover and dare to try something different!

Title: Renga Poetry: A Nature Writing Workshop with Karen McCarthy Woolf
Teaser: How do we write in collaboration with other humans and the more-than human? Join poet Karen McCarthy Woolf (Top Doll, Seasonal Disturbances) for this exploratory workshop on renga poetry…
Description:
How do we write in collaboration with other humans and the more-than human? Join poet Karen McCarthy Woolf (Top Doll, Seasonal Disturbances) for this exploratory workshop on renga poetry. Existing for centuries, renga is a form written collectively by a group of poets - like a lyrical version of the childhood game, Consequence. Today, immerse yourself in nature and gather material and inspiration from the local environment for use today and afterwards.

	Suitable for all levels of writing experience, including none.

Title: Repair Cafe Edinburgh
Teaser: Got something that’s broken? Want to try fixing it but not sure how? Repair Cafes are free community events where you can bring your item and volunteer fixers will guide you through your repair…
Description:
Got something that’s broken? Want to try fixing it but not sure how? Repair Cafes are free community events where you can bring your item and volunteer fixers will guide you through your repair.

	Not everything's fixable at our events - we're limited by time, spare parts, safety, capacity.

	If you’ve got something that you want to fix, email us at repaircafeedinburgh@gmail.com to confirm suitability and to reserve your place.

	For more details, visit Repair Cafe.

Title: Laura Bates: Misogyny Reinvented
Teaser: Deepfakes, cyber brothels, AI girlfriends, sex robots – thanks to the new wave of AI-powered technologies, misogyny is getting a chilling modern makeover. Laura Bates exposes the frightening dimensions of this trend in The New Age of Sexism…
Description: Deepfakes, cyber brothels, AI girlfriends, sex robots – thanks to the new wave of AI-powered technologies, misogyny is getting a chilling modern makeover. Laura Bates, founder of the Everyday Sexism Project and present-day icon of women’s rights, exposes the frightening dimensions of this trend in The New Age of Sexism. She’s joined by Heather Parry to discuss the roles we can all play on these emergent battlegrounds for gender equality.

Title: Getting Published with Asli Jensen and Louise Lamont
Teaser: The journey to getting published can feel daunting when you’re on the outside. So, we’re here to bring you an insider’s guide. Join literary agent Louise Lamont as she chats with Asli Jensen and Eilidh Akilade in an inspiring conversation that seeks to…
Description: The journey to getting published can feel daunting when you’re on the outside. So, we’re here to bring you an insider’s guide. Join literary agent Louise Lamont, Asli Jensen (Lime Pictures New Storyteller Award-winning debut author of Love on Sight), and Lindsay Hirst (winner of Scottish Book Trust's New Writers Award and author of The Dangerous Pet Lover's Guide to Dragons) in an inspiring conversation with Eilidh Akilade that seeks to demystify the industry, provide practical tips, and inspire you to take the plunge towards getting published.

Title: Paula Hawkins: An Unexpected Visitor
Teaser: Author of the global phenomenon Girl on a Train, Paula Hawkins joins Val McDermid to talk about her latest page-turning thriller…
Description: What do a swanky art gallery in London and a remote Scottish island - 12 hours from the mainland - have in common? A human bone as it turns out. Isolation, secrecy, adultery, fame, art, and a dead body - The Blue Hour is a rollercoaster ride of thrills. Author of the global phenomenon Girl on a Train, Paula Hawkins joins Val McDermid to talk about her latest page-turning thriller.

Title: Harriet Armstrong & Rosalind Brown: Lessons in Inner Life
Teaser: Two razor-sharp debut novelists talk with Sasha de Buyl about the fitful, lurching paths we take on the coming-of-age journey…
Description: Two razor-sharp debut novelists talk with Sasha de Buyl about the fitful, lurching paths we take on the coming-of-age journey. Harriet Armstrong’s To Rest Our Minds and Bodies is a poignant, wry portrait of a young woman struggling to retain a sense of self in the final year of her undergrad, while Rosalind Brown’s Practice exquisitely depicts the minutiae of a day in the life of a very fastidious student writing an essay on Shakespeare’s sonnets.

Title: Dive into an Ocean Adventure with Martin Stewart
Teaser: Ocean explorer Sandy Fin: diver of the deep and puzzler of puzzles. Can he save the Museum of Seaside Stories and its collection of treasures?…
Description: Ocean explorer Sandy Fin: diver of the deep and puzzler of puzzles. Can he save the Museum of Seaside Stories and its collection of treasures? Dive into hilarious coastal adventure with award-winning author Martin Stewart and help restore the museum to its former glory as he shares his new book Sandy Fin: Operation Splash Landing with you. Full of laughs, this event will celebrate the great outdoors and our connection to nature.

Title: Saving the Day with Science with Chanté Timothy
Teaser: Look out! A new graphic novel series is exploding its way onto our bookshelves. Meet Nova, a young super scientist with a thirst for knowledge, experiments, and adventures. Just like a supernova in the sky, she’s blazing with energy and excitement!…
Description: Look out! A new graphic novel series is exploding its way onto our bookshelves. Meet Nova, a young super scientist with a thirst for knowledge, experiments, and adventures. Just like a supernova in the sky, she’s blazing with energy and excitement! Join Chanté Timothy as she shares her vibrant, colourful new series Supa Nova with a spectacular heroine.

Title: Shared Reading with Open Book
Teaser: Join Open Book Lead Readers for an informal and relaxed shared reading session. Each session will explore a chapter from a debut book from this year's Festival programme. No experience necessary, all reading materials will be provided on the day……
Description: Join Open Book Lead Readers for an informal and relaxed shared reading session. Each session will explore a chapter from a debut book from this year's Festival programme. No experience necessary, all reading materials will be provided on the day.

Title: Colum McCann: Heart of Darkness at the Bottom of the Sea
Teaser: Has the ultra-connected nature of modern life left humanity more lonely? Are some connections better severed? In Colum McCann's Twist, a journalist is sent to report on the repair of the undersea cables that make modern communication possible when the……
Description: Has the ultra-connected nature of modern life left humanity more lonely? Are some connections better severed? In Colum McCann's Twist, a journalist is sent to report on the repair of the undersea cables that make modern communication possible when the vessel's captain vanishes. Today, the National Book Award-winning author of Let the Great World Spin talks with Festival director Jenny Niven about his dark new Conrad-esque novel and the power of stories to repair a broken world.

Title: Jeremy Atherton Lin & Charlie Porter: Trying to Make it Home
Teaser: Juxtaposing past and present, ecstasy and heartache, both authors use homes as a structure to explore and illuminate queer histories. They discuss capturing queer truths in their discussion today…
Description: Jeremy Atherton Lin’s Deep House: The Gayest Love Story Ever Told combines a kaleidoscopic history of the battle for marriage equality with a radically intimate memoir. Tender, funny, stylish, sexy – the book sweeps across three decades, across houses and countries, tracing the story of American Lin and his British partner trying to build a life together while navigating the precarious legal landscape facing immigrants and LGBTQI+ people. Juxtaposing past and present, ecstasy and heartache, Lin joins us to discuss this epic tale of love, law, and home today. Chaired by Cole Collins.

Title: Ece Temelkuran: Coming Together to Fight Dictatorship
Teaser: How did things get so bad, and how can we begin to try and make them better? Turkish political commentator, novelist, poet, and winner of the El Mundo International Journalism Award, Ece Temelkuran joins us to unpack two books attempting to answer both…
Description: How did things get so bad, and how can we begin to try and make them better? Turkish political commentator, novelist, poet, and winner of the El Mundo International Journalism Award, Ece Temelkuran joins us to unpack two books attempting to answer both sides of this question. In How to Lose a Country, she outlines the slide from democracy to dictatorship, while Together emphasises community as a means of instigating positive change. Chaired by Talat Yaqoob.

Title: Book Fest vs Fringe: The Ultimate Quiz
Teaser: Showing it’s possible to be funny AND know your way around a contents page, 6 stars of page and stage battle it out in the ultimate book quiz hosted by Thanyia Moore…
Description: The Book Festival isn’t the only show in town during August – stars galore will also be massing in Edinburgh for the Festival Fringe, allegedly. But who knows their Atwood from their elbow? Whose TBR pile is scraping the ceiling? Showing it’s possible to be funny AND know your way around a contents page, 6 stars of page and stage battle it out in the ultimate book quiz hosted by Thanyia Moore. On the Fringe team we have Michelle Brasier, Zoë Coombs Marr, and Josh Glanc; and representing the Book Festival we have Gemma Cairney, Joseph Coelho, and Heather Parry.

Title: Raymond Antrobus: The Quiet Ear
Teaser: As the first ever poet to win the Rathbones Folio Prize (for The Perseverance), we’re delighted to have Raymond Antrobus back with us to launch his debut work of non-fiction, The Quiet Ear…
Description: As the first ever poet to win the Rathbones Folio Prize (for The Perseverance), Raymond Antrobus provided a compelling insight into the d/Deaf experience. We’re delighted to have Antrobus back with us to launch his debut work of non-fiction, The Quiet Ear, at this year’s Festival. Part memoir, part call to action, it tells of his experience growing up as deaf child to Jamaican and English parents, searching for acceptance, and ultimately finding his people. Chaired by Colin Grant.

Title: Samanta Schweblin: Beauty and the Sinister
Teaser: Unnerving, strange, and skin-prickling are words frequently used to describe leading Argentinian writer Samanta Schweblin’s short stories, which expertly balance literary elegance with emotional depth…
Description: Unnerving, strange, and skin-prickling are words frequently used to describe leading Argentinian writer Samanta Schweblin’s short stories, which expertly balance literary elegance with emotional depth. Her new collection, Good and Evil and Other Stories, unleashes six new tales of the uncanny, and today she speaks to Kirsty Logan about her startling imagination, and how embracing the eerie can reveal unnameable human emotions.

Title: Let's Rock with Robert Tregoning
Teaser: Get up and dance as author, choreographer, and former West End performer Robert Tregoning shares his latest book, The Rock Family Band…
Description: Get up and dance as author, choreographer, and former West End performer Robert Tregoning shares his latest book, The Rock Family Band. The story follows Sam, a quiet flute player who feels he doesn’t fit in with his rock star family. Come and learn how our differences can be exactly what brings us together in this fun, interactive event that will get you on your feet.

Title: Where Magic Happens with Unicorn Academy
Teaser: Get ready for a sparkly Unicorn Academy adventure based on the hit TV show in this special unicorn extravaganza. It’s going to be a summer to remember on Unicorn Island as Layla works in the library, trying to make a name for herself. It’s going to be…
Description: Get ready for a sparkly Unicorn Academy adventure based on the hit TV show in this special unicorn extravaganza. It’s going to be a summer to remember on Unicorn Island as Layla works in the library, trying to make a name for herself. Come along for a special screening of the new episode, and take part in unicorn arts, crafts, and activities. It’s going to be magical!

Title: Celebrate 10 Years of Read Write Count with Tracey Corderoy and Steven Lenton
Teaser: Shifty McGifty and Slippery Sam are back for a PAW-some new adventure…
Description:
This special event is in partnership with Scottish Book Trust, celebrating 10 years of Read Write Count, Scotland's national book-gifting campaign. Get an exclusive first peek at what’s in this year's bags!

	Shifty McGifty and Slippery Sam are back for a PAW-some new adventure. Join author Tracey Corderoy and illustrator Steven Lenton to find out how the robber dogs turned crime-solving-baking-duo keep saving the day. Expect storytelling, live-drawing, games, and loads of fun as the characters come to life. 

	This is a Schools event that is available for livestream only.

Title: Robert Macfarlane: Is A River Alive?
Teaser: Robert Macfarlane's radiant writing on nature, people, and place is in a class unto itself, and the Guardian has slated Is a River Alive? as the biggest publishing event of 2025…
Description: Robert Macfarlane's radiant writing on nature, people, and place is in a class unto itself, and the Guardian has slated Is a River Alive? as the biggest publishing event of 2025. This passionate, perspective-shifting treatise revives the idea that rivers are living beings and should be treated as such. Macfarlane will discuss 'thirsty notebooks', rivers as co-authors, and writing his most personal and political book to date. Chaired by Cal Flyn.

Title: Chantal Lyons, Sophie Pavelle & Peter Cairns: Landscape, and Beavers, and Boars (Oh, My!)
Teaser: Sharing their deep understanding of what we're lucky to have in nature and how to repair the damage done, Wainwright Prize-­shortlisted author of Groundbreakers, Chantal Lyons, To Have or to Hold author Sophie Pavelle, and photographer and rewilding…
Description: Chantal Lyons' Wainwright Prize-­shortlisted Groundbreakers investigates the wild boar's dramatic re-emergence in Britain after seven centuries, while in To Have or to Hold, Sophie Pavelle examines eight symbiotic relationships in nature to demonstrate the critical interconnections between ecosystems. They're joined by photographer and rewilding thought leader, Peter Cairns, to share their deep understanding of what we're lucky to have in nature and how to repair the damage done. Chaired by Hannah Rudman.

Title: Creative Repair: A Junk Journals Workshop with Rachel Hazell
Teaser: Explore the Festival’s overarching theme of Repair through the art of junk journaling: transforming discarded ephemera into beautiful books…
Description: Explore the Festival’s overarching theme of Repair through the art of junk journaling: transforming discarded ephemera into beautiful books. This hands-on workshop with bookbinder Rachel Hazell invites you to engage in mindful making through collage. Materials are provided, though you’re invited to bring your own ‘found handwriting’ (from crumpled shopping lists to old birthday cards) allowing you to uncover new personal stories from within their recycled fragments.

Title: Spark Exhibition
Teaser: Young people from the Alternative School at Spartans Community Foundation are back at the festival for the third year, with their brand-new exhibition, Spark. Our writer in residence Owen Sutcliffe has been working with the young people to spark their…
Description: Young people from the Alternative School at Spartans Community Foundation are back at the festival for the third year, with their brand-new exhibition, Spark. Our writer in residence Owen Sutcliffe has been working with the young people to spark their imaginations, ask big questions and get their creative juices flowing. Join us to see their funny, provocative and sparky creative work.

Title: Denise Mina: Bloody Murder
Teaser: Deemed ‘crime-writing royalty’ by Ian Rankin, bestselling author Denise Mina returns to the Festival with her 20th novel, The Good Liar…
Description: Deemed ‘crime-writing royalty’ by Ian Rankin, bestselling author Denise Mina returns to the Festival with her 20th novel, The Good Liar. This clever thriller sees blood-spatter expert, Dr Claudia O’Sheil, get entangled in a conspiracy which threatens her career, reputation, and maybe even her life. How far would you go to protect your loved ones? Would you even cover up a murder? Hear Mina chat morals and murders today with her signature verve and wit. Chaired by Peggy Hughes.

Title: Steph McGovern: Lights, Camera, Kidnap
Teaser: Steph McGovern is no stranger to television; as an award-winning broadcaster, podcaster, and host of her own live daily show, she has seen her fair share of sets. But none as terrifying as the backdrop to her debut novel Deadline. Go behind the scenes of…
Description: Steph McGovern is no stranger to television; as an award-winning broadcaster, podcaster, and host of her own live daily show, she has seen her fair share of sets. But none as terrifying as the backdrop to her debut novel Deadline: live on air, TV reporter Rose's children go missing and she's the only one who can save them. Join McGovern and go behind the scenes of this enticing thriller as she talks to Nicola Sturgeon.

Title: Doug Johnstone: Making Waves in Science Fiction
Teaser: Described by The Scotsman as ‘a master of the page-turning, heart-gripping, plot-driven tale’, Doug Johnstone is also remarkably prolific…
Description: Described by the Scotsman as ‘a master of the page-turning, heart-gripping, plot-driven tale’, Doug Johnstone is also remarkably prolific. Over the years, the McIlvanney Prize-shortlisted author’s focus has shifted from crime to sci-fi, and now he joins us to chat about his 19th novel, The Transcendent Tide, which completes his science fiction Enceladons trilogy: a first contact epic which has taken its characters from Edinburgh’s Portobello beach to the depths of the Arctic Ocean. Chaired by Rachelle Atalla.

Title: The Silk Roads: Ten Years On
Teaser: With our trading relationships with India and China still very much at the fore, join Frankopan as we revisit this seminal book and its ongoing implications…
Description: Ten years ago, Peter Frankopan changed the way we think about the historical relationship between East and West, with The Silk Roads: A New History of the World. The book lived up to its title, shifting focus from the West towards the Eastern crucibles of civilisation, religion, and industry, and opening up a treasure trove of research on previous eras of exchange and collaboration. With our trading relationships with India and China still very much at the fore, join Frankopan as we revisit this seminal book and its ongoing implications.

Title: Vigdis Hjorth: Love Will Tear Us Apart
Teaser: Leading Norwegian author Vigdis Hjorth writes novels that are 'like major fires: destructive and difficult to contain', according to Literary Review. In her latest, If Only, she explores how an impulsive affair at an unremarkable conference descends into…
Description: Leading Norwegian author Vigdis Hjorth writes novels that are 'like major fires: destructive and difficult to contain', according to Literary Review. In her latest, If Only, she explores how an impulsive affair at an unremarkable conference descends into an inferno of jealousy, obsession, and an addiction that can never be sated. Today she joins Kirsty Logan to discuss the destructive potential of love when it binds the wrong people.

Title: Oliver’s Vegetables Workshop with Vivian French
