Teaser: Join bestselling author-illustrator Vivian French as she celebrates the anniversary of Oliver’s Vegetables at this delicious (and nutritious) illustration workshop…
Description: Eating vegetables isn’t always a happy occasion, and no one understands this better than Oliver. He only likes eating chips. Until his grandpa says he has to eat every vegetable that comes out of the ground each day – and Oliver soon discovers they are un-beet-able! Join bestselling author-illustrator Vivian French as she celebrates the anniversary of Oliver’s Vegetables at this delicious (and nutritious) illustration workshop.

Title: Words from the Wards: The Exhibition
Teaser: Following the success of the Words from the Wards project, we worked with Edinburgh College of Art students to illustrate the collected stories. Join us to view the stories and illustrations side by side in our new festival gallery…
Description: Last year, through our Words from the Wards project, we asked the people of Edinburgh to share stories about the former Royal Infirmary, to honour the experiences and memories that people connect with the building’s previous life. Following the success of the project, we worked with Edinburgh College of Art students to illustrate the collected stories. Join us to view the stories and illustrations side by side in our new festival gallery.

Title: Spark Exhibition
Teaser: Young people from the Alternative School at Spartans Community Foundation are back at the festival for the third year, with their brand-new exhibition, Spark. Our writer in residence Owen Sutcliffe has been working with the young people to spark their…
Description: Young people from the Alternative School at Spartans Community Foundation are back at the festival for the third year, with their brand-new exhibition, Spark. Our writer in residence Owen Sutcliffe has been working with the young people to spark their imaginations, ask big questions and get their creative juices flowing. Join us to see their funny, provocative and sparky creative work.

Title: Kate Anderson, Rosemary Goring & Jade Scott: The Captive Queen and Her Son
Teaser: Rosemary Goring's Exile: The Captive Years of Mary, Queen of Scots and Jade Scott's Captive Queen shed remarkable new light on the duplicitous years of Mary's English imprisonment. Meanwhile, Kate Anderson's Art & Court of James VI & I reconsiders Mary's…
Description: Rosemary Goring's Exile: The Captive Years of Mary, Queen of Scots and Jade Scott's Captive Queen shed remarkable new light on the duplicitous years of Mary's English imprisonment. Meanwhile, Kate Anderson's Art & Court of James VI & I reconsiders Mary's only child, a figure often overshadowed by his mother. Join them for a fascinating discussion on the enduring allure of the House of Stuart. Chaired by Anna Groundwater.

Title: Poets on Film
Teaser: Witness the fusion of poetry and film, through a collaboration between WritersMosaic and the Adrian Brinkerhoff Poetry Foundation. This live event features readings and screenings, showcasing the power of spoken word through a cinematic lens. Prepare to…
Description: Witness the fusion of poetry and film, through a collaboration between WritersMosaic and the Adrian Brinkerhoff Poetry Foundation. This live event features readings and screenings, showcasing the power of spoken word through a cinematic lens, where poets including Anthony Anaxagorou, Jo Clement, and Marjorie Lotfi encounter the work of filmmakers Rob Akin and Savannah Acquah. Prepare to have your creative fires stoked by this glorious call­ and-response between literary and visual cultures. Chaired by Colin Grant.

Title: Close Read: Frankenstein by Mary Shelley
Teaser: Today, Nicholas Jubber (Monsterland) dissects Mary Shelley’s gothic classic, Frankenstein, peeling back its layers of language and morality to reach the heart of a tale which has never beaten more strongly…
Description: In our popular Close Read series, a leading author guides you through a deep-diving discussion of a classic text or genre that’s inspired them. Think of it as an event blending friendly book club vibes with insightful study notes. Today, Nicholas Jubber (Monsterland) dissects Mary Shelley’s gothic classic, Frankenstein, peeling back its layers of language and morality to reach the heart of a tale which has never beaten more strongly.

Title: Words from the Wards: The Exhibition
Teaser: Following the success of the Words from the Wards project, we worked with Edinburgh College of Art students to illustrate the collected stories. Join us to view the stories and illustrations side by side in our new festival gallery…
Description: Last year, through our Words from the Wards project, we asked the people of Edinburgh to share stories about the former Royal Infirmary, to honour the experiences and memories that people connect with the building’s previous life. Following the success of the project, we worked with Edinburgh College of Art students to illustrate the collected stories. Join us to view the stories and illustrations side by side in our new festival gallery.

Title: Together We Repair
Teaser: We believe that everyone has a story to tell and that stories help us make sense of our world. We’ve challenged local writers and poets, this year, to respond to 2025’s Festival theme: Repair…
Description: We believe that everyone has a story to tell and that stories help us make sense of our world. We’ve challenged local writers and poets, this year, to respond to 2025’s Festival theme: Repair. Join us as we bring them together to perform their work: a patchwork of ideas on how to make the world a better place. Today featuring writing and performances from the Open Book Creative Writers.

Title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
Teaser: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Appearing today: Morag Hood…
Description: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Appearing today: Morag Hood.

Title: Mairi Kidd & Lesley McDowell: Reimagining History’s (Anti)Heroines
Teaser: Join Mairi Kidd and Lesley McDowell for a romp through 19th century Scotland as they discuss the craft of compelling character studies and inventing voices for women lost to time…
Description: Lesley McDowell’s Love and Other Poisons features a scandalous affair, an unsolved murder, and the disappearance of the socialite who stands accused. Mairi Kidd’s The Specimens reinvents the story of notorious serial killers Burke and Hare, told through the eyes of two very different women. Join the authors for a romp through 19th century Scotland as they discuss the craft of compelling character studies and inventing voices for women lost to time. Chaired by Jemma Neville.

Title: Damian Barr: Forgotten Love
Teaser: Bestselling author of Maggie and Me and host of the Big Scottish Book Club, the ebullient Damien Barr takes us back in time to 1930s Scotland with his intoxicating new novel…
Description: Bestselling author of Maggie and Me and host of the Big Scottish Book Club, the ebullient Damien Barr takes us back in time to 1930s Scotland with his intoxicating new novel. The Two Roberts is about real artists, Robert Colquhoun and Robert MacBryde, who met at Glasgow School of Art, and whose passionate romance Barr now stunningly reimagines. Join him today as he sheds deserved light on the love story of two pioneering Scottish artists. Chaired by Andrew O'Hagan.

Title: Naga Munchetty: It’s (Not) All In Your Head
Teaser: Women’s healthcare is in need of a revolution, and BBC broadcaster Naga Munchetty is ready to fight. She talks with Devi Sridhar about the fundamental flaws in our healthcare system…
Description: Women’s healthcare is in need of a revolution, and BBC broadcaster Naga Munchetty is ready to fight. In It’s Probably Nothing, she explores the difficulties women still face in getting diagnosed and treated, and provides actionable lessons to help women advocate for themselves in medical settings. She talks with Devi Sridhar about the fundamental flaws in our healthcare system and the provocative conversations that inspired her book.

Title: Kirstin Anderson & Lady Unchained: Unlocking the Arts
Teaser: Cultural experiences are a proven springboard for positive change and rehabilitation in the criminal justice system. Yet, despite numerous interventions over the last 50 years, arts provision in UK prisons remains inconsistent. Join Dr Kirstin Anderson…
Description: Cultural experiences are a proven springboard for positive change and rehabilitation in the criminal justice system. Yet, despite numerous interventions over the last 50 years, arts provision in UK prisons remains inconsistent. In The Barlinnie Special Unit: Art, Punishment and Innovation Dr Kirstin Anderson digs into the history of the radical HMP Barlinnie Special unit. While in Behind Bars, poet Lady Unchained advocates for creative life in and after prison. They join our director of Communities and Equalities Noëlle Cobden for a thought­-provoking discussion.

Title: Lanre Bakare, Jen Calleja & Ash Sarkar: Changing the Culture
Teaser: Three vibrant voices shaking up assumptions on class, race, and culture join us for a perspective-shifting discussion…
Description: Three vibrant voices shaking up assumptions on class, race, and culture join us for a perspective-shifting discussion. In We Were There, Guardian arts correspondent Lanre Bakare examines how Black culture and resistance from the 1970s on helped shape modern Britain. Jen Calleja’s translation memoir, Fair, breaks down issues of class and background in the publishing industry. And in Minority Rule, writer and activist Ash Sarkar assesses how the culture wars have been weaponised to divide and rule. Chaired by Sarah Manavis.

Title: Kate Kennedy: The Sound of Four Strings
Teaser: The cello is regarded as the warmest of string instruments and for those who play it, the instrument is like a character in their lives. In Cello, Kate Kennedy illuminates that deep companionship between musician and instrument via a biography of four…
Description: The cello is regarded as the warmest of string instruments and for those who play it, the instrument is like a character in their lives. In Cello, Kate Kennedy illuminates that deep companionship between musician and instrument via a biography of four remarkable cellists: through persecution, injury, and misfortune, through death camps and shipwrecks, into her own present and future. Join her to explore how the very soul of music, without language, speaks to us all. Chaired by Jo Buckley.

Title: Words Can Fly with Donna Ashworth
Teaser: Join poet Donna Ashworth for an enchanting exploration of her new poetry book, Words Can Fly. Each of Donna’s poems explores what is most important in our lives – family, friendships, school, and the world around us…
Description: Join poet Donna Ashworth for an enchanting exploration of her new poetry book, Words Can Fly. Each of Donna’s poems explores what is most important in our lives – family, friendships, school, and the world around us. This fun-filled event will inspire you to celebrate your uniqueness, embrace curiosity, and discover the transformative power of kindness, compassion, and beautiful poetry.

Title: Diane Abbott: A Lifetime of Making a Difference
Teaser: Diane Abbott's journey to Westminster as the UK's first Black female MP is borne of sheer determination. She speaks about her inspirational memoir, A Woman Like Me…
Description: Diane Abbott’s journey to Westminster as the UK’s first Black female MP is borne of sheer determination. The child of Windrush generation Jamaican parents, raised in working class North London, and studying at Cambridge, Abbott has faced ridicule and ire on account of her race and gender, but has remained a committed activist for social change, and outspoken member of the Labour party. Talat Yaqoob speaks today to Abbottabout her inspirational memoir, A Woman Like Me.

Title: Harry Josephine Giles & Malin Lewis: Future Traditions for Queer Scotland
Teaser: Join us for a dazzling celebration of Unco, a new LGBT+ Scots lexicon. Harry Josephine Giles and Malin Lewis present a unique spoken word and music performance, blending old and new language and sounds to explore queer identities and histories…
Description: Join us for a dazzling celebration of Unco, a new LGBT+ Scots lexicon. Harry Josephine Giles and Malin Lewis present a unique spoken word and music performance, blending old and new language and sounds to explore queer identities and histories. After the performance, a discussion with the artists delves further into their creative process and explores the Unco project’s potential to connect Scottish tradition with ideas that boldly face the future. Chaired by Shane Strachan. The development of the performance was supported by Edinburgh Futures Institute.

Title: Fresh Words: The Kavya Prize
Teaser: It’s lunchtime, and (hallelujah!) there’s no need to doomscroll over a sad desk salad. Be the first to discover the literary stars of the future, instead…
Description: It’s lunchtime, and (hallelujah!) there’s no need to doomscroll over a sad desk salad. Be the first to discover the literary stars of the future, instead. In partnership with Scottish Book Trust and other leading talent spotters across the UK, this lively lunchtime event showcases electrifying new voices, so grab your seat before everyone else does. Today, we partner with The Kavya Prize, hearing from writers including 2023 prize winner Jinling Wu and shortlisted authors Theresa Muñoz and Samina Chaudry. They are joined by Scottish Book Trust New Writers Awardees Craig Aitchison and Deborah Chu.

Title: Tanya Talaga: Open Secrets
Teaser: Anishinaabe writer Tanya Talaga's The Knowing is a riveting exploration of her family's story, and a retelling of the country we now call Canada…
Description: Anishinaabe writer Tanya Talaga's The Knowing is a riveting exploration of her family's story, and a retelling of the country we now call Canada. One of Canada's most distinguished journalists, Talaga holds five honorary doctorates, and reported on the Catholic Church's shocking efforts to avoid responsibility regarding Indian Residential Schools. Today she explores how historical actions continue to impact families and communities, and how she came to bring these hidden histories to light. Chaired by Kezia Dugdale.

Title: Queerly Beloved
Teaser: Join Kirsty Logan as she chats to a warm and lively panel of queer writers, including Harry Josephine Giles and Alan Hollinghurst, as they share the books which inspired them as writers and the stories they wish they could have read sooner…
Description: We are gathered here today, under the canvas of the Spiegeltent, to celebrate queer lives, voices, and literature! Join Kirsty Logan as she chats to a warm and lively panel of queer writers, including Harry Josephine Giles, Alan Hollinghurst, and Niall Moorjani as they share the books which inspired them as writers, the stories they wish they could have read sooner, and why it matters so much to see your experiences represented in the culture you consume.

Title: Katie Kitamura: Authenticity Unmasked
Teaser: Join author of Intimacies, Katie Kitamura, as she discusses her hotly anticipated new novel, Audition, exploring what it means to truly know our authentic self and the different roles we play to the outside world…
Description: Shakespeare once wrote, 'All the world's a stage, and the men and women merely players'. We are all constantly playing roles: parent, child, partner, friend. So, who are we really? Join author of Intimacies, Katie Kitamura, as she discusses her hotly anticipated new novel, Audition, exploring what it means to truly know our authentic self and the different roles we play to the outside world. Chaired by Adam Biles.

Title: M John Harrison: The Course of His Art
Teaser: Titan of modern literary science fiction, M John Harrison has never shied away from bending genre and reimaging the form of fantasy novels…
Description: Titan of modern literary science fiction, M John Harrison has never shied away from bending genre and reimaging the form of fantasy novels. In this frank conversation, he joins Camilla Grudova on the rerelease of his 1990s classic The Course of the Heart. They reflect on why the book gained a cult-like following and Harrison will share intriguing memories of a trailblazing 50-year career that has seen his work endure across decades.

Title: Chloe Dalton: Raising Hare
Teaser: Suffering from burnout, political adviser Chloe Dalton retreated from the big city to the English countryside. There she found a seemingly abandoned leveret, or baby hare, and took it home…
Description: Suffering from burnout, political adviser Chloe Dalton retreated from the big city to the English countryside. There she found a seemingly abandoned leveret, or baby hare, and took it home. Longlisted for 2025’s Women’s Prize for Non-Fiction, Raising Hare is the heartwarming story of how this tiny creature changed Dalton’s life, and how care can transcend the boundaries between humans and animals. Dalton joins us to discuss her magical encounter and our Festival theme of Repair. Chaired by Alex Clark.

Title: Fiona Benson, Sarah Shin & Rebecca Tamás: Casting Spells
Teaser: Poetry can be bewitching: the words on the page enchant your mind and rearrange the way you think. Join the writers today as they explore poetry's magical grip on all of us…
Description: Poetry can be bewitching: the words on the page enchant your mind and rearrange the way you think. Never has this been more true than in three-time T.S. Eliot Prize-shortlisted poet Fiona Benson's Midden Witch, and Sarah Shin and Rebecca Tamás' anthology of occult poetry, Spells. But how closely linked are spells and poetry? Alice Tarbuck joins the writers today as they explore poetry's magical grip on all of us.

Title: Richard Holloway: The Grace in Uncertainty
Teaser: In this unmissable event, Holloway shares the texts and music that have shaped him, reflects on a long life defined by great faith and grave doubt, and relates how he’s found a gentle path between the two…
Description: Richard Holloway – the archetypal ‘turbulent priest’ turned writer, broadcaster, and public intellectual – is a true Scottish national treasure. Tonight, with characteristic wit and wisdom, he shares his new memoir, Last Words, which he says will be his final book. In this unmissable event, Holloway shares the texts and music that have shaped him, reflects on a long life defined by great faith and grave doubt, and relates how he’s found a gentle path between the two. Chaired by Jenny Brown.

Title: War of the Worlds with Chris Mould
Teaser: Join Chris for a fascinating talk about how he illustrated, updated and adapted this incredible sci-fi story that’s over 100 years old…
Description: Award-winning author and illustrator Chris Mould brings his latest graphic novel The War of the Worlds to this year’s festival. Based on the H G Wells original classic this is an intriguing re-telling for a brand-new audience. When an alien-filled meteor lands on Earth, protagonist Leon must search for the answers and understand the science of these extraterrestrial creatures. Join Chris for a fascinating talk about how he illustrated, updated and adapted this incredible sci-fi story that’s over 100 years old.

Title: Beyond the Archives with Jo Clifford and Jen Hadfield
Teaser: Now in its centenary year, the National Library of Scotland is a treasure trove of Scotland's literary past - but did you know it also cares for the archives of our nation's contemporary writers? Today, we explore the idea of a 'living archive' with…
Description: Now in its centenary year, the National Library of Scotland is a treasure trove of Scotland's literary past - but did you know it also cares for the archives of our nation's contemporary writers? Today, we explore the idea of a 'living archive' with playwright Jo Clifford and poet Jen Hadfield. Join them for a conversation about building an archive, the creative and curatorial choices involved, and discover the personal objects that fuel each writer's creative life.

Title: Alex Howard: A Cat’s-Eye View of Edinburgh Life
Teaser: In his latest century-spanning novel, The Ghost Cat, Howard’s be-whiskered protagonist is a ghost residing in Edinburgh’s leafy Marchmont. Join Howard at the Festival to chat about inhabiting the moggie mind and how he found inspiration from an…
Description: In Library Cat, bestselling author Alex Howard tugged on readers’ heart strings with his witty collection of observations about the University of Edinburgh’s most famous feline denizen. In his latest century-spanning novel, The Ghost Cat, Howard’s be-whiskered protagonist is a ghost residing in Edinburgh’s leafy Marchmont. Howard joins Mary Paulson-Ellis to chat about inhabiting the moggie mind and how he found inspiration from an Edinburgh tenement.

Title: Plot as Repair: A Workshop with Eleanor Catton
Teaser: Under the guidance of Man Booker Prize-winning Eleanor Catton (The Luminaries, Birnam Wood), you'll consider the breaches of trust and expectation that are integral to plots of every kind and discuss the infinite ways they can be mended, denied…
Description: A good plot feels neither overdetermined nor arbitrary. Its job is to surprise not just the reader, but the characters as well; to create desires, and - eventually - to sate them. Under the guidance of Man Booker Prize-winning Eleanor Catton (The Luminaries, Birnam Wood), you'll consider the breaches of trust and expectation that are integral to plots of every kind and discuss the infinite ways they can be mended, denied, projected, repeated, forgotten, forgiven, and avenged.

Title: Storytelling Yoga with Radhika Sanghani
Teaser: Take a moment for some calm with author Radhika Sanghani in a playful storytelling movement session that will get you stretching, breathing, and using your imagination!…
Description: Take a moment for some calm with author Radhika Sanghani in a playful storytelling movement session that will get you stretching, breathing, and using your imagination! Yogis big and small are invited to connect with their body, release tension, be active, and have some fun. This is all about moving creatively on your yoga mat, being imaginative with your movements and allowing time to express yourself. Please bring your own mat.

Title: Together We Repair
Teaser: We believe that everyone has a story to tell and that stories help us make sense of our world. We've challenged local writers and poets, this year, to respond to 2025's Festival theme: Repair. Join us as we bring them together to perform their work: a…
Description: We believe that everyone has a story to tell and that stories help us make sense of our world. We've challenged local writers and poets, this year, to respond to 2025's Festival theme: Repair. Join us as we bring them together to perform their work: a patchwork of ideas on how to make the world a better place. Today featuring writing and performances from Intercultural Youth Scotland.

Title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
Teaser: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Appearing today: Mama G…
Description: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Appearing today: Mama G.

Title: David Baddiel: A Family Affair
Teaser: My Family: The Memoir sees writer, comedian, and documentarian David Baddiel adapt his hit stand-up show into prose…
Description: My Family: The Memoir sees writer, comedian, and documentarian David Baddiel adapt his hit stand-up show into prose. It's a frank, very funny look at his middle-class Jewish upbringing in London, including his mother's decades ­long affair with a golfing memorabilia salesman and the poignancy of his father's dementia. The Guardian says the book 'engagingly overshares' - expect much more of that and Baddiel's familiar wit in this energetic conversation.

Title: Elaine Feeney: Writing What You Know
Teaser: Booker Prize-longlisted Elaine Feeney is steeped in poetry and storytelling, and echoes of her west of Ireland origins resonate throughout her work. Today hear an author whose characters create shadow histories that stand as a corrective to received…
Description: Booker Prize-longlisted Elaine Feeney is steeped in poetry and storytelling, and echoes of her west of Ireland origins resonate throughout her work. This remains true of her latest novel, Let Me Go Mad in My Own Way, a clear-eyed and deep-hearted family tale centred around a woman whose past returns to disrupt her present. Today hear an author whose characters create shadow histories that stand as a corrective to received narratives

Title: José Pizarro: Redefining Spanish Cooking
Teaser: Legendary chef José Pizarro is an icon of Spanish cuisine in the UK. Today he chats to us about his passion for fresh, quality produce prepared with simplicity and lashings of enthusiasm…
Description: Legendary chef José Pizarro is an icon of Spanish cuisine in the UK. As the man who turned Brindisa into a gastronomic sensation before opening his own beloved eateries, there are few that are better placed to showcase the incredible culinary variety of his homeland. Today he chats about his newest title, The Spanish Pantry, and his passion for fresh, quality produce prepared with simplicity and lashings of enthusiasm. Chaired by Sophie Moxon.

Title: Discover the Secrets of Bees with Ben Hoare
Teaser: Become a pollinator pro in this fabulouzzzzz event with bee-fanatic and author of The Secrets of Bees, Ben Hoare. With his bee-rilliant science facts, Ben will get you to THINK BIG about these small but incredible creatures. Bee prepared to get buzzing……
Description: Become a pollinator pro in this fabulouzzzzz event with bee-fanatic and author of The Secrets of Bees, Ben Hoare. With his bee-rilliant science facts, Ben will get you to THINK BIG about these small but incredible creatures. Bee prepared to get buzzing, bust some bee myths, and take part in amazzzzing games as you learn all about why our planet would be in a sticky situation without bees. (Hive you had enough of our bee puns yet?)

Title: Old Town Bookshop Tour: Meander and Mingle with the Bookshop Crawl UK
Teaser: Amid the crowds and chaos of Edinburgh in August, does calmly exploring the city’s Old Town and quaint bookshops with likeminded people sound more like your cup of tea? If so, we’ve got the perfect tour for you…
Description: Amid the crowds and chaos of Edinburgh in August, does calmly exploring the city’s Old Town and quaint bookshops with likeminded people sound more like your cup of tea? If so, we’ve got the perfect tour for you. Join our partners the Bookshop Crawl UK on a specially curated walking tour, where you’ll meander through cobbled streets, browse a range of local bookshops, and mingle with fellow readers – with some special treats along the way!

Title: Repair Skills Workshop with EFI Makerspace
Teaser: Sharpen your technical repair skills under the guidance of the EFI Makerspace team and learn how 3D printing can be used as a method to repair…
Description:
Sharpen your technical repair skills under the guidance of the EFI Makerspace team. Learn how to use 3D modelling (in Tinkercad) and 3D printing as a method to repair or replace broken parts more cheaply than expensive replacements. Then turn to textiles repair, using your hands and sewing machines to learn new skills!

	Please note: If possible attendees should bring their own laptop devices for use in the workshop session, a limited amount of devices will be available for use if you cannot provide your own.

Title: Close Read with Open Book: Poetry and Repair
Teaser: Join Marjorie Lotfi and Claire Urquhart from Open Book, a charity organising shared reading and creative writing groups, as they lead a warm, lively discussion on a selection of poems that chime with our 2025 Festival theme of Repair…
Description: Join Marjorie Lotfi and Claire Urquhart from Open Book, a charity organising shared reading and creative writing groups, as they lead a warm, lively discussion on a selection of poems that chime with our 2025 Festival theme of Repair. Explore language's healing potential and how the act of creating poetry can salve deep emotional hurt. Reading materials will be provided, no preparation required.

Title: Anita Anand & William Dalrymple: Looting, Repatriation, and All Things Empire
Teaser: Terrific storytellers and co-hosts of the Empire podcast series, Anita Anand and William Dalrymple are experts at getting to the heart of some of history's biggest power struggles. Today they ask what reparations mean in the context of empire?…
Description: Terrific storytellers and co-hosts of the Empire podcast series, Anita Anand and William Dalrymple look at the moral dilemmas raised by the History of the British Empire. Join them as they explore fascinating stories from imperial history, especially the role of the Scots and Irish in what was originally an English project. They also explore the tale of the the tale of the world's most famous diamond, the Koh-i-Noor, brought back to Britain by a Scot, Lord Dalhousie. Chaired by Bee Rowlatt.

Title: Who Will Be Remembered Here
Teaser: 2025 marks 30 years since the first major Pride event in Scotland, yet queer histories have existed for as long as Scotland has. who will be remembered here enlivens these histories through performances, films, and an anthology…
Description: 2025 marks 30 years since the first major Pride event in Scotland, yet queer histories have existed for as long as Scotland has. who will be remembered here enlivens these histories through performances, films, and an anthology. Project curators Lewis Hetherington and CJ Mahony join contributors Mae Diansangu and Harry Josephine Giles for a discussion of how we reconsider the stories of the past, and what it means to 'remember into the future'. Chaired by Gemma Cairney.

Title: Introduction to Graphic Novels: A Workshop with Lizzy Stewart
Teaser: Illustrator Lizzy Stewart (author of the breathtaking graphic novel Alison and genre-evading Walking Distance) introduces you today to the world of graphic storytelling. During this workshop, you'll look at character, finding inspiration, and the way…
Description: Illustrator Lizzy Stewart (author of the breathtaking graphic novel Alison and genre-evading Walking Distance) introduces you today to the world of graphic storytelling. During this workshop, you'll look at character, finding inspiration, and the way that time bends and stretches within a graphic novel or comic-book. All of this will come together in a short-form comic strip which might form the basis of your own future full-length masterpiece.

Title: A Year of Pride and Joy with Simon James Green & Mama G
Teaser: A Year of Pride and Joy with Simon James Green & Mama G…
Description: Discover beloved contemporary LGBTQ+ figures and their remarkable achievements with award-winning author Simon James Green and pantomime dame Mama G in this joyous event spotlighting A Year of Pride and Joy. There are loads of reasons to feel hopeful for the future and Simon and Mama G invite you to share laughter, power, and joy in this uplifting event where we’ll celebrate our life passions and bring together our own voices.

Title: Singing and Stories with Mr Men Little Miss
Teaser: Join storyteller George in a gentle Mr. Men Little Miss story journey. Perfect for young children, you’ll find lots of live music, nursery rhymes, sensory participation, action, and movement – and classic characters from the much-loved Mr. Men Little…
Description: Join storyteller George in a gentle Mr. Men Little Miss story journey. Perfect for young children, you’ll find lots of live music, nursery rhymes, sensory participation, action, and movement – and classic characters from the much-loved Mr. Men Little Miss universe. Get ready to dance, play, and join in with the fun.

Title: Penny Johnson & Raja Shehadeh: What We Choose To Remember
Teaser: What do the physical memorials of the past and how they are remembered tell us about the ongoing conflicts of today?…
Description: What do the physical memorials of the past and how they are remembered tell us about the ongoing conflicts of today? Discussing Forgotten: Searching for Palestine’s Hidden Places and Lost Memorials, lawyer, writer, and human rights activist Raja Shehadeh and writer and researcher Penny Johnson will explore the landscape of Israel and Palestine to show how monuments which have been created, maintained, or neglected map the political and cultural struggles which fragment the land today. Chaired by Mahmoud Muna.

Title: Esther Freud: Excavating the Intimate
Teaser: More than 30 years after her indelible debut, Hideous Kinky, Esther Freud brings us her 10th novel, My Sister and Other Lovers: a scalpel-sharp exploration of intrafamilial intimacies, concerning a mother and two daughters…
Description: More than 30 years after her indelible debut, Hideous Kinky, Esther Freud brings us her 10th novel, My Sister and Other Lovers: a scalpel-sharp exploration of intrafamilial intimacies, concerning a mother and two daughters. We all live these kinds of stories, day in, day out: love, family, fear, longing, secrets, mistrust. We talk today to a novelist at the peak of her powers about how she captures the universal with such compassion. Chaired by Lennie Goodings.

Title: Songs for Ghosts with Clara Kumagai
Teaser: Clara Kumagai made her mark on the YA scene last year with the popular Catfish Rolling, a Yoto Carnegie Medal nominee. Now she’s back, with a beautiful tale of identity, heritage, and memory, Songs for Ghosts, inspired by Puccini’s Madame Butterfly…
Description: Clara Kumagai made her mark on the YA scene last year with the popular Catfish Rolling, a Yoto Carnegie Medal nominee. Now she’s back, with a beautiful tale of identity, heritage, and memory, Songs for Ghosts, inspired by Puccini’s Madame Butterfly. A hundred years separate Japanese-American teenager Adam and a young Japanese woman who are caught between cultures, relationships, and heartbreak. Clara will share this contemporary ghost story today with Alice Tarbuck.

Title: Roland Allen & Hattie Crisell: The Writer and the Page
Teaser: Two authors compare notes today on the act of writing. What does this human desire to put words down tell us about ourselves?…
Description: Two authors compare notes today on the act of writing. Roland Allen’s The Notebook deep dives into the history of this humble invention, providing a tantalising glimpse into the privately recorded thoughts of some of history’s finest intellects. Meanwhile, Hattie Crisell’s In Writing uncovers the mysteries of the creative process through interviews with our most-read contemporary writers. What does this human desire to put words down tell us about ourselves?

Title: Hidden Depths with Chloe Savage
Teaser: Dive in with author Chloe Savage as she takes you on a journey to discover what’s lurking in the deepest, darkest, depths of the ocean. Inspired by her latest book, The Search for Carmella…
Description: Dive in with author Chloe Savage as she takes you on a journey to discover what’s lurking in the deepest, darkest, depths of the ocean. Inspired by her latest book, The Search for Carmella – about a marine biologist who goes looking for a giant sea creature called Carmella – Chloe will encourage curiosity as you explore the incredible creatures that live at the bottom of the sea.

Title: Lucy Rose & Emma van Straaten: Beneath the Surface
Teaser: Obsession. Desire. Rage. Emotions women are expected to swallow and hide from the world. But rather than disappearing, they instead bubble away under the surface…
Description: Obsession. Desire. Rage. Emotions women are expected to swallow and hide from the world. But rather than disappearing, they instead bubble away under the surface until they inevitably explode out with dangerous force. This struggle between society’s rules and the reality of feeling is prevalent in both Lucy Rose’s twisting horror, The Lamb, and Emma van Straaten’s disquieting This Immaculate Body. Join them for a tantalising discussion about obsession, deception, and primal emotion. Chaired by Catherine Wilson Garry.

Title: Bring Your Imagination to Life with Will Sliney
Teaser: Join Marvel comic book artist and SkyKids TV star Will Sliney for an out-of-this-world interactive event! Get ready for Will to take you through a step-by-step droid draw-along and share some artistic tips and tricks. Inspired by his book, Draw with Will…
Description: Join Marvel comic book artist and SkyKids TV star Will Sliney for an out-of-this-world interactive event! Get ready for Will to take you through a step-by-step droid draw-along and share some artistic tips and tricks. Inspired by his book, Draw with Will, which will see you fighting aliens, creating spaceships, and inventing your very own creatures, this event will prove that anyone can draw – you just need imagination.

Title: Charlotte Philby: Dirty Money
Teaser: As the granddaughter of notorious Russian double agent Kim Philby, Charlotte Philby knows a thing or two about mysteries. But her detective ­duo novel, Dirty Money, isn't like other crime-solving fiction: there are two women at the helm…
Description: As the granddaughter of notorious Russian double agent Kim Philby, Charlotte Philby knows a thing or two about mysteries. But her detective ­duo novel, Dirty Money, isn't like other crime-solving fiction: there are two women at the helm. Philby joins us at this thrilling event to discuss writing strong female protagonists, her writing influences, and how her family ties drew her to the detective genre.

Title: Words from the Wards: The Exhibition
Teaser: Following the success of the Words from the Wards project, we worked with Edinburgh College of Art students to illustrate the collected stories. Join us to view the stories and illustrations side by side in our new festival gallery…
Description: Last year, through our Words from the Wards project, we asked the people of Edinburgh to share stories about the former Royal Infirmary, to honour the experiences and memories that people connect with the building’s previous life. Following the success of the project, we worked with Edinburgh College of Art students to illustrate the collected stories. Join us to view the stories and illustrations side by side in our new festival gallery.

Title: Being Your True Self with Dean Atta
Teaser: Shortlisted for the Waterstones Children’s Book Prize for his first novel, Black Flamingo, Dean Atta is back at this year’s Festival with his new coming-of-age tale, I Can’t Even Think Straight. Join us today as we chat to Dean about navigating the world…
Description: Shortlisted for the Waterstones Children’s Book Prize for his first novel, Black Flamingo, Dean Atta is back at this year’s Festival with his new coming-of-age tale, I Can’t Even Think Straight. Written in Dean’s whip-smart style, this verse novel centres on Kai, his decision to come out, and his relationship with his best friend who doesn’t feel ready to do the same. Join us today as Eilidh Akilade chats to Dean about navigating the world as a queer teenager.

Title: Neil Ansell: The Edge of Silence
Teaser: Today Ansell talks to us about becoming critically attuned to listening to the natural world and how he has learned to separate their sounds from commotion of everyday life…
Description: For nature writer Neil Ansell, author of the Wainwright Prize and Highland Book Prize shortlisted The Circling Sky, progressive hearing loss was a spur to hunt down nature’s rarest and most beautiful sounds while he still can, as documented in his new book The Edge of Silence. Today Ansell talks to us about becoming critically attuned to listening to the natural world and how he has learned to separate their sounds from commotion of everyday life. Chaired by Christina Riley.

Title: The Monsters Inside Our Head with Josh Silver & Andy Darcy Theo
Teaser: Hear BookTok star, Andy Darcy Theo (author of the bestselling series The Light That Blinds Us) and YA Book Prize-shortlisted Josh Silver (mental health nurse and author of Trauma/and) discuss how fantasy writing can help us better understand our mental…
Description: Some of the scariest monsters are the ones inside our heads. Hear BookTok star, Andy Darcy Theo (author of the bestselling series The Light That Blinds Us) and YA Book Prize-shortlisted Josh Silver (mental health nurse and author of Trauma/and) discuss how fantasy writing can help us better understand our mental health. Join them to fight the monsters at this uplifting event. Chaired by Yassmin Abdel-Magied.

Title: Creating the Sad Ghost Club with Lize Meddings
Teaser: Join author-illustrator Lize Meddings as she chats about her Sad Ghost Club journey and shows you how to draw your own sad ghost too…
Description: It all started with an idea – an idea to create a place where anyone feeling sad or lonely could come to feel less alone. Now, it’s a community of nearly 600,000 people, a graphic novel series, and a way of thinking that helps repair old wounds and spark joy. Join author-illustrator Lize Meddings as she chats about her Sad Ghost Club journey and shows you how to draw your own sad ghost too. Chaired by Victoria Murray.

Title: Lara Pawson: Object Lessons
Teaser: A timer, a toaster, a squirrel, a toenail – the reviews all agree: after reading Lara Pawson’s electrifying Goldsmith’s Prize-shortlisted Spent Light, you’ll never look at ordinary objects the same way again…
Description: A timer, a toaster, a squirrel, a toenail – the reviews all agree: after reading Lara Pawson’s electrifying Goldsmith’s Prize-shortlisted Spent Light, you’ll never look at ordinary objects the same way again. In the words of her narrator, ‘Everything in this damned world calls for indignation.’ Pawson talks with us about her startling, unconstrained novel and the web of violent and beautiful associations encoded in all things.

Title: Isabel Allende: Identity and Destiny
Teaser: Today, Isabel Allende joins us remotely for an unmissable conversation about her life in letters, and her triumphant return to the multi-generational saga, My Name is Emilia del Valle…
Description: Isabel Allende (appearing remotely) is one of world literature’s luminaries, winning international acclaim more than 40 years ago with her iconic debut, The House of Spirits. Today, she joins us remotely for an unmissable conversation about her life in letters, and her triumphant return to the multi-generational saga, My Name is Emilia del Valle. This unforgettable novel of love, war, and redemption features a restless young Chilean-American writer uncovering family (and personal) truths in an unfamiliar homeland. Chaired by Bee Rowlatt.

Title: Irvine Welsh: The Second Summer of Love
Teaser: With its long-anticipated Trainspotting sequel, Men in Love, the gang ‘come up’ again during the anarchic, decadent peak of late 80s/early 90s rave culture. Edinburgh icon Welsh joins us to pose the timely question: is love really the drug all men crave?…
Description: In 1993, Irvine Welsh wrote Trainspotting – a novel that became a cultural moment, giving us the era-defining Renton, Spud, Sick Boy, and Begbie. With its long-anticipated sequel, Men in Love, the gang ‘come up’ again during the anarchic, decadent peak of late 80s/early 90s rave culture. But this time, they’re getting their kicks elsewhere. Edinburgh icon Welsh joins us to pose the timely question: is love really the drug all men crave? Chaired by Nicola Meighan.

Title: Thought Exercise: Barbara Demick
Teaser: Dig deeper with our Thought Exercise series. Hear from experts on urgent issues of our time, then join in on the discussion during a wide-ranging, interactive exchange…
Description: Dig deeper with our Thought Exercise series. Hear from experts on urgent issues of our time, then join in on the discussion during a wide-ranging, interactive exchange. Today’s guest is multi-award-winning journalist, Barbara Demick (Nothing to Envy, Daughters of the Bamboo Grove), who has extensive experience covering authortitarian regimes in China and North Korea, and the unfolding political situation in America under Trump. Together, discuss how the rise of authoritarianism makes journalists’ role of providing good information both more perilous – and crucial. Chaired by Amina Shah.

Title: Poppy Okotcha & Kathy Slack: Repair – Gardens and Beings
Teaser: The theme for this year's Festival is Repair, and in a world seeking restoration, Poppy Okotcha and Kathy Slack offer a path towardshealing through the garden…
Description: The theme for this year's Festival is Repair, and in a world seeking restoration, Poppy Okotcha and Kathy Slack offer a path towardshealing through the garden. In both A Wilder Way and Rough Patch, they delve into the transformative power of regenerative practices, from nurturing soil to fostering community. With Leonie Bell, they discuss how tending to the Earth cultivates repair within ourselves, and the opportunity to reconnect with the wider world.

Title: Caroline Eden & Monisha Rajesh: The Track Less Travelled
Teaser: All aboard for two globe-spanning journeys! The authors discuss their wondrous travelogues and what they learned along the way with Dan Richards…
Description: All aboard for two globe-spanning journeys! Cold Kitchen author Caroline Eden returns to the Festival with Green Mountains, tasting her way from Armenia, across Georgia, and ending at the Black Sea. Meanwhile, Around the World in 80 Trains author Monisha Rajesh continues her travels in Moonlight Express, this time travelling by sleepers through Norway, Peru, and Pakistan. The authors discuss their wondrous travelogues and what they learned along the way with Dan Richards.

Title: YA Book Prize 2025: Meet the Shortlisted Writers
Teaser: Meet the incredible authors shortlisted for 2025’s YA Book Prize…
Description:
Meet the incredible authors shortlisted for 2025’s YA Book Prize. The award is organised by The Bookseller, and previous winners include Lex Croucher for Gwen and Art Are Not in Love, Danielle Jawando for When Our Worlds Collided, and Alice Oseman for Loveless. As always, this year's winners will be decided by a panel of experts and teenage judges. Come along to hear from some of the best voices in YA today including Faridah Àbíké-Íyímídé, Adiba Jaigirdar, and O.R. Sorrel. (Note: this event takes place twice, with different shortlisted authors appearing each time.) Chaired by Lynsey Rogers.

	This is a Schools event that is available for livestream only.

Title: At What Point with Caitlin O'Ryan
Teaser: Last year, Caitlin O’Ryan’s poem about walking home alone, ‘At What Point’, went viral – her poems have since been shared by the likes of Jameela Jamil, Natasha Bedingfield, and Sarah Cox. Now, her new collection of the same title arrives onto the poetry…
Description:
Age guidance: 18+

	Last year, Caitlin O’Ryan’s poem about walking home alone, ‘At What Point’, went viral – her poems have since been shared by the likes of Jameela Jamil, Natasha Bedingfield, and Sarah Cox. Now, her new collection of the same title arrives onto the poetry scene, focusing on the female experience and society’s expectations. Join Caitlin as she shares her shattering insights with fellow poet, Hollie McNish, and they both try putting the world to rights.

Title: Disrupting the Narrative – A Performance
Teaser: Do you think you know Edinburgh? What about the parts of its story it prefers to conceal? This theatrical poetry performance from Edinburgh's former Makar Hannah Lavery alongside fellow poets Jeda Pearl, Shasta Hanif Ali, Niall Moorjani, and Alycia…
Description: Do you think you know Edinburgh? What about the parts of its story it prefers to conceal? This theatrical poetry performance from Edinburgh's former Makar Hannah Lavery alongside fellow poets Jeda Pearl, Shasta Hanif Ali, Niall Moorjani, and Alycia Pirmohamed, illuminates the hidden history of the city, its institutions, and its people. Set to music by composer Niroshini Thambar, and featuring evocative images from photographer Kat Gollock, your understanding of Edinburgh will be changed forever by this special event. Originally commissioned by Push the Boat Out, with support from Edinburgh 900.

Title: Emma Forrest & Emma Jane Unsworth: The Messy Glory of Youth
Teaser: Join the authors of these gutsy, vivacious novels for a lively discussion with Nyla Ahmad on the fearless nature of obsession and the bruising reality of teenage infatuation…
Description: Emma Forrest's Father Figure sketches a larger-than-life portrait of a smart, impulsive young woman as she embarks on an ill-advised affair with a school friend's father. Meanwhile, in Slags, Emma Jane Unsworth's fictional sisters take a whisky-fuelled roadtrip, trying to unpick the missteps of their teenage years. Join the authors of these gutsy, vivacious novels for a lively discussion with Nyla Ahmad on the fearless nature of obsession and the bruising reality of teenage infatuation.

Title: Alice Mah & Madeleine Watts: Tragedies and Miracles
Teaser: Two writers grappling with our ties, commitments, and inheritance in the wake of environmental catastrophe come together to discuss their compelling new books with Caoilinn Hughes…
Description: Two writers grappling with our ties, commitments, and inheritance in the wake of environmental catastrophe come together to discuss their compelling new books with Caoilinn Hughes. Alice Mah's memoir, Red Pockets, traces her own journey from South China to Scotland, and Madeleine Watts's novel, Elegy, Southwest, traces a young couple's journey through a blasted America. Hear both authors reflecting on what debts we owe - to our ancestors, our past relationships, even ourselves?

Title: Geoff Dyer: Stories from a Vanished Time
Teaser: Post-war Britain can seem increasingly distant, yet Geoff Dyer's delightful new memoir, Homework, brings it back to life with verve and wit. Recalling his working-class Cheltenham childhood of the SOs and 60s, Dyer (a Fellow of the Royal Society of…
Description: Post-war Britain can seem increasingly distant, yet Geoff Dyer's delightful new memoir, Homework, brings it back to life with verve and wit. Recalling his working-class Cheltenham childhood of the SOs and 60s, Dyer (a Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature, known for his prize-winning range) joins Charlotte Higgins to discuss coming of age, the floods of change, and how the pivotal influence of grammar school altered his life's trajectory.

Title: Words from the Wards: The Exhibition
Teaser: Following the success of the Words from the Wards project, we worked with Edinburgh College of Art students to illustrate the collected stories. Join us to view the stories and illustrations side by side in our new festival gallery…
Description: Last year, through our Words from the Wards project, we asked the people of Edinburgh to share stories about the former Royal Infirmary, to honour the experiences and memories that people connect with the building’s previous life. Following the success of the project, we worked with Edinburgh College of Art students to illustrate the collected stories. Join us to view the stories and illustrations side by side in our new festival gallery.

Title: Open Book Shared Reading
Teaser: Join Open Book Lead Readers for an informal and relaxed shared reading session. Each session will explore a chapter from a de but book from this year's Festival programme. No experience necessary, all reading materials will be provided on the day…
Description: Join Open Book Lead Readers for an informal and relaxed shared reading session. Each session will explore a chapter from a debut book from this year's Festival programme. No experience necessary, all reading materials will be provided on the day.

Title: Find the Liar
Teaser: Get your best poker face on, and don your Traitors-style cloak, to sniff out the liar amongst you in this uproarious game, led by thriller author Cynthia Murphy…
Description: Get your best poker face on, and don your Traitors-style cloak, to sniff out the liar amongst you in this uproarious game, led by thriller author Cynthia Murphy.

Title: Devi Sridhar: Health For All
Teaser: What's the key to a longer, healthier life? Is the answer in self-help books and disciplined individual optimisation, or should we be holding governments to account for their policies on everything from pandemic preparedness to water treatment?…
Description: What's the key to a longer, healthier life? Is the answer in self-help books and disciplined individual optimisation, or should we be holding governments to account for their policies on everything from pandemic preparedness to water treatment? Edinburgh University's Personal Chair of Global Health Devi Sridhar (who became a household name during the pandemic), believes it's the latter, as she makes clear in today's no-nonsense conversation about How Not to Die (Too Soon). Chaired by Isabel Hardman.

Title: Kintsugi as Repair: A Workshop with Halle O’Neal
Teaser: In Japanese culture, there's a philosophy that imperfections should be embraced, and this is embodied in the centuries-old art of kintsugi, in which gold lacquer is used to repair ceramics. Rather than hiding the cracks, this visible act of mending…
Description: In Japanese culture, there's a philosophy that imperfections should be embraced, and this is embodied in the centuries-old art of kintsugi, in which gold lacquer is used to repair ceramics. Rather than hiding the cracks, this visible act of mending illuminates them, creating something beautiful out of what was once broken. Capturing imaginations across the world, this is your chance to absorb the history of kintsugi and its modern evolution with artist and academic Halle O'Neal as you enact the practice yourself. Kintsugi kits provided.

Title: Julie Farrell, Elizabeth Kellingley & Cat Mitchell: Towards an Inclusive Future
Teaser: Author and Inklusion Guide co­founder, Julie Farrell, senior Publishing lecturer at the University of Derby, Cat Mitchell, and Elizabeth Kellingley, access manager at Bloomsbury discuss the impact of their collective disability activism on authors…
Description: Diversity and inclusion are hot topics, but are we making headway or is it lip service? Author and Inklusion Guide co­founder, Julie Farrell, senior Publishing lecturer at the University of Derby, Cat Mitchell, and Elizabeth Kellingley, access manager at Bloomsbury discuss the impact of their collective disability activism on authors, readers, employees, and organisations. Join them to hear about the creation of the new UK Disability Network and their exciting plans for an inclusive future.

Title: Gubsmacked presents Flyte Nyte 2025
Teaser: Like the modern rap battle, ‘flytings’ flourished in 15th century Scotland as a form of entertainment, and as a means of garnering respect, attention, and speaking truth to power. Today, GUBSMACKED presents the dazzlingly rude and boisterous Flyte Nyte 20…
Description:
Like the modern rap battle, ‘flytings’ flourished in 15th century Scotland as a form of entertainment, and as a means of garnering respect, attention, and speaking truth to power. Today, GUBSMACKED presents the dazzlingly rude and boisterous Flyte Nyte 2025! Colin Bramwell, Iona Lee, and Leyla Josephine host poets, rappers, and spoken word artists all fighting to become the first Flyting Champion using nothing but wit, verse, extravagant verbal abuse, and name-calling – highbrow it isnae!

	The line up will feature:

	Joelle Taylor versus Hannah Lavery
	Michael Mullen versus Ross McLeary
	Bee Asha versus Kate Ireland
	Amelia Baylor versus Darren Connell

Title: Adam Alexander, Andy Hamilton & Mo Wilde: Wild Solutions
Teaser: From foraging to seed saving, and the joy of rediscovering nature, Adam Alexander, Andy Hamilton, and Mo Wilde offer practical wisdom and philosophical insights. Join them for a wide-ranging discussion about how cultivating a deeper connection with…
Description: From foraging to seed saving, and the joy of rediscovering nature, Adam Alexander and Mo Wilde offer practical wisdom and philosophical insights. Alexander's The Accidental Seed Heroes, Hamilton's New Wild Order, and Wilde's Free Food each offer a unique perspective on our relationship with the natural world. Join them for a wide-ranging discussion about how cultivating a deeper connection with nature might be the key to saving us all. Chaired by Hannah Rudman.

Title: Scots Rhymetime with Craigmillar Books for Babies
Teaser: Join Craigmillar Books for Babies with a special Scots Rhymetime! Enjoy Scots rhymes, songs, lots of cuddles, and fun to support attachment and bonding with your wee ones…
Description: Join Craigmillar Books for Babies with a special Scots Rhymetime! Enjoy Scots rhymes, songs, lots of cuddles, and fun to support attachment and bonding with your wee ones.

Title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
Teaser: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Appearing today: Joseph Coelho…
Description: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Appearing today: Joseph Coelho.

Title: You're Invited to Acorn Wood!
Teaser: It’s time for a dance in Acorn Wood! Join Hare and all her friends for a party to remember as we celebrate 25 years of the beloved interactive board book series by iconic duo, author Julia Donaldson and illustrator Axel Scheffler…
Description: It’s time for a dance in Acorn Wood! Join Hare and all her friends for a party to remember as we celebrate 25 years of the beloved interactive board book series by iconic duo, author Julia Donaldson and illustrator Axel Scheffler. There will be fun with stories, rhymes, and songs – and maybe even a visit from Postman Bear.

Title: Gurnaik Johal & Madeleine Thien: Places in Flux
Teaser: Take imaginative flight with two international novelists whose work takes us to truly marvellous realms…
Description: Take imaginative flight with two international novelists whose work takes us to truly marvellous realms. Gurnaik Johal (Somerset Maugham Award-winner for story collection, We Move) presents his debut novel, Saraswati, where a mythical holy river flowing again causes personal and political turmoil. Meanwhile, Madeleine Thien’s philosophical The Book of Records sees a woman and her father arrive at the Sea: a fantastical place containing intellectual migrants and refugees from throughout history. In conversation with Dina Nayeri.

Title: Chris Chibnall: From Broadchurch to the White Hart
Teaser: What do you do when you hand over the reins as showrunner of Doctor Who, one of the most high-profile jobs in British TV? In Chris Chibnall’s case, you write your debut crime thriller, Death at The White Hart…
Description: What do you do when you hand over the reins as showrunner of Doctor Who, one of the most high-profile jobs in British TV? In Chris Chibnall’s case, you write your debut crime thriller, Death at The White Hart, a mystery about a big city detective moving back to Dorset to investigate a pub landlord’s savage murder. As the creator of the similarly rural hit series, Broadchurch, it’s a genre Chibnall knows a thing or two about. Chaired by Denise Mina.

Title: Repair Skills Workshop with EFI Makerspace
Teaser: Sharpen your technical repair skills under the guidance of the EFI Makerspace team and learn how to use 3D printing as a method to repair…
Description:
Sharpen your technical repair skills under the guidance of the EFI Makerspace team. Learn how to use 3D modelling (in Tinkercad) and 3D printing as a method to repair or replace broken parts more cheaply than expensive replacements. Then turn to textiles repair, using your hands and sewing machines to learn new skills!

	Please note: If possible attendees should bring their own laptop devices for use in the workshop session, a limited amount of devices will be available for use if you cannot provide your own.

Title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
Teaser: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers. Appearing today: Jill Calder…
Description: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers.Appearing today: Jill Calder.

Title: First Edition: Once Upon a Time in Holyrood
Teaser: Start your day with the facts. In our First Edition events you can join leading journalists from across the media (and the world) as they discuss the day's breaking news over a cup of coffee…
Description: Start your day with the facts. High quality, thorough, and trustworthy journalism has never been more important in helping us understand the world as it really is, so in our First Edition events you can join leading journalists from across the media (and the world) as they discuss the day's breaking news over a cup of coffee. Today's guests are Shona Craven, Kenny Farquharson and Peter MacMahon. Chaired by Jemma Neville.

Title: Chris Bryant: A Life Less Ordinary
Teaser: Winner of the 2020 Parliamentary Book Award for Best Non-Fiction and the first MP to celebrate his civil partnership in the Palace of Westminster, Chris Bryant brings his candid new memoir, A Life and a Half, to this year’s Festival…
Description: Winner of the 2020 Parliamentary Book Award for Best Non-Fiction and the first MP to celebrate his civil partnership in the Palace of Westminster, Chris Bryant brings his candid new memoir, A Life and a Half, to this year’s Festival. From his years as an Anglican priest to his upbringing with an alcoholic mother, Bryant doesn’t shy away from the challenges of his life. He joins us to discuss the darkness, joy, and headiness of his formative years. Chaired by Peter MacMahon.

Title: Torrey Peters Presents…
Teaser: In this exclusive Book Festival event, Torrey Peters – PEN/Hemingway Award-winning author of Detransition, Baby and the kaleidoscopic Stag Dance – co-curates performances from some of the most exciting trans writers and artists around…

Description: Presented by Edinburgh Futures Institute’s creative projects team. Poet Jennifer Williams, visual artist Jimmy Turner, academic Jo Balfour-Oatts, and facilitator Matjaz Vidmar invite you to consider impractical repairs of material objects. Exploring how we can repair objects with creative writing and sculpture, we’ll investigate how artistic and embodied ideas and techniques can help us to imagine positive futures, affecting present change. Please bring along a broken object with personal significance that you’d like to repair in this way.
