Title: Sara Sheridan: Feminism on the High Seas
Teaser: Beloved Scottish historical fiction writer Sara Sheridan's latest novel is a swashbuckling rollick of feminist fervour and seductive suspense…
Description: Beloved Scottish historical fiction writer Sara Sheridan's latest novel is a swashbuckling rollick of feminist fervour and seductive suspense. From civil war-torn Brazil to Georgian London, you'll be enchanted by the fierce heroine and enigmatic captain at the heart of On Starlit Seas. The author of The Fair Botanists (Waterstones Scottish Book of the Year 2022) talks today about combining creativity with history and diverse readings of historical facts. Chaired by Lin Anderson.

Title: Sue Lawrence: Secrets Unearthed
Teaser: We’re delighted to welcome prolific cookery writer, novelist, and journalist Sue Lawrence back with her latest enthralling historical novel, Whispers in the Glen…
Description: We’re delighted to welcome prolific cookery writer, novelist, and journalist Sue Lawrence back with her latest enthralling historical novel, Whispers in the Glen. Set across both World Wars, sisters Effie and Nell love each other dearly, but when a plane carrying British and Canadian soldiers crashes in their village, how far will they will go to keep secrets hidden from each other? Join Lawrence as she delves into this captivating story today. Chaired by Susan Mansfield.

Title: Elodie Harper: History’s Child
Teaser: In the aftermath of defeat, what kind of legacy did Boudicca, warrior queen and mastermind of one of history’s greatest revolts, leave her child?…
Description: In the aftermath of defeat, what kind of legacy did Boudicca, warrior queen and mastermind of one of history’s greatest revolts, leave her child? Today, Elodie Harper, bestselling author of the Wolf Den trilogy, launches her latest standalone novel, Boudicca’s Daughter, and talks to Dr Jean Menzies about her rapid rise to becoming one of Britain’s bestselling historical novelists.

Title: Olesya Khromeychuk & Jen Stout: Remembering Victoria Amelina
Teaser: Victoria Amelina was a Ukrainian novelist, literary festival curator, and, following Russia’s invasion, a war crimes investigator. Halfway through writing her nonfiction account of the war, Amelina was wounded in a Russian missile attack – days later…
Description: Victoria Amelina was a Ukrainian novelist, literary festival curator, and, following Russia’s invasion, a war crimes investigator. Halfway through writing her nonfiction account of the war, Amelina was wounded in a Russian missile attack – days later, she died of her injuries. In the aftermath, writers and friends came together to edit and assemble her manuscript, Looking at Women Looking at War. At the end of last year, Amelina was posthumously awarded a 2024 IPA Prix Voltaire Special Award, and the book won the 2025 Orwell Prize for Political Writing. Today, in conversation with Roxani Krystalli, Olesya Khromeychuk and Jen Stout pay moving tribute to Amelina’s extraordinary life and legacy.

Title: Pankaj Mishra: After Gaza, What Next?
Teaser: In the concise and pointed The World After Gaza, Pankaj Mishra uses the war in the Middle East as a starting point to examine the competing histories of the last century and how they’ve shaped differing political and moral imaginations…
Description: In the concise and pointed The World After Gaza, essayist and novelist Pankaj Mishra uses the war in the Middle East as a starting point to examine the competing histories of the last century and how they’ve shaped differing political and moral imaginations. From much of the world’s experience of slavery, colonialism, and decolonisation, to the West’s narratives of the triumphant defeat of 20th century totalitarianism and the spread of liberal capitalism, Mishra offers an unwavering analysis on how these memories are shaping the current moment, and how the balance of power is shifting. Join Mishra as he speaks with Gavin Francis about how new histories can orient us.

Title: Rachel Kushner: Profound and Wickedly Entertaining
Teaser: Rachel Kushner has called writing her Booker Prize-shortlisted novel Creation Lake 'the most fun I've ever had in my life'. She talks with Francisco Garcia today about reinventing the espionage novel, her obsession with Neanderthal genetics, and the…
Description: Rachel Kushner has called writing her Booker Prize-shortlisted novel Creation Lake 'the most fun I've ever had in my life'. Meet Sadie Smith, a sardonic, 30-something spy-for-hire sent to infiltrate a gang of radical eco-activists whose leader lives in a cave. But beneath this parodic spy novel lies a profound treatise on human history. Kushner talks with Francisco Garcia today about reinventing the espionage novel, her obsession with Neanderthal genetics, and the shortcomings of modern man.

Title: Grace Spence Green: Recovery and Radical Acceptance
Teaser: When a freak accident irreversibly changed Grace Spence Green’s life at just 22 years old, she developed a resilience she never thought possible. Join Spence Green, in conversation with Gavin Francis, to challenge the way we think about disability…
Description: When a freak accident irreversibly changed Grace Spence Green’s life at just 22 years old, she developed a resilience she never thought possible. In her extraordinary, life-affirming new work of non-fiction, To Exist as I Am, Spence Green shares her journey from a dedicated young medical student to a patient with a serious spinal injury, and what led her to become a vocal disability activist. Join Spence Green, in conversation with Gavin Francis, to challenge the way we think about disability.

Title: Dan Jones: A Heart-Pounding Finale
Teaser: We all have characters that stay with us long after we stop reading. So how does it feel when you've spent a decade writing characters, and the time comes to put that last full stop on the page? Dan Jones is finding out. Join the bestselling historian…
Description: We all have characters that stay with us long after we stop reading. So how does it feel when you've spent a decade writing characters, and the time comes to put that last full stop on the page? Dan Jones is finding out. Join the bestselling historian and novelist as he discusses Lion Hearts: the thrilling final instalment of Essex Dogs, his epic trilogy set during the Hundred Years War. Chaired by Alice Winn.

Title: Alisha Fernandez Miranda, Emma Gannon & Jessica Stanley: Love Undone
Teaser: Most romance novels are all about the happily ever after. But what happens when ever after doesn’t end up looking so… happy?…
Description: Most romance novels are all about the happily ever after. But what happens when ever after doesn’t end up looking so… happy? Today, Alisha Fernandez Miranda (Someone’s Gotta Give), Emma Gannon (Table for One), and Jessica Stanley (Consider Yourself Kissed) discuss how their new novels all focus on something far more beautiful: the messy relationship we have with ourselves. Chaired by Abigail Bergstrom.

Title: Shon Faye: Love Without Bounds
Teaser: In Love in Exile, Shon Faye (author of the acclaimed bestseller The Transgender Issue) explores what happens when we break the constraints of conventionality and embrace love in all its forms…
Description: In Love in Exile, Shon Faye (author of the acclaimed bestseller The Transgender Issue) explores what happens when we break the constraints of conventionality and embrace love in all its forms. Love, Faye argues, is as much a collective question as a personal one. This is a book of and for our times: for seeing and knowing love, in whatever form it takes. Join Faye today in what’s sure to be an unmissable conversation with Maggie Nelson.

Title: Ekow Eshun & Imaobong Umoren: New Empires
Teaser: Join Ekow Eshun and Imaobong Umoren for this timely, fascinating discussion about the continuing hold of colonialism on contemporary life…
Description: In Black Earth Rising – a compelling anthology of African, Latin American, and Native American artists – writer and broadcaster Ekow Eshun interweaves colonialism, climate crisis, and contemporary art. Meanwhile, London School of Economics associate professor Imaobong Umoren’s Empire Without End is an astute study of Britain’s involvement in the Caribbean, presenting her latest research on colonialism and empire. Join both authors for this timely, fascinating discussion about the continuing hold of colonialism on contemporary life. Chaired by Irenosen Okojie.

Title: Ash Sarkar: Immigrants Aren’t Eating Your Pets
Teaser: One of the left’s most prominent commentators, Ash Sarkar wades right into the middle of the culture wars in Minority Rule in hyper-intelligent, acid fashion…
Description: One of the left’s most prominent commentators, Ash Sarkar wades right into the middle of the culture wars in Minority Rule in hyper-intelligent, acid fashion. Join Heather Parry as Sarkar attempts to tear apart the modern morass of identity politics while also reckoning with some of her own long held views. The goal? To expose the minority that’s really screwing us over.

Title: Happy Hills with Sophy Henn
Teaser: Join the colourful, fun world of award-winning author-illustrator Sophy Henn as she shares Happy Hills: Mr Big Fluff Rules…
Description: Meet the happy and not-so-happy residents of Happy Hills – a place where anything can happen (and always does). Join the colourful, fun world of award-winning author-illustrator Sophy Henn as she shares Happy Hills: Mr Big Fluff Rules. She’ll help you create characters that you can turn into your very own comic strips. Expect lots of giggles and crazy creations along the way!

Title: Maggie Nelson: How Does a Body Connect with Itself?
Teaser: Maggie Nelson's intellectually nimble works of non-fiction (including The Argonauts) have earned her both Guggenheim and MacArthur Fellowships along with a reputation as one her generation's most versatile thinkers. Her latest work, Pathemata: Or, The…
Description: Maggie Nelson's intellectually nimble works of non-fiction (including The Argonauts) have earned her both Guggenheim and MacArthur Fellowships along with a reputation as one her generation's most versatile thinkers. Her latest work, Pathemata: Or, The Story of My Mouth, is a characteristically experimental reckoning with her own chronic pain, twisted through dreams and her restless imagination, the pandemic pulsing insistently in the background. Join Harry Josephine Giles for a fascinating conversation with one of America's most innovative writers.

Title: Edward Carey: Theatre of the Absurd
Teaser: The mutifaceted Edward Carey is a novelist, playwright, and illustrator whose creations have a Gothic sensibility, at once enchanting and unsettling. His eccentric new work, Edith Holler, tells the story of a young woman trapped in a theatre she believes…
Description: The mutifaceted Edward Carey is a novelist, playwright, and illustrator whose creations have a Gothic sensibility, at once enchanting and unsettling. His eccentric new work, Edith Holler, tells the story of a young woman trapped in a theatre she believes will crumble should she ever leave. Today Carey speaks to Hannah McGill about his characteristically unconventional love letter to the stage and those who write for it, and his multidisciplinary approach to writing.

Title: Sami Timimi: Searching for Normal
Teaser: The approach to both mental health and neurodivergence in clinical settings has changed enormously in the 30 years that Dr Sami Timimi has been a practicing psychiatrist…
Description: The approach to both mental health and neurodivergence in clinical settings has changed enormously in the 30 years that Dr Sami Timimi has been a practicing psychiatrist. His view is that this has not necessarily led to improved outcomes, but to an overall pathologisation of human emotion and behaviour. His new book Searching for Normal explores his perspective on the influence of, and at times unintended harms created by, the pharmaceutical industry, media, and psychiatric establishment. As overall societal attitudes and approaches to mental health change, Dr Timimi gives his radical view on these challenging and vital topics 'from the field'. Chaired by Gavin Francis.

Title: Freedom of Expression: The Long View
Teaser: The debate around freedom of expression feels more contested than ever. But the concept of freedom of expression in the arts is relatively recent, and it was only in 1968 that censorship of plays was abolished in Britain…
Description: The debate around freedom of expression feels more contested than ever. But the concept of freedom of expression in the arts is relatively recent, and it was only in 1968 that censorship of plays was abolished in Britain. Today's event takes a long and wide view of this fragile artistic right, and how it can be protected today. Panellists include influential sociologist and Chair of London Centre for the Humanities Richard Sennett; Labour politician and leading advocate for the creative industries Baroness Thangam Debbonaire; and distinguished poet and former Archbishop of Canterbury Rowan Williams.

Title: Mark Watson: One Minute Away
Teaser: Whether it's texting Greg Davies (almost) every day for a year for Taskmaster, podcasting, touring, or popping up in panel shows, comedian and writer Mark Watson goes at life full-pelt - just like delivery rider Damir in his new novel, One Minute Away…
Description: Whether it's texting Greg Davies (almost) every day for a year for Taskmaster, podcasting, touring, or popping up in panel shows, comedian and writer Mark Watson goes at life full-pelt - just like delivery rider Damir in his new novel, One Minute Away. When Damir's daily race through the city is stopped short by romantic serendipity, edamame beans are spilled and lives are changed. Join Watson today as he discusses love, modern life and what it means to be truly connected. Chaired by Zara Janjua.

Title: Partha Dasgupta: Valuing our World
Teaser: Today, Partha Dasgupta discusses his groundbreaking book On Natural Capital, advocating for why nature should be given the same economic value as the resources we extract from it…
Description: The New York Times called Cambridge economist Partha Dasgupta ‘the most important person you’ve never heard of’. Responsible for the fundamental shift in how we now approach the economics of biodiversity, he’s the author of a report commissioned by the UK Government setting out ways we must account for nature in economic decision-making. Today, he discusses his groundbreaking book On Natural Capital, advocating for why nature should be given the same economic value as the resources we extract from it. Chaired by Paul Behrens.

Title: Comic Chaos with Tom Percival
Teaser: Squirrel and Duck might seem strange housemates, but they are drawn together by their secret – they are the only talking animals in the world. Get ready for a wonderfully zany event with Tom Percival as he introduces Squirrel and Duck: Mission Improbable…
Description: Squirrel and Duck might seem strange housemates, but they are drawn together by their secret – they are the only talking animals in the world. Get ready for a wonderfully zany event with Tom Percival as he introduces Squirrel and Duck: Mission Improbable. Hear all about how they outwit bungling art thieves with only the help of a pet cactus! Tom will share his tips and tricks for off-the-wall stories and illustrations – and laugh-out-loud moments along the way!

Title: Jonathan Coe: Cosy Crime Meets Political Thriller
Teaser: The Independent called Jonathan Coe the 'funniest serious novelist' in Britain. In The Proof of My Innocence, a blistering political critique of a chaotic post-Brexit Britain gets wrapped up in a murder mystery featuring a trepidatious reporter, a…
Description: The Independent called Jonathan Coe the 'funniest serious novelist' in Britain. In The Proof of My Innocence, a blistering political critique of a chaotic post-Brexit Britain gets wrapped up in a murder mystery featuring a trepidatious reporter, a sinister Rightwing thinktank, and a literary enigma. The bestselling author of Middle England talks with Samuel Fisher about this riotous blend of satire, suspense, and crime caper.

Title: Joseph O’Connor: Beleaguered City
Teaser: International award-winning author Joseph O’Connor returns to the Festival with the next novel in his thrilling, historical Rome Escape Line series…
Description: International award-winning author Joseph O’Connor returns to the Festival with the next novel in his thrilling, historical Rome Escape Line series. In The Ghosts of Rome, the activists are on a mission to smuggle refugees to safety, until their work is compromised by the arrival of a mysterious parachutist – is he an ally or an imposter? O’Connor joins us to discuss his brilliant career as one of Ireland’s most prolific historical novelists.

Title: Talking About the Things That Matter with Munroe Bergdorf
Teaser: How do we talk about the really tough stuff? Luckily for us, Munroe Bergdorf is an expert in communicating across divides. The writer, activist, model, and contributing editor of British Vogue returns with her new book Talk to Me. Covering everything…
Description: How do we talk about the really tough stuff? Luckily for us, Munroe Bergdorf is an expert in communicating across divides. The writer, activist, model, and contributing editor of British Vogue returns with her new book Talk to Me. Covering everything from beauty standards to cancel culture, Bergdorf is here to guide us towards speaking our truths. Hear her reflect on the power of confident communication. Chaired by Anahit Behrooz.

Title: Torrey Peters: Dancing with Gender
Teaser: Torrey Peters’ bestselling novel Detransition, Baby burst onto shelves in 2021. Her follow-up, the vibrant and ambitious Stag Dance, waltzes across four breathtaking tales that explore the space between male and female, binary and non-binary, and delight…
Description: Torrey Peters’ bestselling novel Detransition, Baby burst onto shelves in 2021. Her follow-up, the vibrant and ambitious Stag Dance, waltzes across four breathtaking tales that explore the space between male and female, binary and non-binary, and delight in skipping between genres. By turns gruesome, romantic, unsettling, surprising, and always inventive, join Peters as she discusses her vivid celebration of queer and trans lives across place and time with Harry Josephine Giles.

Title: Deborah Frances-White: A Little More Conversation
Teaser: Podcaster, comedian, and bestselling author of The Guilty Feminist, Deborah Frances-White wants to know when we stopped talking and, more importantly, listening to each other…
Description: Podcaster, comedian, and bestselling author of The Guilty Feminist, Deborah Frances-White wants to know when we stopped talking and, more importantly, listening to each other. In Six Conversations We're Scared to Have, she considers the art of conversation and suggests it's time we agree to disagree. Join Frances-White for this funny, illuminating event that takes a deep-dive into topics such as freedom of speech, and explores ways to discuss the trickiest matters. Chaired by A C Grayling.

Title: Richard Lloyd Parry, Edward Wong & Yuan Yang: On East Asia
Teaser: From East China's geopolitical ambitions to South Korea's huge cultural influence and recent political turmoil, East Asia looms larger than ever in global news cycles. Yet beyond the headlines, how much do we understand these major international powers'…
Description: From East China's geopolitical ambitions to South Korea's huge cultural influence and recent political turmoil, East Asia looms larger than ever in global news cycles. Yet beyond the headlines, how much do we understand these major international powers' cultural and political contexts? This revelatory panel event features the Times' Asia editor, Richard Lloyd Parry; New York Times journalist and At the Edge of Empire author, Edward Wong; and author of 2025 Women's Prize for Non-Fiction-shortlisted Private Revolutions, Yuan Yang. Chaired by Isabel Hilton.

Title: Ivo Graham: The Glory and the Chaos
Teaser: Ivo Graham is a whirlwind of a man. A hugely popular comedian, club night DJ, podcast host, TaskMaster flop, and a father: he simply can’t do things by halves…
Description: Ivo Graham is a whirlwind of a man. A hugely popular comedian, club night DJ, podcast host, Taskmaster flop, and a father: he simply can’t do things by halves. Yardsticks for Failure lays bare Graham’s experience of living in chaos, and offers a gleeful glimpse behind the grubby curtain of stand-up into the bargain. There’s joy and accomplishment to revel in – but also abject failure, perpetual exhaustion, and several missed trains. But hey, life is all about balance… right? Chaired by Michael Pedersen.

Title: Sigrid Rausing: An Intertwining of Minds
Teaser: When celebrated Swedish author Johanna Ekström learned she was dying of cancer, she asked her friend Sigrid Rausing to distil 13 handwritten notebooks into one final published work. The result, And the Walls Became the World All Around, is a sublime…
Description: When celebrated Swedish author Johanna Ekström learned she was dying of cancer, she asked her friend Sigrid Rausing to distil 13 handwritten notebooks into one final published work. The result, And the Walls Became the World All Around, is a sublime, devastating ‘memoir in duet’ between deceased and survivor, a testament to friendship, and a haunting meditation on grief. Today, Rausing discusses her remarkable friend and this profound literary experiment with Caoilinn Hughes.

Title: Helen Carr & Lorna Hutson: Eras of Change
Teaser: Join two authors unpicking the grand narratives that have birthed the image of the British Isles. Helen Carr uncovers the untold stories of the 14th-century Plantagenet era in Sceptred Isle, while Lorna Hutson's England's Insular Imagining: The…
Description: Join two authors unpicking the grand narratives that have birthed the image of the British Isles. Helen Carr uncovers the untold stories of the 14th-century Plantagenet era - through revolution, plague, and social change - in Sceptred Isle, while Lorna Hutson's England's Insular Imagining: The Elizabethan Erasure of Scotland uses the idea of a 'sceptred isle' as a jumping off point to examine the inconvenient reality of Scotland for Elizabethan England. Hear both authors in conversation today with Joyce McMillan.

Title: Elly Griffiths: Cold Cases Stuck in Time
Teaser: Number one Sunday Times bestselling author of the Dr Ruth Galloway Mysteries, Elly Griffiths, returns with a brand new crime series. With 26 novels under her belt, how does Griffiths continue to keep her characters fresh, plot lines exciting, and twists…
Description: Number one Sunday Times bestselling author of the Dr Ruth Galloway Mysteries, Elly Griffiths, returns with a brand new crime series. With 26 novels under her belt, how does Griffiths continue to keep her characters fresh, plot lines exciting, and twists unexpected? Join us for this tantalising event as she sits down with Mary Paulson-Ellis to discuss The Frozen People, the first in a series where cold cases take centuries to solve.

Title: Lucy Easthope: Roadmaps for Resilience
Teaser: Explore the practical and philosophical dimensions of crisis response with Lucy Easthope, emergency planner and international advisor on disaster recovery…
Description: Explore the practical and philosophical dimensions of crisis response with Lucy Easthope, emergency planner and international advisor on disaster recovery. Her essential new book, Come What May, offers a framework for how we can respond when hit by life’s unexpected twists, turns, and troubles. Join this thought-provoking conversation between Easthope and Devi Sridhar about resilience, preparedness, and the human response to adversity. An important conversation under our Festival theme, Repair.

Title: Christopher de Bellaigue: Power and Politics in the Ottoman Empire
Teaser: Christopher de Bellaigue joins us today discussing the life of the feared 16th century Sultan, Suleyman the Magnificent, and his relevance to today’s Middle East…
Description: A foreign correspondent for the Economist and New Yorker in Turkey, Iraq, and Iran, Christopher de Bellaigue’s books showcase his expertise in Middle Eastern politics, past and present. The Telegraph called his book The Lion House ‘Wolf Hall for the Ottoman Empire’, and his latest, The Golden Throne, returns to that era. He joins us today, discussing the life of the feared 16th century Sultan, Suleyman the Magnificent, and his relevance to today’s Middle East. Chaired by Alex Pearson.

Title: Jonathan Watts: Dom Phillips’ How to Save the Amazon
Teaser: In 2022, while on a research trip for How to Save the Amazon, journalist Dom Phillips and Indigenous rights defender Bruno Pereira were murdered. In a show of solidarity, fuelled by their conviction that rigorous journalism must not be silenced…
Description: In 2022, while on a research trip for How to Save the Amazon, journalist Dom Phillips and Indigenous rights defender Bruno Pereira were murdered. In a show of solidarity, fuelled by their conviction that rigorous journalism must not be silenced, colleagues and supporters worked together to complete the book which tells the stories of rainforest defenders. Today we speak to Jonathan Watts, the Guardian's global environment editor, to celebrate Phillips' life and work. Chaired by Cal Flyn.

Title: Danny Sriskandarajah: People Have the Power
Teaser: This is an event for people who want to fight back against the unhappy narratives around them, with an author whose life and work emphasises taking action in difficult circumstances…
Description: This is an event for people who want to fight back against the unhappy narratives around them, with an author whose life and work emphasises taking action in difficult circumstances. Talking about Power to the People, New Economics Foundation CEO (and former Oxfam GB CEO) Danny Sriskandarajah discusses examples of and strategies for global citizen action, in order to deliver a society that works for the many and not for the few. Chaired by Liz Lloyd.

Title: Gordon Corera: The Spy in the Archive
Teaser: We are delighted to welcome journalist and writer Gordon Corera for a discussion about his new book, The Spy in the Archive: How One Man Tried to Kill the KGB…
Description:
Gordon Corera has spent over two decades covering intelligence, national security, cybersecurity, and risk. As the BBC's former Security Correspondent, he reported from all over the world, explaining the complex worlds of espionage, terrorism and geopolitics, and is the only journalist to have interviewed serving heads of both the CIA and MI6. And as the current co-host of the popular The Rest is Classified podcast, he has access to some of the most secretive organisations and agencies in the world and an uncanny ability to make complex, sometimes troubling information relevant, accessible, and entertaining.

	The author of several books, including The Art of Betrayal: The Secret History of MI6, and The Russians Among Us, his latest title, The Spy in the Archive: How One Man Tried to Kill the KGB, tells the remarkable story of how Vasili Mitrokhin – an introverted archivist who loved nothing more than dusty files – ended up changing the world. As the in-house archivist for the KGB, the secrets he was exposed to inside its walls turned him first into a dissident and then a spy, a traitor to his country but a man determined to expose the truth about the dark forces that had subverted Russia, forces still at work in the country today.

Title: Should Rivers Be Afforded Personhood?
Teaser: Around the world, a growing movement seeks to protect rivers by declaring them living beings entitled to fundamental rights. This vital, perspective-shifting panel - a cornerstone of our Repair theme - is chaired by Guardian environmental editor…
Description: Around the world, a growing movement seeks to protect rivers by declaring them living beings entitled to fundamental rights. With her petition to grant legal personhood to the Clyde, novelist Louise Welsh brought this campaign to Scotland. She's joined by Robert Macfarlane, whose latest book is a passionate treatise supporting this idea, and Monica Feria-Tinta, the pioneering barrister at the forefront of the climate justice movement. This vital, perspective-shifting panel - a cornerstone of our Repair theme - is chaired by Guardian environmental editor, Jonathan Watts.

Title: Mark Kermode & Jenny Nelson: The Sound of Movie Music
Teaser: Jaws, Indiana Jones, Jurassic Park… Would these movies be quite as iconic without their incredible scores? Journalist and broadcaster Mark Kermode, alongside writer and expert audio producer Jenny Nelson, are better placed than anyone to explore this…
Description: Jaws, Indiana Jones, Jurassic Park… Would these movies be quite as iconic without their incredible scores? Journalist, broadcaster and ultimate film authority, Mark Kermode, alongside writer and expert audio producer Jenny Nelson, are better placed than anyone to explore this question. Co-authors of Surround Sound: The Stories of Movie Music, they’ll discuss their shared passion for the craft of making music for movies and a composer’s ability to elevate a film from ‘great’ to ‘epic’.

Title: Dark Magic with Saara El-Arifi & Juno Dawson
Teaser: Bestselling authors Saara El-Arifi and Juno Dawson join us for an enthralling conversation about all things dark fantasy. Come along to delve into their otherworldly tales: Human Rites and Cursebound…
Description: Bestselling authors Saara El-Arifi and Juno Dawson join us for an enthralling conversation about all things dark fantasy. In Human Rites, Dawson’s hotly anticipated finale to the Her Majesty’s Coven series, we find a reunited but broken coven heading into a final battle between good and evil. In Cursebound, El-Arifi’s fantastical follow-up to Faebound, Queen of the Fae is declaring all-out war on the realm. Come along to delve into these otherworldly tales as they both chat to Irenosen Okojie.

Title: Joseph Jebelli: We Need to Calm Down
Teaser: When was the last time you stopped to rest and just let your mind wander? Well, if you need any encouragement to do that more, come hear neuroscientist Joseph Jebelli discussing the findings of his latest book, The Brain at Rest…
Description: When was the last time you stopped to rest and just let your mind wander? Well, if you need any encouragement to do that more, come hear neuroscientist Joseph Jebelli discussing the findings of his latest book, The Brain at Rest, with Maddison Connaughton. By deftly blending science with personal stories and practical tips, Jebelli unpacks how resting can have profound implications on just about everything – from creativity to life expectancy. Sign us up!

Title: Philip Marsden & Vanessa Taylor: How We Use the Natural World
Teaser: The natural world, and humanity's fraught relationship with it, slips into focus in this event…
Description: The natural world, and humanity's fraught relationship with it, slips into focus in this event. Philip Marsden's Under a Metal Sky investigates the history of humanity's extraction of minerals, from the Bronze Age and the Industrial Revolution to the present day. Meanwhile, environmental historian Vanessa Taylor's Seven Rivers delves into the histories, cultures, and ecosystems surrounding seven of the world's great rivers, asking what the future holds for them. Join their urgent discussion with Jo Sharp.

Title: Kit de Waal: When You’re Busy Making Other Plans
Teaser: Fw people understand the vagueries of the human heart such as My Name Is Leon author Kit de Waal, who returns to the Festival to discuss her latest novel, The Best of Everything…
Description: Few people understand the vagueries of the human heart such as My Name Is Leon author Kit de Waal, who returns to the Festival to discuss her latest novel, The Best of Everything. A book bursting with joy and tenderness about how love changes our lives, it follows meticulous organiser, Paulette, who finds her perfect life plans waylaid when she unexpectedly ends up caring for two children. In conversation with Damian Barr.

Title: Ambrose Parry: In the Old Town
Teaser: Join the bestselling writing duo Chris Brookmyre and Dr Marisa Haetzman (aka Ambrose Parry) as they unpack our city’s dark past with Peggy Hughes…
Description: It’s 1854, Edinburgh. Apprentice Sarah Fisher is secretly training as a medic under Dr Will Raven’s expertise; soon, though, she’ll discover the seedy underbelly to Victorian society. Historical Edinburgh is brought back to vivid life in The Death of Shame, Ambrose Parry’s latest Raven and Fisher mystery. Join the bestselling writing duo Chris Brookmyre and Dr Marisa Haetzman (aka Ambrose Parry) as they unpack our city’s dark past with Peggy Hughes.

Title: Brilliant Bugs with Simon Mole & Gecko
Teaser: Did you know there is a whole world right beneath our feet? Down in the ground below, there are worms and scorpions, beetles and caterpillars. Musician Gecko joins Simon Mole for this bug-tastic event as they celebrate the fantastic world of bugs…
Description: Join poet Simon Mole and musician Gecko for a family show full of poems, raps and songs all about your favourite brilliant bugs (and some you haven’t heard of yet!). A fun & interactive invitation to explore the secret world beneath our feet. Every tune is an earworm - even the ones about woodlice!

Title: Join the Merry Bear Band with David Litchfield
Teaser: Get ready to go on a musical adventure. Acclaimed author-illustrator David Litchfield and his Bear Band are on a 10th anniversary concert tour! We can bear-ly contain our excitement…
Description: Get ready to go on a musical adventure! Acclaimed author-illustrator David Litchfield and his Bear Band are on a 10th anniversary concert tour! David will share a special edition of his bestselling The Bear and the Piano accompanied by live music from his Merry Band of Bears. After this special storytime, stick around and create your own animal themed artwork. We can bear-ly contain our excitement!

Title: Chris Whitaker: Darkness Uncovered
Teaser: Chris Whitaker’s All the Colours of the Dark became a word-of-mouth sensation last year, and shows no signs of slowing down…
Description: Chris Whitaker’s All the Colours of the Dark became a word-of-mouth sensation last year, and shows no signs of slowing down. Folding a love story, a coming-of-age tale, and a fist-bitingly tense thriller into one, John Marrs has called this mesmerising novel ‘a truly exceptional masterclass in storytelling’. The international bestselling author chats with us about this story of love, death, truth, and the spaces in between. Chaired by Halla Mohieddeen.

Title: Kate Foster: Echoes of Edinburgh’s Past
Teaser: The remarkable, dramatic story of Maggie Dickson ('Half Hangit Maggie') has intrigued and horrified Grassmarket drinkers for decades. In The Mourning Necklace, Kate Foster breathes new life into her story…
Description: The remarkable, dramatic story of Maggie Dickson ('Half Hangit Maggie') has intrigued and horrified Grassmarket drinkers for decades. In The Mourning Necklace, Kate Foster breathes new life into the story of Maggie's forbidden affair, secret pregnancy, and botched execution, using her captivating writing to shed light on women of the past, as she did in Women's Prize-shortlisted novel The Maiden. Be whisked back to 1720s Edinburgh via Foster's superlative storytelling today. Chaired by Jenny Brown.

Title: Madeleine Thien & Priya Basil: Objects Talk Back
Teaser: The Humboldt Forum's 'Objects Talk Back' project invited authors to select an object from the museum's collection and write about it however they wished. Novelist Madeleine Thien chose the painting, 'Three Uyghur Princes'. She talks with project curator…
Description: The Humboldt Forum's 'Objects Talk Back' project invited authors to select an object from the museum's collection and write about it however they wished. Novelist Madeleine Thien chose the painting, 'Three Uyghur Princes'. She talks with project curator Priya Basil about her approach to this unusual brief, how encounters with objects can remake us, and how the project intersects with one of the thorniest parts of our Repair theme – reparations – by engaging with gaps, erasures, and (un)truths in colonial histories.

Title: Nussaibah Younis: Fundamentally Funny
Teaser: Shortlisted for 2025's Women's Prize for Fiction, Fundamentally combines Nussaibah Younis' career in academia and Middle East peacekeeping with her recent training in stand-up comedy. Younis talks with us today about navigating cultural divides and the…
Description: Shortlisted for 2025's Women's Prize for Fiction, Fundamentally combines Nussaibah Younis' career in academia and Middle East peacekeeping with her recent training in stand-up comedy. In this darkly funny debut, set in an Iraqi internment camp for ISIS brides, Younis explores the grey areas that exist when faced with questions of identity, faith, and family. Younis talks with Anahit Behrooz today about navigating cultural divides and the intricacies of interweaving whip-smart humour and international crises.

Title: Tash Aw & Alan Hollinghurst: Intimate Histories
Teaser: Two master novelists meet today for a spellbinding conversation…
Description: One of our finest contemporary authors, Alan Hollinghurst's Our Evenings spans half a century, following its protagonist from his school days to becoming an artist, as Britain transforms around him. Tash Aw's The South, the first in a sweeping four-book series, tells of the longing that blooms between two boys as they and their families navigate great change. Two master novelists meet today for a spellbinding conversation. Chaired by Andrés N Ordorica.

Title: Frances Wilson & Francesca Wade: Rediscovering Muriel Spark and Gertrude Stein
Teaser: In Electric Spark, Frances Wilson digs into Muriel Spark's young life, uncovering untold experiences and strange encounters that ultimately shaped Spark as a person and writer. Meanwhile, in Gertrude Stein: An Afterlife, Francesca Wade shares unseen…
Description: In Electric Spark, Frances Wilson digs into Muriel Spark's young life, uncovering untold experiences and strange encounters that ultimately shaped Spark as a person and writer. Meanwhile, in Gertrude Stein: An Afterlife, Francesca Wade shares unseen writing from Stein's personal archive, revealing her radical nature and why Stein wanted to be remembered for her work, not her personality. They join Lennie Goodings today, discussing how much of the mythology that surrounds these authors is actually true.

Title: Najwan Darwish: Poems for Palestine
Teaser: Hear Darwish - described as one of the foremost contemporary Arab poets - discuss what it means to survive, how to avoid bring desensitised by conflict, and the incredible tenacity of the human spirit…
Description: Najwan Darwish's lyrical and pulsating poetry has never been more relevant. His collection, No One Will Know You Tomorrow, draws from five volumes published in Arabic, here translated into English, alongside new work, to showcase the horror of living in a war-torn land, while shining a light on the beauty of the Palestinian landscape. Hear Darwish - described as one of the foremost contemporary Arab poets - discuss what it means to survive, how to avoid bring desensitised by conflict, and the incredible tenacity of the human spirit. Chaired by Marjorie Lotfi.

Title: Madeleine Thien & Deepa Bhasthi: The Sanctity of Language
Teaser: Words matter. But how far can language take us – or lead us away from – where we want to be?…
Description: Words matter. But how far can language take us – or lead us away from – where we want to be? ‘Words can erase and distort so many things,’ says Madeleine Thien (The Book of Records). ‘Justice, reason, democracy, freedom, goodness, truth—we have used these words in the service of widely different intentions.’ She’s joined today by writer and translator Deepa Bhasthi (Heart Lamp), who in 2025 became the first translator of colour to win the International Booker Prize. Chaired by Dina Nayeri.

Title: Sam Dalrymple: The Legacy of Partition
Teaser: Join filmmaker and historian Sam Dalrymple for an insightful conversation about the complex history and geopolitics of Asia…
Description: Filmmaker and historian of the global south Sam Dalrymple has responded to 1947’s partition of India and Pakistan by co-founding Project Dastaan, which uses VR technology to connect displaced families with the villages of their roots. His first book, Shattered Lands, goes even further, examining five key partitions which broke up the enormous Asian territory formerly known as the Indian Empire. Join him today for an insightful conversation about the complex history and geopolitics of Asia. Chaired by Anita Anand.

Title: Michael Hutchinson: Understanding Endurance
Teaser: Few know what it takes to navigate the intense mental and physical demands of professional cycling quite like Michael Hutchinson. A writer and former champion professional cyclist, his latest book, Further, is a deep dive into the world of extreme…
Description: Few know what it takes to navigate the intense mental and physical demands of professional cycling quite like Michael Hutchinson. A writer and former champion professional cyclist, his latest book, Further, is a deep dive into the world of extreme endurance. Today he joins Emily Chappell to discuss the insights he gained from talking to the world's top endurance experts, as well as his own terrifying experiences going further than ever before.

Title: Malcolm X at 100
Teaser: Malcolm X was born 100 years ago this year. Yet his legacy of resistance ‘by any means necessary’ continues to resonate globally. With special guests Bonnie Greer, Vayu Naidu, and Ekow Eshun. Chaired by Colin Grant…
Description: Malcolm X was born 100 years ago this year. Yet his legacy of resistance ‘by any means necessary’ continues to resonate globally. From the Civil Rights movement to post-colonial struggles, his words and life ignite and inspire change. This event, in partnership with WritersMosaic, delves into Malcolm X’s enduring role as a revolutionary and a symbol of defiance. With special guests Clementine Burnley, Vayu Naidu, and Ekow Eshun. Chaired by Colin Grant.

Title: Sunil Amrith: The Burning Earth
Teaser: In The Burning Earth, environmental historian at Yale University and MacArthur Genius fellow Sunil Amrith creates an ambitiously complete history of the way 500 years of human development has driven environmental change and destruction…
Description: In The Burning Earth, environmental historian at Yale University and MacArthur Genius fellow Sunil Amrith creates an ambitiously complete history of the way 500 years of human development has driven environmental change and destruction. From empires and their colonisation of the globe, coal mining to oil extraction, and the legacy of 20th century wars, he'll reveal today the full cost of the journey from there to here. In conversation with David Farrier.

Title: Judy Murray: See You in Court
Teaser: Judy Murray needs no introduction: former tennis professional and coach, and of course mother of Those Tennis Brothers, she’s an icon of the game. Latterly, she’s become a figurehead for women in sport and has also subjected herself to the rigours of…
Description: Judy Murray needs no introduction: former tennis professional and coach, and of course mother of Those Tennis Brothers, she’s an icon of the game. Latterly, she’s become a figurehead for women in sport and has also subjected herself to the rigours of Strictly. She now returns to the Festival with her second novel, tennis club whodunit Game, Set & Murder. Chaired by Jenny Colgan.

Title: Romantically Yours with Elle McNicoll & Harry Trevaldwyn
Teaser: Romance is in the air in this YA rom-com event that will explore how to boldly be yourself, no matter who’s watching. In Elle McNicoll’s Wish You Were Her, autistic actress Allegera wants to enjoy a normal teenage summer at a book festival but…
Description: Romance is in the air in this YA rom-com event that will explore how to boldly be yourself, no matter who’s watching. In Elle McNicoll’s Wish You Were Her, autistic actress Allegera wants to enjoy a normal teenage summer at a book festival but misunderstandings arise and (romantic) drama unfolds, whilst in Harry Trevaldwyn’s The Romantic Tragedies of a Drama King, Patch’s mission is to find himself his first boyfriend. Hear both authors in conversation with Juno Dawson.

Title: Shaun Walker: The Spies Next Door
Teaser: Guardian central and eastern Europe correspondent Shaun Walker joins us in conversation with Charlotte Higgins, discussing his secret history, The Illegals, where he puts a decade reporting from Moscow to good use, revealing, with the pace and intrigue…
Description: Thought the deep cover Russian spies masquerading as an all-American family in the TV series The Americans were fiction? Not according to Guardian central and eastern Europe correspondent Shaun Walker, who joins us in conversation with Charlotte Higgins. In his secret history, The Illegals, Walker puts a decade reporting from Moscow to good use, revealing, with the pace and intrigue of a spy thriller, Russia’s century-long placing of international agents in extreme, long-term deep cover.

Title: Jenny Colgan: Coming Back Home
Teaser: Home may be where the heart is - but what happens when that home is invaded by your unemployed (and very grumpy) 30-year-old kid? Jenny Colgan's Meet Me at the Seaside Cottages explores the ever-evolving relationship between a mother and her adult…
Description: Home may be where the heart is - but what happens when that home is invaded by your unemployed (and very grumpy) 30-year-old kid? Jenny Colgan's Meet Me at the Seaside Cottages explores the ever-evolving relationship between a mother and her adult daughter as they're forced to live together after years apart. Reflecting on love, acceptance, and new beginnings, get swept up in this conversation with the bestselling author today. Chaired by Kylie Reid.

Title: Steve Crawshaw & Philippe Sands: Prosecuting the Powerful
Teaser: Is justice possible when war crimes have been committed? Should retribution, reconciliation, or something else be the goal? Two leading authors discuss this tense subject from their own experience…
Description: Is justice possible when war crimes have been committed? Should retribution, reconciliation, or something else be the goal? Two leading authors discuss this tense subject from their own experience. Writer and international lawyer Philippe Sands KC represented Palestine at the International Court of Justice in recent key rulings, while as a former journalist and UK director of Human Rights Watch, Steve Crawshaw reports in Prosecuting the Powerful on the history of putting national leaders on trial.

Title: Reeta Chakrabarti: Finding Belle
Teaser: Reeta Chakrabarti will be familiar to anyone who has watched BBC news, but now she has made the leap from journalist and chief newsreader to novelist…
Description: Reeta Chakrabarti will be familiar to anyone who has watched BBC news, but now she has made the leap from journalist and chief newsreader to novelist. Her sensitive, insightful debut, Finding Belle, takes us from the beaches of Mombasa to the suburbs of England. Mother-daughter relationships and weighty family secrets haunt its pages. Today, Chakrabarti joins Alisha Fernandez Miranda for a discussion of connection and forging new identities.

Title: Anshel Pfeffer, Ece Temelkuran & Shaun Walker: No Kings Here
Teaser: How do we survive the era of the authoritarian strongman leader? Why do these men hold a monopoly on political power? And what are the alternatives to their rule?…
Description: How do we survive the era of the authoritarian strongman leader? Why do these men hold a monopoly on political power? And what are the alternatives to their rule? Journalists Anshel Pfeffer (Haaretz, Economist), Ece Temelkuran (Der Spiegel, Guardian), and Shaun Walker (Guardian) have written extensively about Benjamin Netanyahu, Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, and Vladimir Putin, respectively, and they arrive equipped to illuminate what lasting impact all three will have on Europe and the world. Chaired by Halla Mohieddeen.

Title: Tracy Borman: The Royal Lie That Started a War
Teaser: Succession meets the 17th century English monarchy in historian and novelist Tracy Borman’s revealing new book The Stolen Crown, which puts forward that Queen Elizabeth I didn’t, in fact, name King James VI of Scotland as her deathbed successor…
Description: Succession meets the 17th century English monarchy in historian and novelist Tracy Borman’s revealing new book The Stolen Crown, which puts forward that Queen Elizabeth I didn’t, in fact, name King James VI of Scotland as her deathbed successor – a lie which led to England’s descent into civil war within half a century under the Stuart’s rule. In this launch event, enjoy an hour of historical intrigue, deception, and chaos with the author of Anne Boleyn & Elizabeth I.

Title: Katie Kitamura, Yiyun Li & Mahmoud Muna: The Case for Books
Teaser: The freedom to write and sell books is fundamental to a democracy, so in these censorious times how best can we disagree without silencing?…
Description: The freedom to write and sell books is fundamental to a democracy, so in these censorious times how best can we disagree without silencing? Here to talk it out robustly are Audition author Katie Kitamura, who's spoken out against Trump's attacks on language; novelist Yiyun Li, who's written about self-censorship in China and online; and bookseller Mahmoud Muna, whose Educational Bookshop in Jerusalem was recently raided by the Israeli Army, accused of 'disrupting order' by selling books and educational material.

Title: Scribbles and Smells with Jim Smith
Teaser: Draw along with global bestselling author and comics creator Jim Smith celebrating his full-colour graphic novel series, My Big Fat Smelly Poo Diary. Join Jim as he introduces the hilarious and lovable characters, best friends Pedro, Olga, and Ozzy (AKA…
Description: Draw along with global bestselling author and comics creator Jim Smith celebrating his full-colour graphic novel series, My Big Fat Smelly Poo Diary. Join Jim as he introduces the hilarious and lovable characters, best friends Pedro, Olga, and Ozzy (AKA the Poopies) and follow them on a series of madcap, episodic adventures. This highly interactive event will feature readings, draw-along, tips and tricks on crafting comics. Pencils at the ready, laughter guaranteed!

Title: Monica Feria-Tinta: Litigating for Mother Nature
Teaser: If corporations can have legal rights, why shouldn't nature? Meet the pioneering British-Peruvian lawyer at the forefront of the climate justice movement: Monica Feria-Tinta…
Description: If corporations can have legal rights, why shouldn't nature? Meet the pioneering British-Peruvian lawyer at the forefront of the climate justice movement: Monica Feria-Tinta. In A Barrister for the Earth, she unravels her most inspiring successes helping ordinary people hold the biggest perpetrators of environmental damage to account. She talks with us today about the groundbreaking potential of these new legal frameworks to help repair the relationship between people and the planet. Chaired by Paul Behrens.

Title: Tony Juniper & Friederike Otto: Fighting Climate Injustice
Teaser: The climate crisis isn't just about the environment; it's about the way global inequality means the world's most vulnerable people are being hit first and hardest. So argues physicist and climate researcher Friederike Otto, whose Climate Injustice looks…
Description: The climate crisis isn't just about the environment; it's about the way global inequality means the world's most vulnerable people are being hit first and hardest. So argues physicist and climate researcher Friederike Otto, whose Climate Injustice looks at global case studies, from floods in Pakistan to Australian wildfires, and environmentalist Tony Juniper, whose book, Just Earth, posits necessary system changes. Today they talk with Alice Mah about how fighting inequality is fighting climate change.

Title: Dan Gunn & Frances Wilson: The Legacy of Muriel Spark
Teaser: With access to over 3,000 letters penned by Muriel Spark, distinguished professor Dan Gunn has spent five years decoding the enigmatic author while compiling The Letters of Muriel Spark. Meanwhile, journalist Frances Wilson's fascination with Spark led…
Description: With access to over 3,000 letters penned by Muriel Spark, distinguished professor Dan Gunn has spent five years decoding the enigmatic author while compiling The Letters of Muriel Spark. Meanwhile, journalist Frances Wilson's fascination with Spark led her to delve into the formative years of Edinburgh's daughter to write Electric Spark. Join them today as they discuss Spark's legacy and how they reframed her personal letters and archive for a public audience. Chaired by Calum Barnes.

Title: Loud Poets Grand Slam Final 2025
Teaser: Returning for a third year, the highly anticipated Loud Poets Grand Slam Final promises to be a Festival highlight, combining music with fist-thumping, side-tickling poetry. Having qualified through a series of nationwide Slams, 12 poets compete for a £3……
Description: Returning for a third year, the highly anticipated Loud Poets Grand Slam Final promises to be a Festival highlight, combining music with fist-thumping, side-tickling poetry. Having qualified through a series of nationwide Slams, 12 poets compete for a £3,000 prize and the coveted title of Slam Champion. Hosted by Kevin Mclean with musical accompaniment from Jack Hinks, plus a special performance from last year's winner, and this year's sacrificial poet, EmmaClaire Brightlyn.

Title: Peter F Hamilton: Space Opera Goes Digital
Teaser: Today, Hamilton talks about the thrill of imagining a wildly far-flung future and his dual roles as novelist and video game consultant…
Description: AD 43,000, the Centauri Cluster: the abandoned Earth is a mere footnote in humanity’s ancient, intergalactic history. This is the setting of space opera titan Peter F Hamilton’s latest novel, Exodus: The Archimedes Engine, as well as that of a bold new action-adventure video game from Archetype Entertainment. Today, Hamilton talks about the thrill of imagining a wildly far-flung future and his dual roles as novelist and video game consultant. Chaired by Eris Young.

Title: Clare Hunter & Callum Robinson: With Our Hands
Teaser: From wood to thread, Callum Robinson and Clare Hunter both explore the powerful stories held within crafted objects…
Description: From wood to thread, Callum Robinson and Clare Hunter both explore the powerful stories held within crafted objects. Robinson is a woodworker whose book Ingrained blends memoir and nature writing. Hunter's Making Matters celebrates the potential of creative making, exploring craft traditions from across the centuries. Today, they discuss the cultural and personal significance of craft, and how it can enable us to see the world in new, inspiring ways. Chaired by Craft Scotland's Stacey Hunter.

Title: Jenny Lau, Chitra Ramaswamy & Sami Tamimi: Food and Home
Teaser: Food profoundly shapes our sense of home and belonging, no matter which country or cuisine we identify most closely with. Jenny Lau, Sami Tamimi, and Chitra Ramaswamy come together to discuss the kaleidoscope of stories and connections that come alive…
Description: Food profoundly shapes our sense of home and belonging, no matter which country or cuisine we identify most closely with. Jenny Lau (An A-Z of Chinese Food (Recipes Not Included)), Sami Tamimi (Boustany), and Times food critic Chitra Ramaswamy come together to discuss the kaleidoscope of stories and connections that come alive through the simple acts of cooking, eating, and sharing recipes. A nourishing conversation, chaired by Candice Chung, awaits!

Title: Alan Taylor: Edinburgh in its Own Words
Teaser: Edinburgh and the literary tradition go together hand-in-glove, and with Edinburgh: The Autobiography, writer and editor Alan Taylor draws together the story of our 900-year-old capital as told by those who have written about it - writers including…
Description: Edinburgh and the literary tradition go together hand-in-glove, and with Edinburgh: The Autobiography, writer and editor Alan Taylor draws together the story of our 900-year-old capital as told by those who have written about it - writers including Walter Scott, Ian Rankin, Robert Louis Stevenson, Charles Dickens, and Muriel Spark (who called it 'the city of Calvinism, high teas, and loveless alliances'). Hear Taylor talking about this compelling urban portrait today. Chaired by Mike Wade.

Title: Sophie Elmhirst: For Better or Worse
Teaser: What is a marriage, if not being stuck on a raft with another, trying to survive? That's the question, both literally and figuratively, at the heart of Sophie Elmhirst's remarkable Maurice and Maralyn…
Description: What is a marriage, if not being stuck on a raft with another, trying to survive? That's the question, both literally and figuratively, at the heart of Sophie Elmhirst's remarkable Maurice and Maralyn. The astonishing true story of a couple shipwrecked by a whale in the remote Pacific, it's both gripping, elegiac, and told as evocatively as any novel. Sam Baker joins its Orwell Prize-shortlisted author to uncover the deeper questions underpinning this tender portrait.

Title: Ulrike Herrmann, Emma Holten & Cahal Moran: The True Cost of Capitalism
Teaser: Dig into this thorny topic with journalist, broadcaster, and former banker, Ulrike Herrman, activist and gender policy consultant Emma Holten and economist and host of the Unlearning Economics YouTube channel, Cahal Moran…
Description: What does an economic system stacked against most of its users and the planet itself reveal about what we most value? Dig into this thorny topic with journalist, broadcaster, and former banker, Ulrike Herrmann (The End of Capitalism); activist and gender policy consultant Emma Holten (Deficit); and economist and host of the Unlearning Economics YouTube channel, Cahal Moran (Why We're Getting Poorer). They come together for an eye-opening conversation that will educate, enrage, and - most importantly - inspire. Chaired by Kezia Dugdale.

Title: Henry McLeish & James Mitchell: Scottish Devolution – How’s It Going?
Teaser: Henry McLeish (former Scottish first minister and leader of the Labour Party in Scotland) and James Mitchell (director of the Academy of Government at the University of Edinburgh): two authors with heavyweight viewpoints on Scottish politics and…
Description: Henry McLeish (former Scottish first minister and leader of the Labour Party in Scotland) and James Mitchell (director of the Academy of Government at the University of Edinburgh): two authors with heavyweight viewpoints on Scottish politics and devolution. Their new book, Unfinished Business, looks back on the achievements, challenges, and possibilities presented by the creation of the modern Scottish Parliament in 1998. An essential event for anyone intrigued by Scottish politics' workings. Chaired by Brian Taylor.

Title: Tariq Ali: Fighting the Empire
Teaser: At 81 years old, political activist, journalist, and filmmaker Tariq Ali has witnessed countless global conflicts and world-defining movements. Through a series of eyewitness accounts and reflections, Ali's memoir, You Can't Please All, recounts modern…
Description: At 81 years old, political activist, journalist, and filmmaker Tariq Ali has witnessed countless global conflicts and world-defining movements. Through a series of eyewitness accounts and reflections, Ali's memoir, You Can't Please All, recounts modern historical periods from the fall of the Soviet Union to the war on terror in the USA, while at the same time providing a poignant family history of his parents' early years in Pakistan. It's an honour to welcome him today, in conversation with Henry Bell.

Title: Jonathan Freedland: Defying a Dictator
Teaser: Author, journalist, and host of both BBC Radio 4’s The Long View series and the Guardian’s Politics Weekly America podcast, Jonathan Freedland has won both the Orwell Prize for Journalism and the Somerset Maugham Award for Non-Fiction…
Description: Author, journalist, and host of both BBC Radio 4’s The Long View series and the Guardian’s Politics Weekly America podcast, Jonathan Freedland has won both the Orwell Prize for Journalism and the Somerset Maugham Award for Non-Fiction. An insightful and authoritative voice on modern history, today he speaks to Kenny Farquharson about his varied career, and the current resonance of his book The Traitors Circle, a true story of rebellion against the Nazis.

Title: Conjure Up Magical Stories with Abi Elphinstone
Teaser: Join bestselling author Abi Elphinstone with her new book, Ember Spark and the Unicorn’s Secret, as she reveals where she finds her ideas – from shower gel bottles and street signposts to adventures in Mongolia – as well as tips for how to dream up your…
Description: Rusty Fizzbang, vet to magical beasts, needs an apprentice. Ember Spark, looking for adventure, is his newest recruit. But keeping magical beasts a secret isn’t an easy task! Join bestselling author Abi Elphinstone with her new book, Ember Spark and the Unicorn’s Secret, as she reveals where she finds her ideas – from shower gel bottles and street signposts to adventures in Mongolia – as well as tips for how to dream up your own stories.

Title: Marianne Brown & Joni Buchanan: No Woman is an Island
Teaser: Dive into history, the environment, and the Scottish Isles in this conversation with environmental journalist Marianne Brown and Gaelic Literature Awards­-shortlisted Joni Buchanan…
Description: Dive into history, the environment, and the Scottish Isles in this conversation with environmental journalist Marianne Brown and Gaelic Literature Awards­-shortlisted Joni Buchanan. In The Shetland Way, Brown arrives on Shetland for her father's funeral then can't leave due to lockdown; there, a new windfarm's development causes tension as islanders fear for their fragile local environment. Meanwhile, in Women of the Hebrides, Buchanan tells of women's historic contribution to these islands in English and Gaelic. Chaired by Jen Stout.

Title: Kevin Guyan & Keio Yoshida: Queer Rights and Realities
Teaser: Writer-researcher Kevin Guyan and human rights lawyer Keio Yoshida both grapple with the complex realities – the challenges and triumphs – of queer existence in contemporary society…
Description: Writer-researcher Kevin Guyan and human rights lawyer Keio Yoshida both grapple with the complex realities – the challenges and triumphs – of queer existence in contemporary society. Guyan’s Rainbow Trap delves into the societal pressures and expectations that can constrain queer identities, while Yoshida’s Pride and Prejudices examines the flawed legal frameworks shaping LGBTQ+ experiences. Join them for a vital conversation with Caro Clarke about justice, visibility, and the ongoing fight for equality.

Title: Bolu Babalola & Beth O'Leary: Meet Not-So-Cutes
Teaser: Bolu Babalola and Beth O'Leary chat to Nyla Ahmad about the awkwardness of love…
Description: In Bolu Babalola's fiery new novel, Sweet Heat, ex-partners Kiki and Malakai are reunited at a friend's wedding, whether they like it or not. Meanwhile, bestselling author of The Flat Share, Beth O'Leary brings us a new punchy new romantic comedy with Swept Away, which sees Lexi and Zeke having a cringey one night stand, then ending up all at sea (literally) on a house boat. Babalola and O'Leary chat to Nyla Ahmad about the awkwardness of love.

Title: Ben Okri: Festival for the Broken-Hearted
Teaser: Winner of the Booker Prize, Ben Okri doubles the festival spirit on offer with Madame Sosostris & the Festival for the Broken-Hearted…
Description: Winner of the Booker Prize, Ben Okri doubles the festival spirit on offer with Madame Sosostris & the Festival for the Broken-Hearted. Inspired by A Midsummer Night’s Dream and 'The Wasteland', it’s written with Okri’s unique and hypnotic blend of realism and magical realism, with language that conjures myth and slides into poetry. Today, he discusses bewitching fables, human connections, and the transformative power of festivals. Chaired by Esa Aldegheri.

Title: Miriam Toews & Marjorie Lotfi: Can Words Repair?
Teaser: Today, Miriam Toews and Marjorie Lotfi discuss the potential of language – as a salve, an answer, and a way to help us through…
Description: A Truce That Is Not Peace is the first time Miriam Toews has published a non-fiction work about her own life. The work remakes her world through literary form and proposes the question: how far can words reach? Today, Toews is joined by Marjorie Lotfi, author of The Wrong Person to Ask, to discuss the potential of language – as a salve, an answer, and a way to help us through. Chaired by Amina Shah.

Title: Anna Groundwater: Finding Scotland’s Place in World History
Teaser: Though small in landmass, Scotland and her people have had a mighty impact on the world over many centuries. In Connecting Scotland's History, Anna Groundwater demonstrates the richness, depth, and diversity of Scotland's story…
Description: Though small in landmass, Scotland and her people have had a mighty impact on the world over many centuries. In Connecting Scotland's History, Anna Groundwater (National Museum of Scotland's principal curator of Renaissance and Early Modern History) demonstrates the richness, depth, and diversity of Scotland's story. Hear her talking about the immersive timeline which charts 2,000 years of Scots history alongside its British and world equivalents. Chaired by Mairi Kidd.

Title: Michael Pedersen: Charged by Starlight
Teaser: Edinburgh’s Makar, Michael Pedersen, is an effervescent poet, poignant memoirist, anarchic event host… and now a debut novelist. He joins Russell Tovey to discuss the offbeat Muckle Flugg…
Description: Edinburgh’s Makar, Michael Pedersen, is an effervescent poet, poignant memoirist, anarchic event host… and now a debut novelist. He joins Russell Tovey to discuss the offbeat Muckle Flugga, which recounts the unsettling arrival of a stranger on a windswept island, setting asunder the lives of its lighthouse keeper and his dreamer son, Ouse. In the ensuing tug of war for Ouse’s affections, Pedersen asks what might happen when dreams are dragged to earth? The evening is completed by a special guest performance by Reuben Kaye.

Title: Josephine Quinn: The World that Made the West
Teaser: Historian and archaeologist Josephine Quinn is an expert in ancient history, from Greece and Rome to Phoenicia. Today, she shares lessons from her new book, How the World Made the West…
Description: Historian and archaeologist Josephine Quinn is an expert in ancient history, from Greece and Rome to Phoenicia. Today, she shares lessons from her new book, How the World Made the West, showing how the West’s history was not one of isolation, but characterised by exchange, mingling, and encounters with other cultures. Join Quinn for a fascinating discussion with Jamie Jauncey which puts a whole new understanding of Western civilisation in the frame.

Title: Pocket Shakespeare with Chris Riddell & Michael Rosen
Teaser: A Beginner’s Guide to the Best Bits of the Bard, and explore love, heartbreak, magic, superstition, and more (with the help of some special guests). Expect jokes, classic insults, and drawings of epic proportions!…
Description: Two powerhouses of children’s literature captivate in this magical event that brings William Shakespeare’s work to life. Poet Michael Rosen and illustrator Chris Riddell, both former Children’s Laureates, share Pocket Shakespeare: A Beginner’s Guide to the Best Bits of the Bard, and explore love, heartbreak, magic, superstition, and more. Expect jokes, classic insults, drawings of epic proportions, and some unforgettable readings from special guests Athena Kugblenu and Catherine Wilson.

Title: How Does Your Garden Grow? With Frances Tophill
Teaser: Hear Frances Tophill, author of How to Grow a Garden, sharing all about the wonderful plants and creatures that call your back garden their home and discover all different types of gardens: from vegetable ones to tropical glass houses…
Description: Calling all those green of thumb! This is a special conversation all about gardens, being kind to nature, and discovering what we can do to help plants grow. Hear Frances Tophill, author of How to Grow a Garden, sharing all about the wonderful plants and creatures that call your back garden their home and discover all different types of gardens: from vegetable ones to tropical glass houses. Chaired by Sophy Henn.

Title: From Aotearoa to Alba: A Literary Exchange
Teaser: Scotland and New Zealand are separated by 11,113.48 miles. Yet in a cultural and literary sense, the distance isn't quite so great. Join us for a vibrant celebration of the poetic connections between the two nations, based on a shared love of performance…
Description: As the aeroplane flies, Scotland and New Zealand are separated by 11,113.48 miles. Yet in a cultural and literary sense, the distance isn't quite so great. Join us for a vibrant celebration of the poetic connections between the two nations, based on a shared love of performance and music. Featuring special guests including Dominic Hoey, Gen Fricker, Jackie Kay, Becky Manawatu, Hollie McNish, and Michael Pedersen - a rich exchange of culture and creativity awaits. Plus, we'll be joined by the amazing Gemma Cairney for a DJ set to see out the evening.

Title: The People Speak
Teaser: Join a host of acclaimed writers and actors, including the one and only Viggo Mortensen (The Lord of the Rings, Captain Fantastic) and the iconic Vanessa Redgrave (The Devils, Atonement, Mrs Dalloway), for powerful performances of stories, speeches, and…
Description: Join a host of acclaimed writers and actors - including the one and only Viggo Mortensen (The Lord of the Rings, Captain Fantastic), Stephen Rea (The Crying Game, Interview with the Vampire), author Ahmed Masoud, singer-songwriter Miwa Nagato-Apthorp, writer Irenosen Okojie, and writer, curator, and journalist Ekow Eshun - for powerful performances of stories, speeches, and songs of protest and rebellion from around the world, and across history. Inspired by the work of people’s historian Howard Zinn and directed by Anthony Arnove (co-editor with Colin Firth of The People Speak), their words shimmer with strength, inspiration, and a vision for a better future. Hosted by Anthony Arnove.

Title: Sarah Hall & Elizabeth O'Connor: Fantastic Folklore
Teaser: Master storyteller Sarah Hall’s Helm follows a mischievous wind through the stories of the humans who experienced it. Meanwhile, Elizabeth O’Connor’s devastating debut Whale Fall tells of a woman longing for escape from island life and discovering a way…
Description: Master storyteller Sarah Hall’s Helm follows a mischievous wind through the stories of the humans who experienced it. Meanwhile, Elizabeth O’Connor’s devastating debut Whale Fall tells of a woman longing for escape from island life and discovering a way out. Join them as they discuss the folklore at the core of these compelling novels and the importance of passing stories down the generations. Chaired by Di Speirs.

Title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
Teaser: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers…
Description: Join us for a relaxed morning story especially for your littlest readers with our guest, Rachel Plummer.

Title: Candice Chung & Katie Goh: Food is Life
Teaser: In Candice Chung and Katie Goh’s memoirs, food is a love language, a commodity, and a way of saying the unsayable…
Description: In Candice Chung and Katie Goh’s memoirs, food is a love language, a commodity, and a way of saying the unsayable. Chung’s Chinese Parents Don’t Say I Love You unpicks family dynamics and the rituals of dining together, while Goh’s Foreign Fruit uses the complex history of the orange as a framework for her personal story. They chat with us about how food informs our understanding of the world, and our place in it. Chaired by Xuanlin Tham.

Title: The Work of Translation: A Workshop with Daniel Hahn
Teaser: Award-winning literary translator, editor, and critic Daniel Hahn returns to the Festival with his popular translation workshop, taking you through the process of translating a piece of fiction and the painstaking, exhilarating work it takes to find the……
Description:
Award-winning literary translator, editor, and critic Daniel Hahn returns to the Festival with his popular translation workshop, taking you through the process of translating a piece of fiction and the painstaking, exhilarating work it takes to find the right words. This two-hour session is for enthusiastic novices who want to improve their practice – and anyone who is fascinated by the nuances of language.

	Daniel Hahn is no longer able to appear and this event will go ahead with Iona Macintyre and Fiona Mackintosh, both Senior Lecturers in Spanish, Portuguese and Latin American Studies at the University of Edinburgh.

Title: Thinking Differently with Greg Stobbs
Teaser: Think quickly and imagine wildly in author-illustrator Gregg Stobb’s event about celebrating differences and embracing what makes you unique!…
Description: Think quickly and imagine wildly in author-illustrator Greg Stobbs' event about celebrating differences and embracing what makes you unique! Based on Gregg’s imaginative book Cloud Boy, which is inspired by his own experience with ADHD, join Greg for an interactive and accessible event including a drawing activity to create a brand new imaginative creature.

Title: Edinburgh Gin Presents: Ready Steady Cocktail!
Description: Are we cocktail connoisseurs or botanical buffoons? Gin geniuses or glorified juice jugglers? Edinburgh Gin presents Ready, Steady, Cocktail! – the live cocktail challenge where professionals face off against brave amateurs. But there’s a twist: ingredients are picked from the Tombola of Taste – think seaweed, chili or lavender fudge. Can our experts make it magic or will the underdogs steal the show? With a welcome drink, two outrageous creations mixed live on stage and your vote deciding the winner, anything can happen. Raise your glass and cast your vote!
Venue description: The Edinburgh Gin Distillery is a destination unlike any other. It’s here that we welcome guests from all over the world to discover what makes our selection of beautifully crafted, vibrant and naturally flavoured gins so unique. Fire up all senses with a gin tasting , cocktail experience or try your hand at crafting your very own bespoke Gin with our finest botanicals.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Building Lift has weight capacity of 1000kg

Title: Linder +  Adele Patrick: Gimme Danger
Teaser: Linder is one of Britain’s great pop-culture provocateurs, a post-punk musician, and widely exhibited photomontage artist (infamously on the sleeve of the Buzzcocks’ ‘Orgasm Addict’ single). Here, Linder collides in discussion with the great, Booker Prize-shortlisted feminist writer Marina Warner, chaired by EAF Director Kim McAleese, on subjects including feminism, fashion, fairytales, and her artistic […]
Description:
Linder is one of Britain’s great pop-culture provocateurs, a post-punk musician, and widely exhibited photomontage artist (infamously on the sleeve of the Buzzcocks’ ‘Orgasm Addict’ single). 

Here, Linder collides in discussion with the great, Booker Prize-shortlisted feminist writer Marina Warner, chaired by EAF Director Kim McAleese, on subjects including feminism, fashion, fairytales, and her artistic obsession with the human body.

! Due to illness, Marina Warner will no longer be part of this event, and Adele Patrick, founder and director of Glasgow Women’s Library, will be in her place.

Title: who will be remembered here: In-Conversation
Teaser: 2025 marks 30 years since the first major Pride event in Scotland, yet queer histories have existed for as long as Scotland has. who will be remembered here enlivens these histories through performances, films, and a book. Project curators Lewis Hetherington and CJ Mahony join contributors Mae Diansangu and Harry Josephine Giles for a discussion […]
Description:
2025 marks 30 years since the first major Pride event in Scotland, yet queer histories have existed for as long as Scotland has. who will be remembered here enlivens these histories through performances, films, and a book. 

Project curators Lewis Hetherington and CJ Mahony join contributors Mae Diansangu and Harry Josephine Giles for a discussion of how we reconsider the stories of the past and what it means to ‘remember into the future’.

Title: Digital Siblings
Description: In this exhibition students of Farmingdale State College (SUNY) and Edinburgh Napier University showcase their explorations into mixed reality and visitor attractions. Digital siblings are a range of interactive applications and products that create remote experiences with real spaces. For this edition, the student interns have been exploring Jupiter Artland and considering what it would mean to digitally bring Fringe visitors closer to the sculpture park. Expect to see novel prototypes and uses of interactive technology for bringing people and places together. Join us for this one-night-only exhibition at our Merchiston Campus.
Artist: Farmingdale State College and Edinburgh Napier University
Venue description: Venue 373.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, Reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking

Title: Andrii Kymach: Ukraine
Description: Ukraine’s BBC Cardiff Singer of the World Winner 2019 (opera), Andrii Kymach baritone returns to Edinburgh with rising star accompanist Jâms Coleman (piano) in a new recital, Ukraine, specially devised for 2025's Day of Ukraine Independence (24th August 2025). This follows his hugely successful 2024 recital Arias, which celebrated Edinburgh and Kyiv's 35th twinning anniversary (1989-2024). The historic 2025 event is supported by the Consulate of Ukraine and the Consulate Generals of Germany and France in Edinburgh.
Venue description: A beautiful, easily accessible 18th century New Town church, which hosts a variety of musical performances – from soloists to choirs, instrumentalists to small orchestras and bands in all musical genres: classical, folk, jazz, songs from the shows, opera, world music. Enjoy light lunches and snacks in the Undercroft cafe, or see the exquisite Georgian interior of the Church.

Title: Bach and Brahms
Description: Join this talented London-based cello/piano duo as they perform a series of three consecutive concerts of sonatas by these musical giants in the Georgian splendour of Edinburgh New Town Church. Not to be missed.
